title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
嘉靖庚子江西鄉試廵御史
謝九儀被
簡按其地寔惟監臨肆申徃執走
檄于諸藩藩遴儒臣典試事乃
諸藩遴如檄也故吉以次十
二人與焉盖介以經弗介以
===
人遴
明命杜私覬也比期胥至而簾外
諸執事亦恪選稱矣乃八月
丙寅率入院遂齋而拜于階
曰求賢惟人臣事
君義惟公明慎乃役之貞弗率者
殃及之廼進提學副使蘇祐
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序

嘉靖庚子，江西鄉試，廵御史謝九儀被簡按其地，寔惟監臨。肆申徃執，走檄于諸藩，藩遴儒臣典試事，乃諸藩遴如檄也。故吉以次十二人與焉。盖介以經，弗介以人，遴明命，杜私覬也。比期胥至，而簾外諸執事亦恪選稱矣。乃八月丙寅，率入院，遂齋而拜于階，曰：「求賢，惟人臣事君義；惟公明慎，乃役之貞。弗率者，殃及之。」廼進提學副使蘇祐
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the gengzi year of the Jiajing reign [1540], at the Jiangxi Provincial Examination, the Regional Inspector, Censor Xie Jiuyi, had been selected to inspect the region and accordingly served as Supervising Official. He reaffirmed the former procedures [?] and dispatched official communications to the provincial administrations, directing them to select Confucian officials to conduct the examination. The provincial administrations made their selections as instructed. Thus Ji, together with the others in sequence, twelve men in all, took part. Recommendations were based on expertise in the Classics, rather than personal connections; the selection made the commands clear [?] and forestalled private ambitions. By the appointed time, all had arrived, and the officials serving outside the examination curtain had likewise been carefully selected and were suitable for their duties.

On the bingyin day of the eighth month, they entered the examination compound together. They then purified themselves and bowed at the steps, declaring: “Seeking worthy men is the duty of a minister in serving his sovereign. Impartiality, discernment, and care are the proper foundations of this service. May calamity befall anyone who fails to observe them.” They then admitted those whom Su You, Vice Commissioner serving as Education Intendant, …

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
所選士凡三千有奇三試之
錄中式者九十有五人以
獻錄成吉以例得言夫色以五
錯章而繪弗離于素也味以
五錯美而瀝弗離于玄也故
大羹不和大圭不琢質存而
本眞也昔文質遞禪乃孔子
===
雖郁郁是從而彬彬君子未
嘗不想望焉故其言曰辭達
而已矣辭也者指所之也弗
宣則道無由顯弗約則言亦
以不袞是故吉躁以多寡辨
斐文以狂簡名穆哉淵乎聖
人意也唐宋征士以詞賦概
punctuated: 所選士凡三千有奇，三試之，錄中式者九十有五人以獻。錄成，吉以例得言：夫色以五錯章，而繪弗離于素也；味以五錯美，而瀝弗離于玄也。故大羹不和，大圭不琢，質存而本眞也。昔文質遞禪，乃孔子雖郁郁是從，而彬彬君子未嘗不想望焉。故其言曰：「辭達而已矣。」辭也者，指所之也。弗宣，則道無由顯；弗約，則言亦以不袞。是故吉躁以多寡辨，斐文以狂簡名。穆哉！淵乎！聖人意也。唐宋征士以詞賦概
translation_en:
…The candidates selected by him numbered more than three thousand. They were examined in three sessions, and ninety-five successful candidates were entered on the list for presentation. When the record was completed, I, Ji, was entitled by precedent to offer these remarks:

The five colors, intermingled, produce brilliant patterns, yet painting never dispenses with its plain ground. The five flavors, intermingled, produce delicious tastes, yet the liquid never dispenses with plain water [?]. Thus the great sacrificial broth is unseasoned, and the great jade tablet is uncarved: their substance is preserved and their foundation remains true. In former times, refinement and substance prevailed in succession. Although Confucius followed the splendid refinement [of Zhou], he never ceased to aspire to the gentleman in whom refinement and substance are harmoniously balanced. Thus he said: “Words need only convey their meaning.” Words point toward what one intends. Without adequate expression, the Way cannot become manifest; without concision, words likewise fail to achieve completeness [?]. Thus “auspiciousness and impetuosity” are distinguished by quantity [?], while accomplished literary expression is described as “bold in aspiration but unrestrained.” How solemn! How profound is the sage’s meaning!

Under the Tang and Song, men were recruited for office using verse and rhapsodies as a general standard…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
葉蘩本根蹷矣我
皇祖受
命始用釐革乃文教丕闡賔興如
成周矣故當時之文渾渾噩噩
噩一百數十年來中或少異然
體雖襜弗縟節雖明弗急製
雖嚴弗峭聲雖振弗厲是亦
足以程矣邇則擷藻摛奇稍
涉鉤棘之習我
===
皇上神聖中興
憲天作人敦正文體重頒
大號而薄海承
休率迺
皇極矣今觀江右之文沉深者性
punctuated: 葉蘩，本根蹷矣。我皇祖受命，始用釐革，乃文教丕闡，賔興如成周矣。故當時之文渾渾噩噩噩，一百數十年來，中或少異，然體雖襜弗縟，節雖明弗急，製雖嚴弗峭，聲雖振弗厲，是亦足以程矣。邇則擷藻摛奇，稍涉鉤棘之習。我皇上神聖中興，憲天作人，敦正文體，重頒大號，而薄海承休，率迺皇極矣。今觀江右之文，沉深者性
translation_en:
…the foliage flourished, but the roots had collapsed. When our imperial ancestor received Heaven’s mandate, he began instituting reforms; literary education then flourished greatly, and the ceremonial selection of worthy men resembled that of the Zhou dynasty. Thus the writing of that time was whole and unspoiled [?; the transcription repeats 噩]. In the hundred and several tens of years since, there have occasionally been slight changes. Yet although its form was expansive [?], it was not overornamented; although its cadences were distinct, they were not hurried; although its construction was rigorous, it was not harsh; and although its sound was resonant, it was not strident. This, too, was sufficient to serve as a model. Recently, however, writers have gathered ornate expressions and displayed curiosities, drifting somewhat into a tortuous and thorny manner of writing.
Our sagely Emperor has brought about a restoration. Taking Heaven as his model in cultivating men of talent, he has made literary style substantial and correct and has again promulgated a great proclamation. All within the seas have received his beneficence and conformed to the imperial norm. Now, observing the writing of Jiangyou, in those whose writing is profound, their nature …

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
以靜定而攝矣莊重者氣以
端默而凝矣䟽暢者心以貞
明而澄矣要約者道以易簡
而會矣瀏亮者德以淵朗而
淑矣猗歟
社稷之良乎語云金從鏤始瑩
木從劓始器象從磋始澤玉
從飾始璲故多士之反𣽎
===
聖天子涵移之化也而於孔子所
謂彬彬者符矣茲旅升有階
矣其思所以爲君子也乎多
士懋之哉是役也〔吉與〕訓導
許〔士德〕爲考試官學正王〔采〕
羅〔士賢〕王〔琮〕教諭毛〔孔刪〕陳
punctuated:
以靜定而攝矣，莊重者氣以端默而凝矣，䟽暢者心以貞明而澄矣，要約者道以易簡而會矣，瀏亮者德以淵朗而淑矣。猗歟，社稷之良乎！語云：「金從鏤始瑩，木從劓始器，象從磋始澤，玉從飾始璲。」故多士之反𣽎，聖天子涵移之化也，而於孔子所謂彬彬者符矣。茲旅升有階矣，其思所以爲君子也乎？多士懋之哉！
是役也，〔吉與〕訓導許〔士德〕爲考試官，學正王〔采〕、羅〔士賢〕、王〔琮〕，教諭毛〔孔刪〕、陳
translation_en:
…is brought under control through stillness and composure. In those whose writing is solemn, vital force is concentrated through uprightness and reserve; in those whose writing flows freely, the mind is clarified through steadfastness and illumination; in those whose writing is concise, the Way is comprehended through ease and simplicity; in those whose writing is clear and resonant, virtue is refined through depth and brightness. Ah, are these not worthy men of the state! As the saying goes: “Metal begins to shine only after engraving; wood becomes a useful vessel only after cutting; ivory gains its sheen only after polishing; jade becomes a pendant only after embellishment.” Thus, these scholars’ return to simplicity [?] is the result of the sage Son of Heaven’s nurturing and transforming influence, and accords with what Confucius called the harmonious balance of refinement and substance. Now there are steps by which they may advance together. Should they not reflect on how to become gentlemen? Scholars, strive diligently!
For this examination, 〔Ji and〕 Assistant Instructor Xu 〔Shide〕 served as Examiners. Instructors Wang 〔Cai〕, Luo 〔Shixian〕, and Wang 〔Cong〕, and Instructors Mao 〔Kongshan〕 and Chen …

text:
浙江處州府慶元縣儒學教諭汪澄江〔如練福建懷安縣人戊子貢士〕
湖廣辰州府盧溪縣儒學教諭官德章〔達卿福建閩縣人丁酉貢士〕
浙江金華府金華縣儒學教諭楊世瑞〔鳳來福建候官縣人丁酉貢士〕
湖廣永州府祁陽縣儒學教諭文世英〔伯彩廣西護衛人戊子貢士〕
浙江寧波府慈谿縣儒學訓導彭漢〔源㠾廣東新會縣人辛卯貢士〕
印卷官
江西等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷文廷用〔良佐湖廣會同縣人監生〕
江西等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷盧溥〔文博直隸長洲縣人監生〕
收掌試卷官
===
南昌府知府謝存儒〔懋珍湖廣蒲圻縣人丙戌進士〕
廣信府知府趙鏜〔振夫湖廣江陵縣人辛巳進士〕
九江府知府韋尚賢〔思肖福建南安縣人辛巳進士〕
贛州府知府康河〔德清陝西武功縣人癸未進士〕
受卷官

袁州府知府范欽〔堯卿浙江鄞縣人壬辰進士〕
吉安府知府李清〔介卿湖廣龍陽縣人癸未進士〕
吉安府同知張孟澄〔淵甫浙江鄞縣人壬午貢士〕
punctuated:
浙江處州府慶元縣儒學教諭汪澄江〔如練，福建懷安縣人，戊子貢士〕。
湖廣辰州府盧溪縣儒學教諭官德章〔達卿，福建閩縣人，丁酉貢士〕。
浙江金華府金華縣儒學教諭楊世瑞〔鳳來，福建候官縣人，丁酉貢士〕。
湖廣永州府祁陽縣儒學教諭文世英〔伯彩，廣西護衛人，戊子貢士〕。
浙江寧波府慈谿縣儒學訓導彭漢〔源㠾，廣東新會縣人，辛卯貢士〕。

江西等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷文廷用〔良佐，湖廣會同縣人，監生〕。
江西等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷盧溥〔文博，直隸長洲縣人，監生〕。

收掌試卷官：
南昌府知府謝存儒〔懋珍，湖廣蒲圻縣人，丙戌進士〕。
廣信府知府趙鏜〔振夫，湖廣江陵縣人，辛巳進士〕。
九江府知府韋尚賢〔思肖，福建南安縣人，辛巳進士〕。
贛州府知府康河〔德清，陝西武功縣人，癸未進士〕。

受卷官：
瑞州府知府孫鑾〔朝珂，直隸武進縣籍，定遠縣人，辛巳進士〕。
袁州府知府范欽〔堯卿，浙江鄞縣人，壬辰進士〕。
吉安府知府李清〔介卿，湖廣龍陽縣人，癸未進士〕。
吉安府同知張孟澄〔淵甫，浙江鄞縣人，壬午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Wang Chengjiang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Qingyuan County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Rulian and was from Huai’an County, Fujian. He was a tribute student of the wuzi year.
Guan Dezhang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Luxi County, Chenzhou Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Daqing and was from Min County, Fujian. He was a tribute student of the dingyou year.
Yang Shirui, Instructor of the Confucian School of Jinhua County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Fenglai and was from Houguan County, Fujian. He was a tribute student of the dingyou year.
Wen Shiying, Instructor of the Confucian School of Qiyang County, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Bocai and was from the Guangxi Princely Guard. He was a tribute student of the wuzi year.
Peng Han, Assistant Instructor of the Confucian School of Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Yuanyuan [?] and was from Xinhui County, Guangdong. He was a tribute student of the xinmao year.

Officials Responsible for Printing Examination Papers:
Wen Tingyong, Registrar in the Registry of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Liangzuo and was from Huitong County, Huguang. He was an Imperial University student.
Lu Pu, Registrar in the Registry of the Jiangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Wenbo and was from Changzhou County, Zhili. He was an Imperial University student.

Officials Responsible for the Custody of Examination Scripts:
Xie Cunru, Prefect of Nanchang, had the courtesy name Maozhen and was from Puqi County, Huguang. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingxu year.
Zhao Tang, Prefect of Guangxin, had the courtesy name Zhenfu and was from Jiangling County, Huguang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.
Wei Shangxian, Prefect of Jiujiang, had the courtesy name Sixiao and was from Nan’an County, Fujian. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.
Kang He, Prefect of Ganzhou, had the courtesy name Deqing and was from Wugong County, Shaanxi. He was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Officials Responsible for Receiving Examination Scripts:
Sun Luan, Prefect of Ruizhou, had the courtesy name Chaoke. He was registered in Wujin County, Zhili, and was originally from Dingyuan County. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.
Fan Qin, Prefect of Yuanzhou, had the courtesy name Yaoqing and was from Yin County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.
Li Qing, Prefect of Ji’an, had the courtesy name Jieqing and was from Longyang County, Huguang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.
Zhang Mengcheng, Vice Prefect of Ji’an, had the courtesy name Yuanfu and was from Yin County, Zhejiang. He was a tribute student of the renwu year.

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
廣信府同知徐官〔伯賢浙江蕭山縣人 丁丑進士〕
袁州府推官劉學易〔道甫山東壽光縣人 戊戌進士〕
彌封官
贛州府推官趙承謙〔德光直隸常熟縣籍 江陰縣人戊戌進士〕
袁州府分宜縣知縣陳鵠〔鳴霄浙江紹興衛籍 武進縣人戊戌進士〕
吉安府吉水縣知縣施譓〔敬叔浙江鄞縣人 戊戌進士〕
吉安府龍泉縣知縣歐禮〔汝和湖廣郴州人 乙酉貢士〕
撫州府臨川縣知縣胡士恂〔秉誠浙江臨海縣人 壬午貢士〕
廣信府貴溪縣知縣袁鳳鳴〔子時湖廣辰州衛籍 盱眙縣人戊戌進士〕
===
謄錄官
南康府通判趙迎〔汝賓河南鞏縣人 丙戌進士〕
南昌府奉新縣知縣胡億〔原一廣西儀衛司籍 慶元縣人己卯貢士〕
臨江府清江縣知縣沈儀〔懋德浙江仁和縣人 己卯貢士〕
吉安府泰和縣知縣王春復〔學孜福建晉江縣人 戊戌進士〕
撫州府東鄉縣知縣吳璋〔朝獻雲南騰衝衛籍 餘姚縣人乙酉貢士〕
饒州府鄱陽縣知縣徐方〔直大浙江餘姚縣人 乙未進士〕
對讀官
瑞州府高安縣知縣潘鉉〔希舉直隸婺源縣人 戊子貢士〕
punctuated:
廣信府同知徐官〔伯賢，浙江蕭山縣人，丁丑進士〕。袁州府推官劉學易〔道甫，山東壽光縣人，戊戌進士〕。

彌封官：
贛州府推官趙承謙〔德光，直隸常熟縣籍，江陰縣人，戊戌進士〕。袁州府分宜縣知縣陳鵠〔鳴霄，浙江紹興衛籍，武進縣人，戊戌進士〕。吉安府吉水縣知縣施譓〔敬叔，浙江鄞縣人，戊戌進士〕。吉安府龍泉縣知縣歐禮〔汝和，湖廣郴州人，乙酉貢士〕。撫州府臨川縣知縣胡士恂〔秉誠，浙江臨海縣人，壬午貢士〕。廣信府貴溪縣知縣袁鳳鳴〔子時，湖廣辰州衛籍，盱眙縣人，戊戌進士〕。

謄錄官：
南康府通判趙迎〔汝賓，河南鞏縣人，丙戌進士〕。南昌府奉新縣知縣胡億〔原一，廣西儀衛司籍，慶元縣人，己卯貢士〕。臨江府清江縣知縣沈儀〔懋德，浙江仁和縣人，己卯貢士〕。吉安府泰和縣知縣王春復〔學孜，福建晉江縣人，戊戌進士〕。撫州府東鄉縣知縣吳璋〔朝獻，雲南騰衝衛籍，餘姚縣人，乙酉貢士〕。饒州府鄱陽縣知縣徐方〔直大，浙江餘姚縣人，乙未進士〕。

對讀官：
瑞州府高安縣知縣潘鉉〔希舉，直隸婺源縣人，戊子貢士〕。
translation_en:
Xu Guan, Vice Prefect of Guangxin Prefecture, had the courtesy name Boxian and was from Xiaoshan County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the dingchou year.
Liu Xueyi, Prefectural Judge of Yuanzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Daofu and was from Shouguang County, Shandong. He was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.

Sealing Officials:
Zhao Chengqian, Prefectural Judge of Ganzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Deguang. He was registered in Changshu County, Zhili, originated from Jiangyin County, and was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.
Chen Hu, Magistrate of Fenyi County in Yuanzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Mingxiao. He was registered with Shaoxing Guard in Zhejiang, originated from Wujin County, and was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.
Shi Hui, Magistrate of Jishui County in Ji’an Prefecture, had the courtesy name Jingshu and was from Yin County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.
Ou Li, Magistrate of Longquan County in Ji’an Prefecture, had the courtesy name Ruhe and was from Chenzhou, Huguang. He was a tribute student (gongshi) of the yiyou year.
Hu Shixun, Magistrate of Linchuan County in Fuzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Bingcheng and was from Linhai County, Zhejiang. He was a tribute student of the renwu year.
Yuan Fengming, Magistrate of Guixi County in Guangxin Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zishi. He was registered with Chenzhou Guard in Huguang, originated from Xuyi County, and was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.

Transcription Officials:
Zhao Ying, Assistant Prefect of Nankang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Rubin and was from Gong County, Henan. He was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.
Hu Yi, Magistrate of Fengxin County in Nanchang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yuanyi. He was registered with the Guangxi Ceremonial Guard Office, originated from Qingyuan County, and was a tribute student of the jimao year.
Shen Yi, Magistrate of Qingjiang County in Linjiang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Maode and was from Renhe County, Zhejiang. He was a tribute student of the jimao year.
Wang Chunfu, Magistrate of Taihe County in Ji’an Prefecture, had the courtesy name Xuezi and was from Jinjiang County, Fujian. He was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.
Wu Zhang, Magistrate of Dongxiang County in Fuzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Chaoxian. He was registered with Tengchong Guard in Yunnan, originated from Yuyao County, and was a tribute student of the yiyou year.
Xu Fang, Magistrate of Poyang County in Raozhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zhida and was from Yuyao County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Proofreading Officials:
Pan Xuan, Magistrate of Gao’an County in Ruizhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Xiju and was from Wuyuan County, Zhili. He was a tribute student of the wuzi year.

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
吉安府廬陵縣知縣袁衮〔補之直隸吳縣人戊戌進士〕
建昌府南城縣知縣曹逵〔顯卿直隸太倉州人己丑進士〕
南康府星子縣知縣阮朝隨〔予方湖廣麻城縣人壬午貢士〕
南康府建昌縣知縣徐九皐〔遠卿雲南右衛人戊子貢士〕
贛州府瑞金縣知縣王鈇〔公儀福建福州中衛人壬辰進士〕
巡綽官
南昌衛指揮使朱恩〔汝治直隸懷遠縣人〕
贛州衛指揮使馮英〔德華直隸無錫縣人〕
南昌衛指揮僉事楊慶〔以善山東滋陽縣人〕
袁州衛指揮僉事馮恩〔德厚直隸來安縣人〕
===
搜檢官
南昌衛指揮使魏清〔澄之湖廣應山縣人〕
南昌衛指揮僉事曹椿〔時喬直隸吳縣人〕
南昌衛指揮僉事汪材〔大用直隸和州人〕
南昌衛左所副千戶王嵩〔峻瞻直隸遷安縣人〕
供給官
江西都指揮使司經歷司經歷羅威〔汝重四川遂寧縣人吏員〕
江西等處承宣布政使司經歷司都事潘鍇〔廷剛浙江仁和縣人知印〕
punctuated:
吉安府廬陵縣知縣袁衮〔補之，直隸吳縣人，戊戌進士〕。建昌府南城縣知縣曹逵〔顯卿，直隸太倉州人，己丑進士〕。南康府星子縣知縣阮朝隨〔予方，湖廣麻城縣人，壬午貢士〕。南康府建昌縣知縣徐九皐〔遠卿，雲南右衛人，戊子貢士〕。贛州府瑞金縣知縣王鈇〔公儀，福建福州中衛人，壬辰進士〕。

巡綽官：南昌衛指揮使朱恩〔汝治，直隸懷遠縣人〕。贛州衛指揮使馮英〔德華，直隸無錫縣人〕。南昌衛指揮僉事楊慶〔以善，山東滋陽縣人〕。袁州衛指揮僉事馮恩〔德厚，直隸來安縣人〕。

搜檢官：南昌衛指揮使魏清〔澄之，湖廣應山縣人〕。南昌衛指揮僉事曹椿〔時喬，直隸吳縣人〕。南昌衛指揮僉事汪材〔大用，直隸和州人〕。南昌衛左所副千戶王嵩〔峻瞻，直隸遷安縣人〕。

供給官：江西都指揮使司經歷司經歷羅威〔汝重，四川遂寧縣人，吏員〕。江西等處承宣布政使司經歷司都事潘鍇〔廷剛，浙江仁和縣人，知印〕。
translation_en:

Cao Kui, courtesy name Xianqing, was Magistrate of Nancheng County, Jianchang Prefecture. He was from Taicang Subprefecture, Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year.

Ruan Chaosui, courtesy name Yufang, was Magistrate of Xingzi County, Nankang Prefecture. He was from Macheng County, Huguang, and was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the renwu year.

Xu Jiugao, courtesy name Yuanqing, was Magistrate of Jianchang County, Nankang Prefecture. He was from Yunnan Right Guard and was a tribute scholar of the wuzi year.

Wang Fu, courtesy name Gongyi, was Magistrate of Ruijin County, Ganzhou Prefecture. He was from Fuzhou Central Guard, Fujian, and was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.

Patrol Officials:

Zhu En, courtesy name Ruzhi, was Commander of Nanchang Guard. He was from Huaiyuan County, Zhili.

Feng Ying, courtesy name Dehua, was Commander of Ganzhou Guard. He was from Wuxi County, Zhili.

Yang Qing, courtesy name Yishan, was Assistant Commander of Nanchang Guard. He was from Ziyang County, Shandong.

Feng En, courtesy name Dehou, was Assistant Commander of Yuanzhou Guard. He was from Lai’an County, Zhili.

Search and Inspection Officials:

Wei Qing, courtesy name Chengzhi, was Commander of Nanchang Guard. He was from Yingshan County, Huguang.

Cao Chun, courtesy name Shiqiao, was Assistant Commander of Nanchang Guard. He was from Wu County, Zhili.

Wang Cai, courtesy name Dayong, was Assistant Commander of Nanchang Guard. He was from He Subprefecture, Zhili.

Wang Song, courtesy name Junzhan, was Deputy Battalion Commander of the Left Battalion of Nanchang Guard. He was from Qian’an County, Zhili.

Supply Officials:

Luo Wei, courtesy name Ruzhong, was Registrar in the Registry of the Jiangxi Regional Military Commission. He was from Suining County, Sichuan, and had a clerical-service background.

Pan Kai, courtesy name Tinggang, was Office Manager in the Registry of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission. He was from Renhe County, Zhejiang, and had served as a Seal Keeper.

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子貢問曰有一言而可以終身行之者乎
子曰其恕乎己所不欲勿施於人
誠者天之道也誠之者人之道也誠者不
勉而中不思而得從容中道聖人也誠
之者擇善而固執之者也
言近而指遠者善言也守約而施博者善
道也
===
易
泰小往大來吉亨
敦艮之吉以厚終也
見乃謂之象形乃謂之器
易之爲書也廣大悉備有天道焉有人道
焉有地道焉兼三才而兩之故六六者
非他也三才之道也
書
彰厥有常吉哉
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子貢問曰：「有一言而可以終身行之者乎？」子曰：「其恕乎！己所不欲，勿施於人。」

誠者，天之道也；誠之者，人之道也。誠者，不勉而中，不思而得，從容中道，聖人也。誠之者，擇善而固執之者也。

言近而指遠者，善言也；守約而施博者，善道也。

易

泰：小往大來，吉亨。

敦艮之吉，以厚終也。

見乃謂之象，形乃謂之器。

易之爲書也，廣大悉備，有天道焉，有人道焉，有地道焉。兼三才而兩之，故六。六者，非他也，三才之道也。

書

彰厥有常，吉哉！
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Zigong asked, “Is there a single word that one can put into practice throughout one’s life?” The Master said, “Perhaps reciprocity! What you do not desire for yourself, do not impose on others.”

Sincerity is the Way of Heaven; making oneself sincere is the human Way. One who is sincere hits the mark without effort, attains understanding without deliberation, and follows the Way naturally and at ease: such a person is a sage. One who makes himself sincere chooses what is good and holds firmly to it.

Words that concern what is near yet point to what is far are good words. Holding to what is essential yet applying it broadly is the good Way.

Book of Changes

Tai (Peace): The small departs and the great comes. Auspicious; success.

The auspiciousness of steadfast stillness lies in bringing matters to an end with substantial virtue.

What becomes manifest is called an image; what takes form is called a concrete object.

The Book of Changes is vast and comprehensive, containing everything. It contains the Way of Heaven, the human Way, and the Way of Earth. It combines the Three Powers and doubles them, thus making six lines. These six are nothing other than the Way of the Three Powers.

Book of Documents

Make manifest their constancy—auspicious indeed!

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
惟臣欽若惟民從乂
欽哉往敷乃訓慎乃服命率由典常以蕃
王室弘乃烈祖律乃有民永綏厥位毗
予一人世世享德萬邦作式俾我有周
無斁
功崇惟志業廣惟勤惟克果斷乃罔後艱
詩
九月築場圃十月納禾稼黍稷重穋禾麻
菽麥嗟我農夫我稼既同上入執宮功
晝爾于茅宵爾索綯亟其乘屋其始播
百穀
===
永錫爾極時萬時億
仲山甫之德柔嘉維則令儀令色小心翼
翼古訓是式威儀是力天子是若明命
使賦王命仲山甫式是百辟纘戎祖考
王躬是保出納王命王之喉舌賦政于
外四方爰發
對越在天駿奔走在廟
punctuated:
惟臣欽若，惟民從乂。

欽哉！往敷乃訓，慎乃服命，率由典常，以蕃王室。弘乃烈祖，律乃有民，永綏厥位。毗予一人，世世享德，萬邦作式，俾我有周無斁。

功崇惟志，業廣惟勤。惟克果斷，乃罔後艱。

詩

九月築場圃，十月納禾稼。黍稷重穋，禾麻菽麥。嗟我農夫，我稼既同，上入執宮功。晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯。亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。

永錫爾極，時萬時億。

仲山甫之德，柔嘉維則。令儀令色，小心翼翼。古訓是式，威儀是力。天子是若，明命使賦。王命仲山甫，式是百辟。纘戎祖考，王躬是保。出納王命，王之喉舌。賦政于外，四方爰發。

對越在天，駿奔走在廟。
translation_en:
Let the ministers reverently comply, and the people will follow and be well governed.

Be reverent! Go forth and disseminate your instructions; attend carefully to the duties entrusted to you. Follow the established statutes and enduring norms, thereby serving as a bulwark for the royal house. Carry forward the achievements of your illustrious ancestors, govern your people, and secure your position forever. Assist me, the One Man, so that generation after generation may enjoy your virtue, and the myriad states take you as their model, ensuring that our Zhou never meets with rejection.

Lofty achievement depends on resolve; extensive accomplishment depends on diligence. If you can act decisively, there will be no subsequent difficulties.

Book of Odes

In the ninth month we prepare the threshing grounds and garden plots; in the tenth month we bring in the crops: the millets, the late-ripening and early-ripening grain, the rice, hemp, beans, and wheat. Ah, we farmers! Once our harvest has all been gathered, we go up to undertake work on the houses. By day you gather thatch; by night you twist ropes. Hurry up onto the roofs to repair them, for soon you must begin sowing the hundred grains.

May you forever be granted blessings in the fullest measure, by tens of thousands and hundreds of millions.

The virtue of Zhongshan Fu takes gentleness and goodness as its rule. His bearing and expression are fine; he is cautious and reverent. He models himself on ancient teachings and diligently cultivates dignified conduct. He obeys the Son of Heaven, who entrusts him with clear commands to disseminate. The king commands Zhongshan Fu: “Be a model for the many lords. Continue the work of your forefathers and protect the king’s person. Convey the royal commands, serving as the king’s throat and tongue. Proclaim the government’s orders abroad, and the four quarters will respond.”

They respond to and exalt the spirits in Heaven, and hasten about in service within the ancestral temple.

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
春秋
春齊侯宋人陳人蔡人邾人會于北杏〔莊公十有三年〕
春齊人陳人曹人伐宋
夏單伯會伐宋〔俱莊公十有四年〕
宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯會晉師于棐林伐鄭〔宣公元年〕
冬公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕
子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子光伐鄭〔襄公九年〕
===
春王正月舍中軍〔昭公五年〕冬築郎囿〔昭公九年〕
晉人執我行人叔孫舍〔昭公二十有三年〕
叔孫舍至自晉〔昭公二十有四年〕
禮記
君子耆老不徒行庶人耆老不徒食
大傅在前少傅在後入則有保出則有師
是以教喻而德成也
樂極和禮極順內和而外順則民瞻其顔
punctuated:
春秋
春，齊侯、宋人、陳人、蔡人、邾人會于北杏。〔莊公十有三年〕春，齊人、陳人、曹人伐宋。夏，單伯會伐宋。〔俱莊公十有四年〕宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯會晉師于棐林，伐鄭。〔宣公元年〕冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。〔襄公九年〕春，王正月，舍中軍。〔昭公五年〕冬，築郎囿。〔昭公九年〕晉人執我行人叔孫舍。〔昭公二十有三年〕叔孫舍至自晉。〔昭公二十有四年〕
禮記
君子耆老不徒行，庶人耆老不徒食。
大傅在前，少傅在後，入則有保，出則有師，是以教喻而德成也。
樂極和，禮極順，內和而外順，則民瞻其顔
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals
In spring, the Marquis of Qi and representatives of Song, Chen, Cai, and Zhu met at Beixing. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕 In spring, forces of Qi, Chen, and Cao attacked Song. In summer, the Earl of Shan joined the attack on Song. 〔Both in the fourteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕 The Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao met the army of Jin at Feilin and attacked Zheng. 〔First year of Duke Xuan.〕 In winter, the duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi (杞), the Viscount of Xiao Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi (齊), in attacking Zheng. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xiang.〕 In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the Central Army was abolished. 〔Fifth year of Duke Zhao.〕 In winter, the game park at Lang was built. 〔Ninth year of Duke Zhao.〕 The men of Jin detained our envoy Shusun She. 〔Twenty-third year of Duke Zhao.〕 Shusun She returned from Jin. 〔Twenty-fourth year of Duke Zhao.〕
Record of Rites
When men of rank grow old, they do not travel on foot; when commoners grow old, they do not eat their food without accompanying dishes.
The Grand Mentor is in front, and the Junior Mentor behind. Within, there is a guardian; outside, there is a preceptor. Thus instruction brings understanding, and virtue is perfected.
Music brings harmony to its fullest extent; ritual brings accord to its fullest extent. With harmony within and accord without, the people look upon his countenance …

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄

慢焉故德煇動於內而民莫不承聽理
發諸外而民莫不承順故曰致禮樂之
道舉而錯之天下無難矣
天子親耕粢盛秬鬯以事上帝故諸侯勤
以輔事於天子
第貳場
論
仁心立政之本
===
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢春和議賑貸詔〔文帝元年〕
擬唐以韓休為黃門侍郎同平章事誥〔開元二十一年〕
擬
賜
聖學心法翰林院學士胡廣等謝表〔永樂七年〕

增減官文書
punctuated:

論
仁心，立政之本。
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢春和議賑貸詔〔文帝元年〕
擬唐以韓休為黃門侍郎、同平章事誥〔開元二十一年〕

translation_en:
…expression and do not contend with him; on seeing his appearance, the people develop no disrespect or arrogance. Thus, when the radiance of virtue stirs within, none among the people fails to listen obediently; when principle manifests itself outwardly, none fails to comply. Hence it is said: once the Way of ritual and music has been fully realized, there is no difficulty in putting it into practice throughout the realm.
The Son of Heaven personally plows to provide sacrificial grain and black millet for aromatic sacrificial wine, with which to serve the Lord on High. Thus the feudal lords exert themselves to assist the Son of Heaven in this service.
Second Session
Discourse
A benevolent heart is the foundation of governance.
One topic assigned [?] from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials.

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
市司評物價
僧道拜父母
官馬不調習
斷罪引律令
第叁場
策五道
問聖人之道與天地爲一而其爲文則與
天地相爲經緯如伏羲之爻象堯舜之
典謨商周之雅頌是已漢唐而下三代
有章秋風有辭帝範有書闕里有賛崇
儒有論其辭非不近古而治則有未逮
其故何歟洪惟我
===
太祖高皇帝
御製諸篇見於儒臣劉基宋濂葉所賛述者眞
與古聖人所作相爲矣今我
皇上
祖德有詩
穀祇蠶壇有賦
punctuated:
市司評物價。僧道拜父母。官馬不調習。斷罪引律令。

第叁場。策五道。

問：聖人之道與天地爲一，而其爲文則與天地相爲經緯，如伏羲之爻象、堯舜之典謨、商周之雅頌是已。漢唐而下，三代有章，秋風有辭，帝範有書，闕里有賛，崇儒有論，其辭非不近古，而治則有未逮，其故何歟？洪惟我太祖高皇帝御製諸篇，見於儒臣劉基、宋濂、葉所賛述者，眞與古聖人所作相爲矣。今我皇上，祖德有詩，穀祇、蠶壇有賦，
translation_en:
The market office appraises commodity prices. Buddhist monks and Daoist priests bow to their parents. Government horses are not trained. Statutes and ordinances are cited in deciding criminal cases.

Third Session. Five Policy Questions.

Question: The Way of the sages is one with Heaven and Earth, and their writings form warp and weft with Heaven and Earth. Such are Fuxi’s hexagram lines and images, the canons and counsels of Yao and Shun, and the odes and hymns of Shang and Zhou. From the Han and Tang onward, there have been a composition on the Three Dynasties [?], verses on the Autumn Wind, the book Model for Emperors, a eulogy on Queli, and a discourse on Honoring Confucian Learning. Their language certainly approaches that of antiquity, yet their government fell short. Why was this?

We reverently reflect that the various writings personally composed by our Emperor Taizu Gao, as praised and expounded by the Confucian officials Liu Ji, Song Lian, and Ye [?], truly accord with the works of the ancient sages [?]. Now our reigning emperor has composed poems on ancestral virtue and rhapsodies on the grain and earth spirits [?] and the Silkworm Altar…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
大衍龍飛有錄皆以精一執中之學發明仁孝
□一有箴
誠敬之理真又與
聖祖所作相孚矣然則
睿謨要旨可能仰窺其萬一耶諸士于諸有
聖化久矣其揄揚之以諭夫日用而不知者
問三王異世不相襲禮五帝殊時不相沿
樂然五禮之制肇自唐虞歷夏商周無
改而周禮大司徒以六樂防萬民之情
===
又不專於大武何歟漢唐以下有叔孫
禮有占觀禮有建隆禮有其□□樂有雅
樂有大安樂其於三代之制同歟異歟
洪惟我
太祖高皇帝功成治定
命牛諒制禮陶凱典樂百八十年熙然太和亦
既定民志和上下矣我
皇上聖德中興中和建極邇者修
脩明禮樂更定
punctuated:
《大衍》《龍飛》有錄，皆以精一執中之學發明仁孝，□一有箴，誠敬之理，真又與聖祖所作相孚矣。然則睿謨要旨，可能仰窺其萬一耶？諸士于諸有聖化久矣，其揄揚之，以諭夫日用而不知者。

問：三王異世，不相襲禮；五帝殊時，不相沿樂。然五禮之制肇自唐虞，歷夏商周無改，而《周禮》大司徒以六樂防萬民之情，又不專於《大武》，何歟？漢唐以下，有叔孫禮，有占觀禮，有建隆禮，有其□□樂，有雅樂，有大安樂，其於三代之制同歟異歟？洪惟我太祖高皇帝功成治定，命牛諒制禮，陶凱典樂。百八十年，熙然太和，亦既定民志、和上下矣。我皇上聖德中興，中和建極，邇者修脩明禮樂，更定
translation_en:
…There are records entitled Great Expansion (Dayan) and the Dragon’s Ascent (Longfei). All draw upon the learning of refinement and single-mindedness, and of holding fast to the Mean, to elucidate the principles of benevolence, filial piety, sincerity, and reverence. The text also mentions an admonition on “□一” here [?]. These writings truly accord with those of the Sagely Ancestor. Might we then reverently discern even a ten-thousandth part of the essential meaning of His Majesty’s wise counsels? You gentlemen have long received the sage influence [?]. Extol it, so as to instruct those who make use of it daily without understanding it.

Question: The Three Kings lived in different ages and did not copy one another’s rites; the Five Emperors lived at different times and did not perpetuate one another’s music. Yet the system of the Five Rites originated under Tang Yao and Yu Shun and remained unchanged through the Xia, Shang, and Zhou. Moreover, in the Rites of Zhou, the Minister of Education used the Six Musical Performances to restrain the feelings of the myriad people, without relying exclusively on the Great Martial Dance (Dawu). Why was this?

From the Han and Tang onward, there were the rites of Shusun, the rites of Zhanguan [?], and the rites of Jianlong; there were “its □□ music” [?], elegant music (yayue), and the Music of Great Peace (Da’an). Were these the same as, or different from, the institutions of the Three Dynasties?

We reverently reflect that, once our Emperor Taizu Gao had accomplished his achievements and established orderly government, he commanded Niu Liang to formulate the rites and Tao Kai to oversee music. For one hundred and eighty years, glorious supreme harmony has prevailed: the people’s aspirations have been settled, and those above and below brought into accord. Our present Emperor, through his sagely virtue, has brought about a resurgence and established the supreme standard through equilibrium and harmony. Recently, he has cultivated and clarified rites and music [?], and revised…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
大明集禮千載一時真為
禮典之盛可能指而言之
與數度數之詳聲容之
與說者謂禮樂二經不可偏廢今樂記
雖附於禮經而全旨未及於大備茲欲
考黃鍾員徑之法截五聲二變之數參
變宮變徵之宜審變律半聲之例定為
樂經一書以補六經之缺有志於禮樂
者其悉心以對
===
問尚友古人學者分內事也而况有功德
于其鄉者乎大江之西故多治績而名
臣彥士載在史志可稽也試舉其表著
者言之有退奸貪逆忠善去檻井而虎
東渡江者有勤於吏職筆翰如流匡輔
王室竟以成功者有風度沉整撫宜春
而列郡是式者有歲旱奏免民租縱囚
如期而還者有計備贖隸而政可推之
天下者有都督洪州修孺子祠而禱輒
應者有卓犖大節奬掖士類不以遷謫
punctuated:
《大明集禮》，千載一時，真為禮典之盛，可能指而言之與？數度數之詳，聲容之與？說者謂禮樂二經不可偏廢。今《樂記》雖附於《禮經》，而全旨未及於大備。茲欲考黃鍾員徑之法，截五聲二變之數，參變宮變徵之宜，審變律半聲之例，定為《樂經》一書，以補六經之缺。有志於禮樂者，其悉心以對。
問：尚友古人，學者分內事也，而况有功德于其鄉者乎？大江之西，故多治績，而名臣彥士載在史志，可稽也。試舉其表著者言之：有退奸貪、逆忠善、去檻井而虎東渡江者；有勤於吏職、筆翰如流、匡輔王室竟以成功者；有風度沉整、撫宜春而列郡是式者；有歲旱奏免民租、縱囚如期而還者；有計備贖隸而政可推之天下者；有都督洪州、修孺子祠而禱輒應者；有卓犖大節、奬掖士類、不以遷謫
translation_en:
…the Collected Rituals of the Great Ming (Da Ming jili)—an occasion encountered once in a thousand years, truly a flourishing of ritual institutions. Can you identify and explain these achievements? The particulars of numerical standards and measures, and of musical sounds and ceremonial forms [?]? Commentators say that neither of the two classics of rites and music may be neglected. Although the Record of Music (Yueji) is now appended to the Classic of Rites, its full purport has not yet been comprehensively set forth. We now wish to investigate the methods for determining the circumference and diameter of the Huangzhong pitch pipe, the numerical proportions for cutting pipes for the five notes and two altered notes, the appropriate use of the altered gong and altered zhi notes, and the rules for altered pitches and half tones [?]. These would be established as a single Classic of Music, filling the gap among the Six Classics. Let those devoted to rites and music apply themselves wholeheartedly to their replies.
Question: To take the ancients as friends is a scholar’s proper undertaking. How much more so when those ancients rendered meritorious service and conferred benefits upon his own region! The country west of the great Yangzi has long abounded in achievements of good government, and its eminent ministers and distinguished scholars are recorded in histories and gazetteers, where they may be examined. Let us cite some of the most conspicuous examples. There was one who dismissed the wicked and greedy, welcomed the loyal and good, and removed cage traps and pit traps, whereupon the tigers crossed the river eastward. There was one who diligently performed his official duties, whose writing flowed freely, and who ultimately succeeded in supporting the royal house. There was one whose bearing was composed and dignified, and whose administration of Yichun became a model for the surrounding commanderies. There was one who, in a year of drought, memorialized requesting remission of the people’s grain taxes, and whose prisoners, released temporarily, returned at the appointed time. There was one who devised arrangements to redeem bondservants [?], and whose methods of government could be extended throughout the realm. There was one who served as Area Commander of Hongzhou and restored the shrine of Ruzi, where prayers invariably received a response. There was one of outstanding integrity who encouraged and supported scholars and did not allow demotion and exile to…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
介意者有自魯郡公遷撫州刺史脩□
築陂而民感其惠者有守義愛民緩期
輟畬以嫁前令之女者有下三章約五
五贊堂條聖賢爲學大端而化民成俗
者有興學校明教化活饑民以萬計者
有爲南安軍司理而不殺人以媚人者
有改鹽法鑿谿石而民賴以爲利者有
爲虔州司法而立斷疑獄者有一錢不
取而妖禽不敢啼樹者有增孝義二十
===
四圖而化民割股救親者有議定歲鑄
奏免錮送止房地出稅放黥配歸農而
江人懷慕者有爲江西轉運使不增羨
餘稱識大體者是皆歷代之選也今名
宦祠亦必羣尸之矣可得而悉指歟抑
皆合於祭義歟仰惟
聖天子作人弘化凡郡縣之吏固亦式承
德意而明功課績迺有不逮於數子者其故
何歟試繹其旨以告
punctuated:
介意者；有自魯郡公遷撫州刺史，脩□築陂，而民感其惠者；有守義愛民，緩期輟畬，以嫁前令之女者；有下三章約，五五贊堂，條聖賢爲學大端，而化民成俗者；有興學校，明教化，活饑民以萬計者；有爲南安軍司理，而不殺人以媚人者；有改鹽法，鑿谿石，而民賴以爲利者；有爲虔州司法，而立斷疑獄者；有一錢不取，而妖禽不敢啼樹者；有增孝義二十四圖，而化民割股救親者；有議定歲鑄，奏免錮送，止房地出稅，放黥配歸農，而江人懷慕者；有爲江西轉運使，不增羨餘，稱識大體者。是皆歷代之選也。今名宦祠亦必羣尸之矣，可得而悉指歟？抑皆合於祭義歟？
仰惟聖天子作人弘化，凡郡縣之吏，固亦式承德意，而明功課績，迺有不逮於數子者，其故何歟？試繹其旨以告。
translation_en:
…take it to heart; there was one who went from being Duke of Lu Commandery to Prefect of Fuzhou, repaired □ and built embankments, for whose beneficence the people were grateful; one who upheld righteousness and cherished the people, extended deadlines and suspended cultivation [?] to provide for the marriage of the previous magistrate’s daughter; one who issued a compact in three articles, established a hall of commendation [?], and set out the principal teachings of the sages and worthies concerning learning, thereby transforming the people and shaping their customs; one who established schools, promoted moral instruction, and saved tens of thousands from starvation; one who served as Judicial Administrator of Nan’an Military Prefecture and would not kill people to curry favor; one who revised the salt regulations and cut through rocks in streams, bringing benefits on which the people relied; one who served as Judicial Officer of Qianzhou and promptly resolved doubtful cases; one who would not accept a single coin, so that even ominous birds dared not cry in the trees; one who added twenty-four illustrations of filial piety and righteousness, inspiring people to cut flesh from their thighs to save their parents; one who deliberated upon and fixed the annual coinage quota, petitioned to end transport under confinement, stopped taxes on houses and land, and released those sentenced to tattooing and penal exile to return to farming, whom the people of Jiangxi remembered with affection; and one who served as Transport Commissioner of Jiangxi, did not increase surplus revenues, and was praised for understanding the larger interests of government. These were all outstanding men of successive dynasties. Surely they are now all enshrined in the shrines to eminent officials. Can you identify every one of them? And does the worship of them all accord with the principles governing sacrifice?
We reverently reflect that the sagely Son of Heaven nurtures talent and extends moral transformation. Officials throughout the prefectures and counties surely also respectfully carry out his virtuous intentions, while their accomplishments are brought to light and their achievements assessed. Yet some fail to match these several men. What accounts for this? Expound the underlying meaning and give your answer.

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
問帝王制馭夷狄之道若干羽之格崇密
之伐見於詩書可考也然似無事於邊
備者豈帝王制勝之策自有出於萬全
者耶後世論馭夷者不過兩科論和戎
者亦止五利而已是耶非耶宋儒之議
果合帝王之道否耶伏惟我
太祖高皇帝汛掃胡元復中國所自有之地
成祖文皇帝丕揚
聖武大舉北伐前代以來未有如我
===
國家之盛者也當時設重鎮者五後又增置
寧夏榆林等衛總爲九邊抑孰爲要害
者耶今邊境雖屢告捷而虜騎時或鼠
伏於河套將何策以制馭之耶邇者
明詔廷臣講求邊備
廟堂之上蓋必有成筭矣然武舉雖設將領
未見其得人清勾雖密行伍未見其克
足寺苑有常牧而馬常告乏歲儲有常
規而食常告匱其在
punctuated: 問：帝王制馭夷狄之道，若干羽之格、崇密之伐，見於詩書，可考也。然似無事於邊備者，豈帝王制勝之策自有出於萬全者耶？後世論馭夷者，不過兩科；論和戎者，亦止五利而已。是耶？非耶？宋儒之議，果合帝王之道否耶？伏惟我太祖高皇帝汛掃胡元，復中國所自有之地；成祖文皇帝丕揚聖武，大舉北伐，前代以來未有如我國家之盛者也。當時設重鎮者五，後又增置寧夏、榆林等衛，總爲九邊，抑孰爲要害者耶？今邊境雖屢告捷，而虜騎時或鼠伏於河套，將何策以制馭之耶？邇者明詔廷臣講求邊備，廟堂之上蓋必有成筭矣。然武舉雖設，將領未見其得人；清勾雖密，行伍未見其克足；寺苑有常牧，而馬常告乏；歲儲有常規，而食常告匱。其在
translation_en:
Question: The ways in which ancient emperors and kings controlled the non-Chinese peoples—such as winning their submission through dances with shields and feather plumes, and campaigning against Chong and Mi—are recorded in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents and can be examined there. Yet they seem to have had no need for frontier defenses. Could it be that the strategies by which these emperors and kings secured victory inherently ensured complete success? Later discussions of controlling non-Chinese peoples comprise no more than two approaches, while arguments for making peace with them enumerate only five advantages. Are these arguments right or wrong? Do the views of the Song Confucian scholars truly accord with the way of the ancient emperors and kings?

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao swept away the Mongol Yuan and recovered the territory that had originally belonged to China. Emperor Chengzu Wen greatly displayed his sagely military might and launched major northern campaigns. No preceding dynasty ever equaled the splendor of our state. At that time, five major garrison commands were established; subsequently, guards such as Ningxia and Yulin were added, making up the Nine Frontier Commands. Which of these occupy the strategically vital positions? Although victories are now repeatedly reported along the frontier, enemy cavalry sometimes lurk like rats in the Hetao region. What strategy should be used to control them?

Recently, an imperial edict instructed the court officials to investigate frontier defenses. Surely those at the highest levels of government already have a settled plan. Yet although the military examinations have been instituted, they have not visibly secured suitable men as commanders. Although the checking of military registers and requisitioning of men are rigorous, the ranks have not visibly reached their full strength. The Court of the Imperial Stud and its pastures maintain regular horse breeding, yet shortages of horses are constantly reported. There are established rules for annual stockpiling, yet provisions are constantly reported to be insufficient. Where the responsibility lies…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
方謂非義耶大抵貴賤之勢雖異而義實同在
子倡之以公則下有是心者孰不興起豈特巨
之忠君欲爲孝弟慈者皆得自盡天下有不平
乎使徒責己薄責人厚則非絜矩喻衆此固吾
夫子非所謂義而亦豈所謂忠恕哉
第貳場
論
仁心立政之本
王渤
同考試官教諭文　批〔萬斛泉源隨地涌出而不可竭非有本者能如是耶是之取爾〕
同考試官教諭楊　批〔意本六經而文逼秦漢其留心古學者耶不然何其約而達微而臧也諸士子〕
諒莫能先矣
考試官訓導許　批〔理明氣暢格古意新論之〕
隹者也
考試官教諭周　批〔不易之論〕
聖人所以致天下之治者不忍人之心而已矣
punctuated:
方謂非義耶？大抵貴賤之勢雖異，而義實同。在子倡之以公，則下有是心者孰不興起？豈特巨之忠君，欲爲孝弟慈者皆得自盡，天下有不平乎？使徒責己薄、責人厚，則非絜矩喻衆，此固吾夫子非所謂義，而亦豈所謂忠恕哉！

第貳場
論
仁心立政之本
王渤

同考試官教諭文，批〔萬斛泉源，隨地涌出而不可竭，非有本者能如是耶？是之取爾。〕
同考試官教諭楊，批〔意本六經，而文逼秦漢，其留心古學者耶？不然，何其約而達、微而臧也！諸士子〕諒莫能先矣。
考試官訓導許，批〔理明氣暢，格古意新，論之〕隹者也。
考試官教諭周，批〔不易之論。〕

聖人所以致天下之治者，不忍人之心而已矣。
translation_en:
…could this then be called unrighteous [?]? Generally, although the positions of the exalted and the lowly differ, righteousness is in fact the same for both. If you [?] take the lead through impartiality, who among those below who possess this disposition would fail to rise to the occasion? Not only would ministers [?] be loyal to their ruler: all who wished to practice filial devotion, fraternal respect, and parental kindness could fully realize their aspirations. Would anything under Heaven remain inequitable? If one merely demands little of oneself and much of others, this is no way to apply the measuring square of reciprocity and instruct the multitude. Our Master would certainly not call this righteousness; how could it be called conscientiousness and reciprocity either?

Second Session
Discourse
A Benevolent Heart Is the Foundation of Government
Wang Bo

Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor, comments: “A spring yielding ten thousand bushels gushes forth wherever it finds an opening and cannot be exhausted. Could anyone without a firm foundation achieve this? This is why I select it.”

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “Its ideas are rooted in the Six Classics, while its writing approaches that of the Qin and Han. Has its author devoted himself to ancient learning? Otherwise, how could it be so concise yet expressive, subtle yet sound? Surely none of the other candidates can surpass him.”

Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Its reasoning is clear and its vital force flows freely; its style is ancient and its ideas fresh. It is an excellent [?] discourse.”

Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “An unassailable argument.”

That by which the sages bring order to all under Heaven is simply a heart that cannot bear the suffering of others.

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
何也仁也吾所受於天地之心也有不忍人之
心斯有不忍人之政是故禮樂刑政所以齊天
下之勢而通其情者皆不忍斯民之心推之也
不然則施之無本治之無具豈能達之天下哉
孟子曰徒善不足以為政徒法不能以自行胡
氏子學孟子而有得者故曰仁心立政之本均
田為政之先蓋仁政必自經界始亦孟子之說
也吾嘗觀之天地矣乾以易知坤以簡能生生
化□無所止息天地之大政也震之出也巽之
===
齊□也離之相見也兌之說也其盛也顧於一陽
之復也乃曰見天地之心焉何也見天地之仁
也苟於復也不能含蓄醞釀俾生意滋息於專
一翕聚之中則亦安能鼓舞和氣囿天下之物
而化生之乎故曰復其見天地之心乎聖人者
法天者也則其仁可知矣政可知矣旣嘗制禮
以一天下矣作樂以和天下矣明刑以齊天下
矣立政以導天下矣田不井而均之則無以定
分無以安業無以平賦無以制變雖有禮樂刑
punctuated:
何也？仁也，吾所受於天地之心也。有不忍人之心，斯有不忍人之政。是故禮樂刑政，所以齊天下之勢而通其情者，皆不忍斯民之心推之也。不然，則施之無本，治之無具，豈能達之天下哉？孟子曰：「徒善不足以為政，徒法不能以自行。」胡氏子學孟子而有得者，故曰：「仁心立政之本，均田為政之先。」蓋仁政必自經界始，亦孟子之說也。
吾嘗觀之天地矣。乾以易知，坤以簡能，生生化□，無所止息，天地之大政也。震之出也，巽之齊□也，離之相見也，兌之說也，其盛也。顧於一陽之復也，乃曰見天地之心焉。何也？見天地之仁也。苟於復也，不能含蓄醞釀，俾生意滋息於專一翕聚之中，則亦安能鼓舞和氣，囿天下之物而化生之乎？故曰：「復，其見天地之心乎！」
聖人者，法天者也，則其仁可知矣，政可知矣。旣嘗制禮以一天下矣，作樂以和天下矣，明刑以齊天下矣，立政以導天下矣，田不井而均之，則無以定分，無以安業，無以平賦，無以制變。雖有禮樂刑
translation_en:
…Why is this? Benevolence is the heart we receive from Heaven and Earth. With a heart that cannot bear the suffering of others comes government that cannot bear their suffering. Thus rites, music, punishments, and administration—the means of ordering conditions throughout the realm and bringing its people's feelings into mutual understanding—all extend this heart that cannot bear the suffering of the people. Otherwise, action would have no foundation and governance no instruments: how could they reach throughout the realm? Mencius said: “Goodness alone is insufficient for government; laws alone cannot put themselves into effect.” Master Hu studied Mencius and gained an understanding of his teaching. Hence he said: “A benevolent heart is the foundation of establishing government; equitable distribution of land is the first priority in governing.” That benevolent government must begin with demarcating field boundaries is also a teaching of Mencius.
I have observed this in Heaven and Earth. Qian exercises its direction through ease, and Kun exercises its capacity through simplicity. Ceaseless generation and transformation [?], never coming to rest, constitute the great governance of Heaven and Earth. Coming forth in Zhen, being brought into order [?] in Xun, becoming visible to one another in Li, and rejoicing in Dui represent its flourishing. Yet it is precisely at the return of a single yang line that we are said to see the heart of Heaven and Earth. Why? Because we see their benevolence. If, at this return, they could not preserve and nurture their potential, allowing the impulse of life to grow within a concentrated unity, how could they stir the harmonious vital force, embrace all things under Heaven, and transform and generate them? Hence the saying: “In Return, do we not see the heart of Heaven and Earth!”
The sage takes Heaven as his model; thus his benevolence can be understood, and his government can be understood. He has instituted rites to unify the realm, created music to harmonize it, clarified punishments to bring it into order, and established government to guide it. Yet unless the fields are arranged under the well-field system and equitably distributed, there is no means to settle allotted shares, secure livelihoods, equalize taxation, or control unforeseen disturbances. Even with rites, music, and punishments…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
政將安施乎聖人愛物之仁亦幾乎息矣是故
聖人知事之難周者莫重乎田而民之難給者
莫重乎食事難周則天下之勢莫可一食難給
則天下之情莫可通故制以經界定爲井田其
立意也遠其慮患也周其制法也詳是以貴賤
有等豐殺有章車服田宅莫敢踰制而天下之
分定矣人無廢業田無曠土樂生利用莫肯轉
徙而天下之業安矣藏不偏多故物無偏罄用
不偏厚故人不偏窮無求於力分之外無貸於
===
力分之內務穡無增稅輟稼無減租而天下之
賦平矣伍兩有法車徒有制寓兵於農伏險於
順靡課而人自奮弛禁而衆不攜田不屯而食
足戍不更而守固而天下之變弭矣變弭則無
急難賦平則無怨讟業安則無離散分定則無
僭侈由是而制禮五禮可舉也由是而作樂六
樂可興也由是而明刑修政五刑入政無淫慝
也何也有恒產而有恒心故也不然分之不定
則曰民之悖戾業之不安則曰民之□亡賦□
punctuated: 政，將安施乎？聖人愛物之仁亦幾乎息矣。是故聖人知事之難周者，莫重乎田；而民之難給者，莫重乎食。事難周，則天下之勢莫可一；食難給，則天下之情莫可通。故制以經界，定爲井田。其立意也遠，其慮患也周，其制法也詳。是以貴賤有等，豐殺有章，車服田宅莫敢踰制，而天下之分定矣。人無廢業，田無曠土，樂生利用，莫肯轉徙，而天下之業安矣。藏不偏多，故物無偏罄；用不偏厚，故人不偏窮。無求於力分之外，無貸於力分之內。務穡無增稅，輟稼無減租，而天下之賦平矣。伍兩有法，車徒有制，寓兵於農，伏險於順。靡課而人自奮，弛禁而衆不攜，田不屯而食足，戍不更而守固，而天下之變弭矣。變弭則無急難，賦平則無怨讟，業安則無離散，分定則無僭侈。由是而制禮，五禮可舉也；由是而作樂，六樂可興也；由是而明刑修政，五刑入政無淫慝也。何也？有恒產而有恒心故也。不然，分之不定，則曰民之悖戾；業之不安，則曰民之□亡；賦□
translation_en:
…and government—how could these be put into practice? The sage’s benevolence in caring for all things would come close to extinction. Thus the sage knew that, among affairs difficult to arrange comprehensively, none was more important than land, and that, among the people’s needs difficult to supply adequately, none was more important than food. If affairs could not be comprehensively arranged, the realm could not be unified; if food could not be adequately supplied, the feelings of people throughout the realm could not be brought into harmony. He therefore regulated land through boundary demarcation and established the well-field system. His purpose was far-reaching, his anticipation of troubles comprehensive, and his regulations detailed.

Consequently, the noble and the humble had their respective ranks, and abundance and restraint followed prescribed rules. None dared exceed the regulations for carriages, dress, fields, and dwellings, and the distinctions throughout the realm were settled. No one abandoned an occupation, and no fields lay waste. People enjoyed life and made beneficial use of resources; none wished to move away, and livelihoods throughout the realm were secure. Stores were not disproportionately abundant in some places, so supplies were not disproportionately exhausted in others. Expenditure was not disproportionately lavish for some, so poverty did not fall disproportionately upon others. Nothing was demanded beyond people’s capacities and allotted obligations, and nothing within those capacities and obligations was remitted. Diligent cultivation brought no increase in taxes; abandoning cultivation brought no reduction in rent. Thus taxation throughout the realm was equitable.

Military units of five and twenty-five had their rules, and chariots and infantry their regulations. Soldiers were incorporated into the farming population, and defensive strength lay concealed within peaceful order. Without being pressed, people exerted themselves; with prohibitions relaxed, the populace did not disperse. Without military agricultural colonies, food was sufficient; without rotating garrison service, defenses were secure. Thus disturbances throughout the realm were quelled. With disturbances quelled, there were no emergencies; with taxation equitable, there were no bitter complaints; with livelihoods secure, there was no dispersal of the people; with distinctions settled, there was no presumptuous extravagance. On this basis, rites could be instituted and the five categories of ritual put into practice; music could be created and the six ceremonial musical performances revived; punishments could be clarified and government put in order, so that the five punishments entered government [?], with no excess or wrongdoing. Why was this? Because those with a constant livelihood have a constant heart.

Otherwise, when distinctions are unsettled, one says that the people are unruly; when livelihoods are insecure, one says that the people [illegible] flee [?]; when taxation [illegible]…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
不平則曰民之游惰變之不弭則曰民之兇獷
其如政焉何哉昔夏后氏五十而貢殷人七十
而助周人百畝而徹其興也勃焉秦開阡陌壞
溝洫先王之政殘之殆盡秦亦與之俱焉無他
心之仁不仁田之均不均耳此可以究立政之
本矣雖然三代遠矣井田不可復矣則斯民終
不被其澤而聖人之仁將湮鬱乎得井田之意
通其變不失其宜師其意不泥其法亦惟人君
有是心耳故孟子曰堯舜之道不以仁政不能
===
平治天下蓋仁政者爲治之本也而仁心者又
爲政之本也人君求所以端其本則天下治矣

不平，則曰民之游惰；變之不弭，則曰民之兇獷。其如政焉何哉？昔夏后氏五十而貢，殷人七十而助，周人百畝而徹，其興也勃焉。秦開阡陌，壞溝洫，先王之政殘之殆盡，秦亦與之俱焉。無他，心之仁不仁，田之均不均耳。此可以究立政之本矣。雖然，三代遠矣，井田不可復矣，則斯民終不被其澤，而聖人之仁將湮鬱乎？得井田之意，通其變，不失其宜，師其意，不泥其法，亦惟人君有是心耳。故孟子曰：「堯舜之道，不以仁政，不能平治天下。」蓋仁政者，爲治之本也，而仁心者，又爲政之本也。人君求所以端其本，則天下治矣。

translation_en:
…is inequitable, they say that the people are idle and indolent; when disturbances are not quelled, they say that the people are fierce and unruly. What can such an approach accomplish in government? Formerly, the Xia rulers allotted fifty mu and levied tribute; the Yin allotted seventy and required assistance in cultivating public land; the Zhou allotted one hundred mu and employed the che levy. Their rise was vigorous. Qin opened up the field boundaries and destroyed the irrigation channels, nearly obliterating the government of the former kings; Qin itself perished along with it. There was no other cause: it was simply a matter of whether the ruler’s heart was benevolent and whether the fields were equitably distributed. Here one may discern the foundation for establishing government.
Nevertheless, the Three Dynasties are long past, and the well-field system cannot be restored. Must the people therefore never receive its benefits, and must the sages’ benevolence remain obscured and unrealized? Grasp the intent of the well-field system, adapt it to changing circumstances without losing what is appropriate, and emulate its intent without adhering rigidly to its rules: this depends solely upon the ruler’s possessing such a heart. Thus Mencius said: “Even with the Way of Yao and Shun, without benevolent government one cannot bring peace and order to the realm.” Benevolent government is the foundation of good rule, and a benevolent heart is, in turn, the foundation of government. If the ruler seeks the means to set this foundation right, the realm will be well governed.
Memorial

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
正味左右莫匪正人和在軾鑾在衡出入
必由善道以迨師保疑丞之設孰非溫文
恭敬之規蓋將居正以體元莫大因心而
立教事存四學道在六經肆秦漢唐宋之
迭興雜黃老申韓而竝用贄詩工誦豈曰
能賢秋禮冬書未聞翼善居肅成而講藝
何裨以海之深開博望以延賢無益搓山
之峻事如有待道不虛行茲蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
===
聖敬日躋
聰明時乂
繼
天立極洽燉化於登三
明物察倫煥鴻猷於邁五
闡制事制心之秘
貽克勤克儉之謨謂
天生下民作之君每數言而彝訓然
又有天下傳之子必教諭而□□成□□□憲其無
punctuated: 正味，左右莫匪正人；和在軾，鑾在衡，出入必由善道。以迨師保疑丞之設，孰非溫文恭敬之規？蓋將居正以體元，莫大因心而立教。事存四學，道在六經。肆秦漢唐宋之迭興，雜黃老申韓而竝用。贄詩工誦，豈曰能賢？秋禮冬書，未聞翼善。居肅成而講藝，何裨以海之深？開博望以延賢，無益搓山之峻。事如有待，道不虛行。茲蓋伏遇皇帝陛下，聖敬日躋，聰明時乂，繼天立極，洽燉化於登三；明物察倫，煥鴻猷於邁五。闡制事制心之秘，貽克勤克儉之謨。謂「天生下民，作之君」，每數言而彝訓然；又有天下，傳之子，必教諭而□□成□□□憲其無
translation_en:
…regulated the flavors; those on either side were all upright men. With the he bell at the carriage’s front rail and the luan bells on its crossbar, every departure and return followed the proper way. And when it came to establishing grand preceptors, grand guardians, grand councillors, and grand assistants, which of these arrangements did not prescribe gentleness, refinement, reverence, and respect? Their purpose was to dwell in rectitude and embody the primal good; nothing was greater than establishing instruction grounded in the heart. Its practices resided in the four schools, and its Way in the Six Classics. Then Qin, Han, Tang, and Song rose in succession, employing a mixture of the teachings of Huang-Lao and Shen Buhai and Han Fei. Presenting poems and having musicians recite them—could this be called making someone worthy? Studying rites in autumn and documents in winter—we have not heard that this fostered goodness. Lecturing on the arts in Sucheng Hall—how did this contribute to an ocean’s depth [?]? Opening the Bowang establishment to invite worthy men did nothing to augment a mountain’s height [?]. These undertakings seemed to await their proper moment; the Way does not take effect unaided.

Now we have reverently encountered Your Majesty the Emperor, whose sagely reverence increases daily and whose perceptiveness brings timely order. Succeeding Heaven and establishing the supreme standard, you spread your profound transforming influence, rising to the rank of the Three Sovereigns; discerning things and examining human relationships, you display your magnificent designs, surpassing the Five Emperors. You elucidate the hidden principles of regulating affairs and governing the heart, and bequeath counsels of diligence and frugality. You say, “Heaven gives birth to the common people and appoints rulers for them”; every few words have the character of enduring instruction. Moreover, possessing All under Heaven and transmitting it to a son necessarily requires teaching and admonition, so that … may be accomplished … [five illegible characters; the following phrase, 憲其無, is incomplete and uncertain: ?]…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
徳主器莫大乎震學古訓迺有獲養正蓋
取諸蒙羣言灝噩而難窺
聖學精微而有要頃及
萬幾之暇爰暨
乙夜之觀本堯舜精一之言及聖賢經傳之
旨事兼作述義切箴規或專言以示倫或
統言而撮要父父子子皆聚此書君君臣
臣同歸于道語勤學則尊師重傳論法
祖則敬
天勤民蓋敎諭之方旣以孝仁禮義爲本而條
目之細至於容貌詞氣之微見諸事深切
著明加之意高明廣大規模遠矣上同文
王世子之篇法戒昭然下陋唐宗帝範之
賜刻之琬琰適隆
燕翼之謀

龍頷俯窺
punctuated: 徳。主器莫大乎震，學古訓迺有獲，養正蓋取諸蒙。羣言灝噩而難窺，聖學精微而有要。頃及萬幾之暇，爰暨乙夜之觀，本堯舜精一之言及聖賢經傳之旨，事兼作述，義切箴規。或專言以示倫，或統言而撮要。父父子子，皆聚此書；君君臣臣，同歸于道。語勤學則尊師重傳，論法祖則敬天勤民。蓋敎諭之方，旣以孝仁禮義爲本，而條目之細，至於容貌詞氣之微。見諸事，深切著明；加之意，高明廣大。規模遠矣，上同《文王世子》之篇；法戒昭然，下陋唐宗《帝範》之賜。刻之琬琰，適隆燕翼之謀；予及臣工，用廣鴻仁之霈。至如踈陋，亦與龍頷，俯窺
translation_en: …virtue. For presiding over the sacred vessels, nothing is greater than Zhen, the hexagram of the eldest son; studying ancient teachings brings attainment, and nurturing rectitude takes its principle from Meng, the hexagram of youthful ignorance. The collected teachings are vast and profound, difficult to fathom; yet sagely learning, subtle and refined, has its essentials. Recently, in the leisure afforded by Your Majesty’s myriad affairs and during your reading in the second watch of the night, you drew upon Yao and Shun’s words concerning refinement and single-mindedness, together with the purport of the sages’ and worthies’ classics and commentaries. Your work combines original composition with transmission, its meaning closely directed toward admonition and guidance. Some passages address particular matters to illuminate human relationships; others speak comprehensively to gather together the essentials. Fathers acting as fathers and sons as sons—all are brought together in this book; rulers acting as rulers and ministers as ministers—all return together to the Way. In speaking of diligent study, it honors teachers and values transmitted teachings; in discussing emulation of the ancestors, it urges reverence for Heaven and diligent care for the people. Its method of instruction takes filial piety, benevolence, ritual propriety, and righteousness as its foundation, while its detailed provisions extend even to the subtleties of appearance, speech, and manner. Applied to affairs, it is penetrating and lucid; in its intentions, lofty and expansive. Far-reaching in scope, it matches the ancient chapter “King Wen as Crown Prince”; clear in its models and admonitions, it leaves far below it the later example of the Tang emperor’s bestowal of the “Model for Emperors” (Di fan). Engraving it upon fine jade fittingly enhances your plans to secure the welfare of your descendants; bestowing it upon your officials extends the abundant outpouring of your great benevolence. title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
金鐀之閟嚴仰見
瑤編之易簡如游河洛重披龍馬之祥若在
唐虞親聞授受之語
帝澤沃江河之潤
天文爛奎璧之輝喜溢縉紳光生蔀屋此
熙朝之盛事爲儒者之極榮臣廣等深惟保
傳以無功重拜
綵綸於有奕
慶雲豐惠雖不遺葑菲之微爵火餘明亦何
===
日星之耀自兹以往益勵厥初尊所聞行所知
補
期不負於
教育道於前承於後庶仰答於涓埃伏願
愼迺永圖
克昌厥後
惇德允元而蠻夷服
本支延百世之長
家齊國治而天下平
punctuated:
金鐀之閟嚴，仰見瑤編之易簡，如游河洛，重披龍馬之祥；若在唐虞，親聞授受之語。帝澤沃江河之潤，天文爛奎璧之輝。喜溢縉紳，光生蔀屋。此熙朝之盛事，爲儒者之極榮。臣廣等深惟保傳以無功，重拜綵綸於有奕。慶雲豐惠，雖不遺葑菲之微；爵火餘明，亦何日星之耀？自兹以往，益勵厥初，尊所聞，行所知，補，期不負於教育；道於前，承於後，庶仰答於涓埃。
伏願愼迺永圖，克昌厥後，惇德允元而蠻夷服，本支延百世之長；家齊國治而天下平。
translation_en:
…the solemn seclusion of the golden coffer; looking upward in reverence, we behold the simplicity and accessibility of the precious volume. It is as though we journeyed beside the Yellow and Luo Rivers and once again beheld the auspicious dragon-horse, or stood in the age of Tang Yao and Yu Shun and personally heard their words on transmitting and receiving sovereignty. Imperial beneficence lavishes the moisture of rivers; imperial writings blaze with the brilliance of the Kui and Bi constellations. Joy overflows among officials, and light shines into humble dwellings. This is a splendid event of our flourishing dynasty and the highest honor for scholars. Your servants Guang and the others reflect deeply that, having rendered no meritorious service as tutors [?], we have again reverently received your resplendent silken edict. The abundant bounty of the auspicious clouds neglects not even humble turnips and radishes such as ourselves; yet how could the lingering gleam of a torch [?] compare with the brilliance of the sun and stars? From this time onward, we shall strive still harder to fulfill our original resolve, honor what we have heard, and practice what we know. We shall make good what is lacking [?], hoping not to fail the instruction and nurture we have received. With the Way set forth before us and carried on afterward [?], we hope thereby to repay, by even a drop or a speck, the favor bestowed upon us.
We humbly wish that you exercise care in your enduring plans and bring prosperity to your descendants; that you honor virtue and trust the good, so that the Man and Yi peoples submit, and the main and collateral branches of your house endure for a hundred generations; and that your household be ordered, your state well governed, and all under Heaven at peace…

心也者道之會也道也者文之會也心而
非道則非所以爲心矣文而非心又豈所

宗社衍萬年之盛。臣廣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第一問。
