帝王之學，一本於道；帝王之道，一本於心。心也者，道之會也；道也者，文之會也。心而非道，則非所以爲心矣；文而非心，又豈所
translation_en:
…may the imperial ancestral temples and altars of state enjoy flourishing prosperity for ten thousand years. Your servants Guang and the others, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Majesty, cannot contain our intense emotion and reverent trepidation. We respectfully submit this memorial expressing our thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session: Five Policy Questions.
First Question.
Lei Da.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor: Our emperor is wholly devoted to the learning of the mind [?]. You have been able to expound it, displaying outstanding and genuine insight. Here is someone who has attained an understanding of the Learning of Principle. Let him be selected.
Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: The wording is respectful and circumspect.
Comment by Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: Clear, fluent, and thoroughly integrated.
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Classical and dignified.

The learning of emperors and kings is rooted entirely in the Way; the Way of emperors and kings is rooted entirely in the mind. The mind is where the Way converges; the Way is where literary expression converges. A mind that does not accord with the Way cannot fulfill what makes it a mind. Literary expression that does not proceed from the mind—how could it be that by which…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
以爲文也哉是則帝王之學必以養心爲
主而養心之要必以體道體道爲功養心體道
則帝王之道盡矣若以心術之微用之於
文辭之末則亦藝焉爾已亦豈帝王之學
哉夫嘗求之於伏羲之爻象堯舜之典謨
商周之雅頌矣即其書而論其世即其世
而論其人然其所言之理即其所行之道
唐虞三代之治可以想見其形容也三代
而下漢高帝有三侯之章武帝有秋風之
===
詞唐太宗教子有書宋眞宗尊孔子有贊
宋理宗崇儒有論宏詞雅什渢渢乎非不
可觀與心無補與治無益雜伯雜夷所以
不能復唐虞三代之舊矣洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
帝王之資出於
天授
聖哲之學本於性成有
大誥以諭天下
punctuated:
以爲文也哉？是則帝王之學必以養心爲主，而養心之要必以體道體道爲功。養心體道，則帝王之道盡矣。若以心術之微，用之於文辭之末，則亦藝焉爾已，亦豈帝王之學哉？夫嘗求之於伏羲之爻象、堯舜之典謨、商周之雅頌矣。即其書而論其世，即其世而論其人，然其所言之理，即其所行之道。唐虞三代之治，可以想見其形容也。三代而下，漢高帝有《三侯》之章，武帝有《秋風》之詞，唐太宗教子有書，宋眞宗尊孔子有贊，宋理宗崇儒有論。宏詞雅什，渢渢乎非不可觀，與心無補，與治無益，雜伯雜夷，所以不能復唐虞三代之舊矣。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，帝王之資出於天授，聖哲之學本於性成，有《大誥》以諭天下，
translation_en:
…be regarded as writing? Thus the learning of emperors and kings must take nourishing the mind as its foundation, and the essential work of nourishing the mind must consist in embodying the Way [the transcription repeats “embodying the Way”]. Nourish the mind and embody the Way, and the Way of emperors and kings is fully realized. If the subtle workings of the mind are applied merely to the peripheral concerns of literary expression, this amounts only to an art. How could it be the learning of emperors and kings?
I have sought this in Fuxi’s hexagram lines and images, the Canons and Counsels of Yao and Shun, and the Odes and Hymns of Shang and Zhou. From their writings one considers their age, and from their age one considers the men themselves. The principles they expressed were precisely the Way they practiced. We can thus imagine the character of government under Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties.
After the Three Dynasties, Emperor Gao of Han composed the piece Three Lords [?], and Emperor Wu composed Autumn Wind. Emperor Taizong of Tang wrote to instruct his sons; Emperor Zhenzong of Song composed a eulogy honoring Confucius; and Emperor Lizong of Song composed a discourse exalting Confucian learning. Their grand compositions and elegant verses were richly flowing and certainly worthy of admiration. Yet they did nothing to nourish the mind or benefit government. Their rule mingled hegemonic practices with barbarian ways, and for this reason they could not restore the ancient order of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao received his imperial endowments from Heaven, while his sagely learning was rooted in his innate nature. He issued the Grand Pronouncements to instruct all under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
大祀文幷歌九章以祀
天地神祇有諭高麗西番等國
詔誥見於儒臣劉基宋濂輩所贊述者有曰與
典謨訓誥實相表裏有曰
聖子
神孫俾爲矜式眞與唐虞三代之文一矣其曰
帝王之治莫盛於堯舜觀其授受其要在執
厥中斯義也其得堯舜之心傳矣乎迨我
□上欽承
===
統丕著
鴻猷
祖德有詩繼
宣宗章皇帝
御製而作也
繼述之志可以感孚
天地矣
大狩龍飛有錄展謁
顯陵而作也
punctuated: 大祀文幷歌九章，以祀天地神祇；有諭高麗、西番等國詔誥。見於儒臣劉基、宋濂輩所贊述者，有曰：「與典謨訓誥實相表裏。」有曰：「聖子神孫，俾爲矜式。」眞與唐虞三代之文一矣。其曰：「帝王之治，莫盛於堯舜。觀其授受，其要在執厥中。」斯義也，其得堯舜之心傳矣乎！迨我□上欽承統，丕著鴻猷。《祖德》有詩，繼宣宗章皇帝御製而作也；繼述之志，可以感孚天地矣。《大狩龍飛》有錄，展謁顯陵而作也。
translation_en:
…a text for the Great Sacrifice, together with nine hymns, for sacrificing to Heaven, Earth, and the spirits; and edicts and proclamations addressed to Gaoli, Xifan, and other countries. Among the commendations written by the Confucian officials Liu Ji, Song Lian, and others, one says: “They are indeed complementary to the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements.” Another says: “Let his sagely sons and divine grandsons take them as their model.” Truly, these writings are at one with those of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. He said: “Among the reigns of emperors and kings, none surpassed those of Yao and Shun. Examining their transmission and reception of sovereignty, its essential principle lay in holding fast to the Mean.” Does not this principle show that he grasped the teaching transmitted from the minds of Yao and Shun?
Coming to our present sovereign [?], who reverently inherited the imperial succession and splendidly manifested his grand designs: there is the poem Ancestral Virtue, composed in continuation of an imperial composition by Emperor Xuanzong Zhang. His resolve to carry forward his predecessor’s work can move Heaven and Earth and win their trust. There is also the Record of the Great Hunt and the Dragon’s Ascent [?], composed on the occasion of his visit to pay respects at Xianling.

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
仁孝之誠可以對越
神明矣
穀祇蠶壇有賦則
敬天勤民之本也非無逸七月之心乎
敬一有箴則脩巳治人之實也非洪範典謨
之旨乎眞與
聖祖之文一矣其曰
皇極建其中王道弘正直又曰惟敬惟一畏天
敬民斯義也其得
===
祖之心傳矣乎其視漢唐宋諸作殆亦騷人
韻士焉耳其可以並觀乎哉是則天道弗
已吾心之道亦弗巳易有大極書有執中
詩有敬止皆此義也有巳則與天有間而
去道也遠矣詩曰小心翼翼昭事上帝又
曰勉勉我王綱紀四方此文王之所以為
文也愚也需育化澤久矣敢以此義而為
當宁獻焉
第二問
punctuated:
仁孝之誠，可以對越神明矣。穀祇蠶壇有賦，則敬天勤民之本也，非《無逸》《七月》之心乎？敬一有箴，則脩巳治人之實也，非《洪範》《典謨》之旨乎？眞與聖祖之文一矣。其曰：「皇極建其中，王道弘正直。」又曰：「惟敬惟一，畏天敬民。」斯義也，其得祖之心傳矣乎！其視漢唐宋諸作，殆亦騷人韻士焉耳，其可以並觀乎哉？是則天道弗已，吾心之道亦弗巳。《易》有大極，《書》有執中，《詩》有敬止，皆此義也。有巳，則與天有間，而去道也遠矣。《詩》曰：「小心翼翼，昭事上帝。」又曰：「勉勉我王，綱紀四方。」此文王之所以為文也。愚也需育化澤久矣，敢以此義而為當宁獻焉。

第二問
translation_en:
…The sincerity of his benevolence and filial devotion enables him to stand worthily before the divine powers. His rhapsodies on the grain and earth deities and the Silkworm Altar [?] express the foundation of revering Heaven and diligently caring for the people. Is this not the spirit of “Against Ease” and “The Seventh Month”? His admonition on “Reverence and Unity” expresses the substance of cultivating oneself and governing others. Is this not the purport of “The Great Plan” and the “Canons and Counsels”? His writings are truly at one with those of the sagely ancestor. He says: “The august standard establishes the mean; the kingly Way extends uprightness.” And again: “Be reverent, be single-minded; stand in awe of Heaven and respect the people.” In this principle, has he not received the transmission of his ancestor’s mind? Viewed against his writings, the various compositions of the Han, Tang, and Song seem merely the work of poets and masters of rhyme. How could they be considered on equal terms?

Thus, the Way of Heaven never ceases, and the Way within our minds likewise never ceases. The Book of Changes speaks of the Supreme Ultimate; the Book of Documents, of holding fast to the mean; and the Book of Poetry, of abiding in reverence. All express this principle. If there is any cessation, a gap opens between oneself and Heaven, and one becomes far removed from the Way. The Book of Poetry says: “With care and reverence, he illustriously served the Lord on High.” It also says: “Diligently our king orders and regulates the four quarters.” This is why King Wen was called Wen, “the Cultured.” Foolish though I am, I have long been nurtured [?] by the beneficence of imperial transformation. I venture to offer this principle to Your Majesty.

Second Policy Question

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
雷賀
同考試官教諭陳　批〔修明禮樂已有〕
〔成典而子欲爲樂經以與禮經並行推究本原深得〕
聖人制作之意可見知本之學矣
同考試官教諭毛　批〔修補樂經〕
考試官訓導許　批〔禮樂之旨此作發明殆盡〕
〔今日首務此作能言其意殆有得於治道者〕
〔足見所學〕
考試官教諭周　批〔純雅〕
===
治天下有道本乎人心而已矣治人心有
道本乎禮樂而已矣何也人生而靜天之
性也感物而動性之欲也而其主之者心
也不有禮樂以爲之制則蕩然靡然將有
無所止極者矣天下何從而治邪故聖人
緣人情以制禮樂蓋所以立其本也記曰
樂者天地之和也禮者天地之序也禮樂
之道蓋通乎天地而繫乎人心者也禮樂
明備則天地斯可以官矣否則此心不存
punctuated:
雷賀

同考試官教諭陳　批〔修明禮樂，已有〕〔成典，而子欲爲樂經，以與禮經並行，推究本原，深得〕聖人制作之意，可見知本之學矣。

同考試官教諭毛　批〔修補樂經。〕

考試官訓導許　批〔禮樂之旨，此作發明殆盡。〕〔今日首務，此作能言其意，殆有得於治道者。〕〔足見所學。〕

考試官教諭周　批〔純雅。〕

治天下有道，本乎人心而已矣；治人心有道，本乎禮樂而已矣。何也？人生而靜，天之性也；感物而動，性之欲也。而其主之者，心也。不有禮樂以爲之制，則蕩然靡然，將有無所止極者矣，天下何從而治邪？故聖人緣人情以制禮樂，蓋所以立其本也。《記》曰：「樂者，天地之和也；禮者，天地之序也。」禮樂之道，蓋通乎天地而繫乎人心者也。禮樂明備，則天地斯可以官矣；否則，此心不存
translation_en:
Lei He 雷賀

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “There are already established canons for clarifying and perfecting rites and music. Yet you wish to compile a Classic of Music to circulate alongside the Classic of Rites. In investigating their foundations and origins, you have deeply grasped the sages’ intentions in creating these institutions. This shows learning that understands the fundamentals.”

Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: “Restoring and supplementing the Classic of Music.”

Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This composition elucidates the purport of rites and music almost exhaustively. It articulates the meaning of the foremost task of the present day, suggesting that its author has attained some understanding of the Way of government. It amply demonstrates his learning.”

Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “Pure and elegant.”

There is a Way to govern all under Heaven: it is rooted simply in the human heart. There is a Way to govern the human heart: it is rooted simply in rites and music. Why is this? That people are still at birth belongs to their Heaven-given nature; that they are moved upon contact with things belongs to the desires of that nature. What presides over these is the heart. Without rites and music to regulate it, the heart will become unrestrained and dissipated, potentially knowing neither bounds nor limits. How, then, could all under Heaven be governed? Thus the sages fashioned rites and music in accordance with human feelings, thereby establishing the foundation.

The Record of Rites says: “Music is the harmony of Heaven and Earth; rites are the order of Heaven and Earth.” The Way of rites and music thus extends through Heaven and Earth and is bound to the human heart. When rites and music are clearly established and fully provided, Heaven and Earth can then be brought under ordered governance. Otherwise, this heart will not be preserved …

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
此理亦從泯沒沒聖人之道亦幾乎熄
矣樂焉何足以配天而禮焉何足以配地
耶五禮六樂之作肇自唐虞皆與人心以
爲之主也三綱五常禮之大體三代因之
而不能變以至於樂則亦兼統而用之周
禮大司徒非不有私於大武而必與六樂
同之蓋不容有所去取於其間矣漢高帝
有叔孫禮唐太宗有貞觀禮宋太祖有建
隆禮而天下未底於中正豈叔孫魏徵之
===
徒未得其人亦當時之治有未辨而禮有
未具焉者邪漢惠帝有安世樂唐高祖有
雅樂宋仁宗有大安樂而天下未協於和
平豈祖孝孫和峴之輩未得其人亦當時
之功有未大而樂有未備焉者邪洪惟我
太祖高皇帝以
聖人之德在
天子之位
命牛諒制禮陶凱典樂復唐虞三代之舊以爲
punctuated: 此理亦從泯沒沒，聖人之道亦幾乎熄矣。樂焉何足以配天，而禮焉何足以配地耶？五禮六樂之作，肇自唐虞，皆與人心以爲之主也。三綱五常，禮之大體，三代因之而不能變。以至於樂，則亦兼統而用之。《周禮》大司徒，非不有私於大武，而必與六樂同之，蓋不容有所去取於其間矣。漢高帝有叔孫禮，唐太宗有貞觀禮，宋太祖有建隆禮，而天下未底於中正，豈叔孫、魏徵之徒未得其人，亦當時之治有未辨而禮有未具焉者邪？漢惠帝有安世樂，唐高祖有雅樂，宋仁宗有大安樂，而天下未協於和平，豈祖孝孫、和峴之輩未得其人，亦當時之功有未大而樂有未備焉者邪？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，以聖人之德在天子之位，命牛諒制禮，陶凱典樂，復唐虞三代之舊，以爲
translation_en:
…this principle likewise sinks into oblivion [the transcription repeats 沒, ?], and the Way of the sages comes close to extinction. How, then, could music be worthy to match Heaven, or ritual worthy to match Earth? The creation of the five categories of rites and the six musical traditions began in the ages of Tang and Yu; all took the human heart as their governing basis [?]. The Three Bonds and Five Constants constitute the fundamental structure of ritual. The Three Dynasties followed them and could not alter them. As for music, they likewise brought the inherited traditions together and employed them all. In the Rites of Zhou, the Minister of Education was not without a preference for the Great Martial Dance (Dawu), yet necessarily accorded it the same treatment as the six musical traditions: there could be no selecting some and discarding others among them.

Emperor Gao of Han had the rites of Shusun; Emperor Taizong of Tang had the Zhenguan rites; and Emperor Taizu of Song had the Jianlong rites. Yet the realm did not attain centrality and correctness. Was this because men such as Shusun and Wei Zheng were not the right men for the task? Or was the government of their times still insufficiently ordered [?], and their ritual institutions still incomplete? Emperor Hui of Han had the Music for Pacifying the Age (Anshi); Emperor Gaozu of Tang had Elegant Music (Yayue); and Emperor Renzong of Song had the Music of Great Peace (Da’an). Yet the realm did not achieve harmony and peace. Was this because men such as Zu Xiaosun and He Xian were not the right men for the task? Or were the achievements of their times not yet great enough, and their music not yet fully developed?

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao, possessing the virtue of a sage and occupying the position of the Son of Heaven, commanded Niu Liang to establish the rites and Tao Kai to take charge of music. He restored the ancient institutions of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, to make them…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
一代之典真
大聖人之所作爲矣迨我
皇上建中和之極懋中興之業修著
大明集禮
郊
廟之祀朝會之儀縣邑里社飲酒讀律之法朝
貢
親征遣將之制以至於弔賻喪儀罔不俱載鍾
律則有律原律數中聲子聲之類雅樂則
===
有樂制樂舞樂歌樂章之說以至俗樂罔
不畢舉是眞可以官天地協陰陽定上下
和神人者矣然天下之人散處於閭閻里
巷之下
聖人制作未得以覩其全書日用之間莫不用
禮而禮或失之於有慝莫不用樂而樂或
失之於有淫則亦何所適從哉是故禮樂
二經不可偏廢禮已備矣而樂經猶有所
未修爲治之道是誠有所未盡者矣然欲
punctuated: 一代之典，真大聖人之所作爲矣！迨我皇上建中和之極，懋中興之業，修著《大明集禮》，郊廟之祀、朝會之儀、縣邑里社飲酒讀律之法、朝貢親征遣將之制，以至於弔賻喪儀，罔不俱載。鍾律則有律原、律數、中聲、子聲之類；雅樂則有樂制、樂舞、樂歌、樂章之說，以至俗樂，罔不畢舉。是眞可以官天地、協陰陽、定上下、和神人者矣！然天下之人散處於閭閻里巷之下，聖人制作，未得以覩其全書。日用之間，莫不用禮，而禮或失之於有慝；莫不用樂，而樂或失之於有淫，則亦何所適從哉？是故禮樂二經不可偏廢。禮已備矣，而樂經猶有所未修，爲治之道，是誠有所未盡者矣。然欲
translation_en:
…the canonical institutions of a dynasty: truly the work of a great sage! When our Emperor established the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony and advanced the enterprise of dynastic renewal, he compiled the Collected Rites of the Great Ming. It records everything: sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temples; ceremonies of court audiences and assemblies; rules for communal drinking ceremonies and readings of the laws in counties, towns, and village communities; regulations for tribute audiences, personal military expeditions by the emperor, and the dispatch of generals; and even condolences, contributions toward funeral expenses, and mourning ceremonies. On bell tuning and pitch standards, it includes such topics as the origins of pitch standards, their numerical relationships, fundamental tones, and octave tones. On ceremonial music, it discusses musical institutions, dances, songs, and compositions; even popular music is comprehensively included. These truly provide the means to order Heaven and Earth, harmonize yin and yang, establish the ranks of superior and inferior, and bring spirits and humans into concord!

Yet the people throughout the realm, scattered among villages and lanes, have not been able to see the complete text of the sage’s institutional creations. In daily life, everyone employs ritual, yet ritual sometimes goes astray through perversity; everyone employs music, yet music sometimes goes astray through excess. What, then, are they to follow? Thus neither of the two classics, of ritual and of music, may be neglected. Ritual is already fully provided for, but the Classic of Music still awaits compilation: in the way of governing, something indeed remains unfulfilled. Yet if one wishes to…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
考黃鍾員徑之法裁五聲六律之變參變
宮變徵之宜審變律半聲之例各極其妙
以定律呂則當本之於
大明集禮合之於禮記以肇其端參之以古人
成法以窮其變采之以先儒格言以致其
詳作爲樂經一書以補六經之缺與禮經
並行於天下使天下之人士傳其義人守
其法父子兄弟夫婦莫不和親長幼朋友
莫不和順如此則政化大行風俗淳美而
===
禮樂達於天下矣嗟夫斯民也與三代之
民一也其心未嘗不同而禮樂之制何其
不同有如是哉蓋三代而上治出於一而
禮樂達於天下三代而下治出於二而禮
樂爲虛文故也人心豈有未一者乎寥寥
千古良有慨嘆幸有
聖天子在上敢不悉心以究乎禮樂之說焉
第三問
陳炌
punctuated:
考黃鍾員徑之法，裁五聲六律之變，參變宮變徵之宜，審變律半聲之例，各極其妙，以定律呂，則當本之於《大明集禮》，合之於《禮記》，以肇其端；參之以古人成法，以窮其變；采之以先儒格言，以致其詳。作爲《樂經》一書，以補六經之缺，與《禮經》並行於天下，使天下之人士傳其義，人守其法，父子兄弟夫婦莫不和親，長幼朋友莫不和順。如此，則政化大行，風俗淳美，而禮樂達於天下矣。嗟夫！斯民也，與三代之民一也，其心未嘗不同，而禮樂之制何其不同有如是哉？蓋三代而上，治出於一，而禮樂達於天下；三代而下，治出於二，而禮樂爲虛文故也。人心豈有未一者乎？寥寥千古，良有慨嘆！幸有聖天子在上，敢不悉心以究乎禮樂之說焉？
第三問
陳炌
translation_en:
…to investigate the rules for the circumference and diameter of the Huangzhong pitch pipe, determine the variations of the five notes and six pitch standards, consider the appropriate use of the altered gong and altered zhi notes, and examine the precedents for altered pitch standards and half-tones, bringing each to its utmost refinement so as to establish the pitch standards, one should take the Collected Rites of the Great Ming as the foundation and bring it into accord with the Record of Rites to lay the groundwork. One should consult the established methods of the ancients to explore all their variations, and draw upon the authoritative sayings of earlier Confucian scholars to provide full detail. A Classic of Music should thus be compiled to fill the gap among the Six Classics and circulate throughout the realm alongside the Classic of Rites. This would enable the scholars of the realm to transmit its meaning and everyone to observe its rules, so that fathers and sons, elder and younger brothers, and husbands and wives would all live in harmony and affection, and elders and juniors and friends would all live in concord. In this way, government and moral transformation would flourish, customs would become sincere and fine, and rites and music would prevail throughout the realm.
Alas! The people of today are the same as the people of the Three Dynasties. Their hearts have never been different; how, then, can their institutions of rites and music differ so greatly? It is because in the Three Dynasties and earlier, government issued from a single source and rites and music prevailed throughout the realm, whereas after the Three Dynasties, government issued from two sources and rites and music became empty forms. How could human hearts ever have lacked this unity? Across the long, desolate ages, there is indeed much to lament! Fortunately, we have a sagely Son of Heaven above us. Dare we fail to devote our whole minds to investigating the teachings of rites and music?
Third Question
Chen Kai

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導彭　批　〔誠偽公私之辨最切爲吏者心術聞斯言者可以興矣〕
同考試官學正王　批　〔爾雅渾厚宛然漢作子其工古文辭者邪〕
同考試官學正羅　批　〔博聞彊記篤志力行之學讀此作可以見矣敬羨敬羨〕
考試官訓導許　批　〔敷陳條荅曲盡其妙可録〕
考試官教諭周　批　〔是知尚友古人者〕
古之吏民者純心以爲民故功烈施於當
===
時聲名垂於後世而亦有以享其祀於無
窮今之吏民者虛文以自爲故名立而隳
亦隨之亦有名未立而輙以敗者此其故
何哉誠偽之所繇分而公私之辨也執事
發策以古人之治江西績效顯著隆載祀
典者爲問其所以開尚友之志而致意於
郡縣之治其憂勤可知已愚謹按祭法曰
法施於民則祀之以死勤事則祀之以勞
定國則祀之能禦大災則祀之能捍大患
punctuated:
同考試官訓導彭批〔誠偽公私之辨，最切爲吏者心術。聞斯言者，可以興矣。〕
同考試官學正王批〔爾雅渾厚，宛然漢作。子其工古文辭者邪？〕
同考試官學正羅批〔博聞彊記，篤志力行之學，讀此作可以見矣。敬羨，敬羨！〕
考試官訓導許批〔敷陳條荅，曲盡其妙，可録。〕
考試官教諭周批〔是知尚友古人者。〕
古之吏民者，純心以爲民，故功烈施於當時，聲名垂於後世，而亦有以享其祀於無窮。今之吏民者，虛文以自爲，故名立而隳亦隨之，亦有名未立而輙以敗者。此其故何哉？誠偽之所繇分，而公私之辨也。執事發策，以古人之治江西、績效顯著、隆載祀典者爲問，其所以開尚友之志，而致意於郡縣之治，其憂勤可知已。愚謹按《祭法》曰：「法施於民則祀之，以死勤事則祀之，以勞定國則祀之，能禦大災則祀之，能捍大患
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Peng, Assistant Instructor: 〔The distinction between sincerity and falsity, and between public and private interests, bears most directly upon the moral disposition of officials. Those who hear these words may be stirred to action.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔Refined, substantial, and rich: this reads just like a Han composition. Are you perhaps an accomplished writer of ancient-style prose?〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor: 〔Learning grounded in wide reading, strong memory, firm resolve, and strenuous practice is evident in this composition. Respect and admiration—respect and admiration!〕
Comment by Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: 〔The exposition and point-by-point responses fully bring out the subtleties. Worthy of selection.〕
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: 〔Here is someone who understands how to take the ancients as friends.〕
Those who governed the people in antiquity served them with an undivided heart. Thus their achievements benefited their own age, their reputations endured in later generations, and they also earned sacrificial offerings in perpetuity. Those who govern the people today use empty formalities to advance their own interests. Thus, once their reputation is established, its ruin follows; some even meet with failure before their reputation is established. Why is this? It lies in the divergence between sincerity and falsity, and the distinction between public and private interests. You, honored examiners, have set a policy question concerning men of antiquity who governed Jiangxi, whose achievements were outstanding, and who were accorded an eminent place in the sacrificial canon. In thereby encouraging the aspiration to take the ancients as friends and directing attention to prefectural and county government, you reveal your diligent concern.
I humbly submit that the “Rules of Sacrifice” states: “Those whose standards benefited the people are to receive sacrifices; those who died in diligent service are to receive sacrifices; those whose labors secured the state are to receive sacrifices; those who could ward off great calamities are to receive sacrifices; those who could avert great afflictions …

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
則祀之聖王之制祭祀而必謹此五者何
哉葢所以端爲吏之趨而示斯民以義之
道也姑自漢以下祀於江右者論之宋叔
庠退奸貪進忠善而虎東渡江其化遠矣
陶士行勤於吏職筆翰如流而匡輔王室
竟以成功其勞著矣夫是有九江之祀房
琯撫宜春而列郡是式建學興禮之功崇
矣韓昌黎刺袁州而其政推之天下計傭
贖隷之法詳矣李德裕爲州長史而奬掖
===
士類不以遷謫介意其大節卓犖矣夫是
有袁之祀狄梁公精忠大節與日月爭光
而奏免民租縱囚歸獄尤繫彭澤之思夫
是有彭澤之祀張曲江危言正論與風霜
俱厲而徜徉子祠禱雨輙應尤繫洪州之
思夫是有南昌之祀顏魯公脩堘築陂溉
田萬頃撫民于今賴之况忠義之素著乎
夫是有撫之祀濂溪周子司理南安洗究
澤物而殺人媚人吾不爲也一言有以奪
punctuated:
則祀之。聖王之制祭祀而必謹此五者，何哉？葢所以端爲吏之趨，而示斯民以義之道也。姑自漢以下祀於江右者論之。
宋叔庠退奸貪，進忠善，而虎東渡江，其化遠矣。陶士行勤於吏職，筆翰如流，而匡輔王室，竟以成功，其勞著矣。夫是有九江之祀。
房琯撫宜春，而列郡是式，建學興禮之功崇矣。韓昌黎刺袁州，而其政推之天下，計傭贖隷之法詳矣。李德裕爲州長史，而奬掖士類，不以遷謫介意，其大節卓犖矣。夫是有袁之祀。
狄梁公精忠大節，與日月爭光，而奏免民租，縱囚歸獄，尤繫彭澤之思。夫是有彭澤之祀。
張曲江危言正論，與風霜俱厲，而徜徉子祠，禱雨輙應，尤繫洪州之思。夫是有南昌之祀。
顏魯公脩堘築陂，溉田萬頃，撫民于今賴之，况忠義之素著乎？夫是有撫之祀。
濂溪周子司理南安，洗究澤物，而「殺人媚人，吾不爲也」，一言有以奪
translation_en:
…then he is to receive sacrifices. Why did the sage kings, in regulating sacrifices, insist on scrupulously observing these five criteria? It was to set officials’ aspirations straight and show the people the way of righteousness. Let us consider those who have received sacrifices in Jiangyou from the Han dynasty onward.
Song Shuxiang dismissed the corrupt and avaricious and advanced the loyal and good; even the tigers crossed the river eastward. Far-reaching indeed was his transforming influence. Tao Shixing diligently performed his official duties, his brush flowing freely; he supported the royal house and ultimately achieved success. Manifest indeed were his meritorious labors. Hence the sacrifices to them in Jiujiang.
Fang Guan governed Yichun so well that the surrounding prefectures took it as their model. Lofty were his achievements in establishing schools and promoting ritual propriety. Han Changli served as prefect of Yuanzhou, and his policies were extended throughout the realm. Detailed were his provisions for reckoning the value of labor to redeem bondservants. Li Deyu served as prefectural secretary-general and encouraged and supported scholars, taking no offense at his demotion and banishment. Outstanding indeed was his integrity. Hence the sacrifices to them in Yuanzhou.
Duke Di of Liang’s pure loyalty and great integrity rivaled the sun and moon in brilliance. His memorial requesting remission of the people’s taxes, and his release of prisoners who subsequently returned to prison, particularly secured his place in the grateful memory of Pengze. Hence the sacrifices to him in Pengze.
Zhang Qujiang’s forthright words and upright arguments were as stern as wind and frost. His lingering at the shrine [?], and the unfailing response to prayers for rain, particularly secured his place in the grateful memory of Hongzhou. Hence the sacrifices to him in Nanchang.
Duke Yan of Lu repaired embankments and built reservoirs, irrigating ten thousand qing of farmland. The people of Fuzhou benefit from these works to this day. How much more deserving was he for his long-established loyalty and righteousness! Hence the sacrifices to him in Fuzhou.
Master Zhou of Lianxi served as prefectural judge in Nan’an, thoroughly investigating cases [?] and extending benefits to others. His declaration, “To kill someone in order to curry favor with another—this I will not do,” was enough, in a single utterance, to quell…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
王迹之氣况得千載不傳之學乎夫是有
南安之祀考亭朱子知南康軍勸學敎民
而下三章約立五賢堂條聖賢爲學大端
有以垂白鹿萬世之規况能集諸儒之大
成乎夫是有南康之祀趙抃守虔則戒諸
縣令使自爲治而改鹽法濂溪石虔以爲
利楊龜山司法于虔則忠信果决而疑獄
立斷虔以爲明夫是有虔之祀沈希顔脩
廢舉墜有功于雩然一錢不取妖禽不敢
===
啼樹矣劉藻興學勸耕亦有功于雩然增
王萬孝義二十四圖民至有割股以救親
者矣夫是有雩之祀范文正公守饒政先
豈弟而歲饑活民以萬計夫是有饒之祀
鍾離瑾令德化守義愛民而緩期輟奮以
嫁前令之女尤爲世所稱夫是有德化之
祀張師亮爲轉運副使奏定歲鑄之楚奏
捐錮送之令而又止旁地出税放縣配歸
農其利博矣張士遜爲轉運使不增羨餘
punctuated: 王迹之氣，况得千載不傳之學乎？夫是有南安之祀。考亭朱子知南康軍，勸學敎民，而下三章約，立五賢堂，條聖賢爲學大端，有以垂白鹿萬世之規，况能集諸儒之大成乎？夫是有南康之祀。趙抃守虔，則戒諸縣令，使自爲治，而改鹽法，濂溪石虔以爲利。楊龜山司法于虔，則忠信果决，而疑獄立斷，虔以爲明。夫是有虔之祀。沈希顔脩廢舉墜，有功于雩，然一錢不取，妖禽不敢啼樹矣。劉藻興學勸耕，亦有功于雩，然增王萬孝義二十四圖，民至有割股以救親者矣。夫是有雩之祀。范文正公守饒，政先豈弟，而歲饑活民以萬計。夫是有饒之祀。鍾離瑾令德化，守義愛民，而緩期輟奮，以嫁前令之女，尤爲世所稱。夫是有德化之祀。張師亮爲轉運副使，奏定歲鑄之楚，奏捐錮送之令，而又止旁地出税，放縣配歸農，其利博矣。張士遜爲轉運使，不增羨餘
translation_en: …the overbearing spirit of Wang Ji [?]—how much more so, then, for having recovered the learning whose transmission had been broken for a thousand years? Hence his worship at Nan’an. Master Zhu of Kaoting, as prefect of Nankang Military Prefecture, encouraged learning and instructed the people. He issued a covenant in three articles, established the Hall of Five Worthies, and set out the principal elements of the sages’ and worthies’ approach to learning, thereby leaving rules for White Deer Grotto Academy for all generations. How much more so, then, for having brought together the great achievements of the Confucian masters? Hence his worship at Nankang. When Zhao Bian governed Qian, he admonished the county magistrates and allowed them to administer their jurisdictions themselves. He also reformed the salt regulations, which benefited Qian [the intervening phrase containing “Lianxi” is garbled: 濂溪石虔]. When Yang Guishan served as judicial officer in Qian, he was loyal, trustworthy, and decisive, settling doubtful cases immediately. The people of Qian considered him discerning. Hence their worship at Qian. Shen Xiyan restored neglected institutions and revived discontinued undertakings, rendering meritorious service at Yu. Yet he would not take a single coin, and even ominous birds dared not cry in the trees. Liu Zao promoted learning and encouraged farming, likewise rendering meritorious service at Yu. He also advanced filial piety and righteousness in the twenty-four tu, or local administrative units [the wording 增王萬孝義 is doubtful]; among the people there were even those who cut flesh from their thighs to save their parents. Hence their worship at Yu. Lord Fan Wenzheng governed Rao, giving precedence to kindness and gentleness in his administration. In a year of famine, he saved tens of thousands of people. Hence his worship at Rao. Zhongli Jin, as magistrate of Dehua, upheld righteousness and cherished the people. He was especially praised by his contemporaries for extending a deadline and suspending an undertaking [?], so that the daughter of the previous magistrate could be married. Hence his worship at Dehua. Zhang Shiliang, as Vice Transport Commissioner, memorialized to establish the annual minting quota [?] and to abolish an order for transport under confinement [?]. He also stopped the levying of taxes on adjoining lands [?] and released those assigned to the counties to return to farming [?]. The benefits he conferred were extensive. Zhang Shixun, as Transport Commissioner, did not increase surplus revenues…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
之利而議者謂其識大體其濟衆矣夫是
有列郡之祀揆之祭法夫何間然哉然數
君子在當時豈有意於民之祀而民祀之
者亦非有以私之也數君子之治純心爲
民而已之利害夷危不計焉則其功德之
在民者遠而流風餘澤猶有以丐被後世
故也仰惟我
聖天子作人弘化屢
渙號申飭郡縣長吏固宜仰承
===
德奮起事功而大江以西未聞有以效今哲
而稱
上意者竊意今之守令能免於拘攣㧀俗循常
習故而廓然爲民深慮者寡也世之吏者
責成於簿書期會之間以爲是大故至於
俗流敗壞而恬不以爲怪一也養禄待遷
僥倖以無罪襲高位寵厚禄自以爲成功
二也竭民之膏血以自媒利取寵一時三
也此三者膠固於中何繇深究民萌以達
punctuated:
之利，而議者謂其識大體，其濟衆矣。夫是有列郡之祀，揆之祭法，夫何間然哉？然數君子在當時，豈有意於民之祀？而民祀之者，亦非有以私之也。數君子之治，純心爲民，而已之利害夷危不計焉，則其功德之在民者遠，而流風餘澤猶有以丐被後世故也。
仰惟我聖天子作人弘化，屢渙號申飭郡縣長吏，固宜仰承德，奮起事功。而大江以西，未聞有以效今哲而稱上意者。竊意今之守令，能免於拘攣㧀俗、循常習故，而廓然爲民深慮者寡也。世之吏者，責成於簿書期會之間，以爲是大故，至於俗流敗壞，而恬不以爲怪，一也；養禄待遷，僥倖以無罪襲高位、寵厚禄，自以爲成功，二也；竭民之膏血，以自媒利，取寵一時，三也。此三者膠固於中，何繇深究民萌以達
translation_en:
…such profits; commentators said that he understood the larger considerations and brought relief to the multitude. Thus these men are worshipped in the various prefectures. Judged by the rules governing sacrifices, what fault could be found with this? Yet did these gentlemen, in their own day, ever intend that the people should worship them? Nor did the people worship them out of personal partiality. In governing, these gentlemen devoted themselves wholeheartedly to the people, taking no account of their own advantage or injury, security or danger. Their achievements and beneficence therefore had an enduring effect upon the people, and their remaining influence and bounty continued to extend to later generations.
We reverently reflect that our sagely Son of Heaven nurtures talent and spreads transforming instruction, repeatedly issuing imperial proclamations to admonish the chief officials of prefectures and counties. They should assuredly receive his virtue with reverence and bestir themselves to accomplish worthy deeds. Yet west of the great river, we have heard of none who emulate the worthy men of today [?] and satisfy His Majesty’s intentions. I venture to think that few present-day prefects and magistrates can escape the constraints of vulgar convention [?] and habitual adherence to established routines, and give broad-minded, profound consideration to the people’s welfare. Officials nowadays demand results only in registers, documents, deadlines, and accounting, regarding these as matters of great importance; when popular customs deteriorate, they remain untroubled and find nothing strange in it. This is the first failing. They live on their salaries while awaiting promotion, hoping by good fortune and a blameless record to attain high office and enjoy generous emoluments, and consider this success. This is the second. They exhaust the people’s lifeblood to secure profit for themselves and win passing favor. This is the third. With these three failings firmly lodged within them, how can they thoroughly investigate the condition of the people and thereby comprehend…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
利害之原哉雖然亦豈無有志之士卓然
不群者然功業卒不逮古何也竊嘗聞之
矣周之卿士各世其家漢郡縣吏皆長子
孫甚以爲姓氏官有定民民有定志故上
易令而下易行也今任吏者率三歲一遷
而或一歲數遷其官矣漢刺史入爲三公
唐制不任州刺史者不得官侍郎不任縣
令不得爲臺郎給舍故激勸之道得而吏
易從也今縣令長滿三歲得任臺諫而守
郡者則不然矣況爲之吏者又從一切因
===
循之謀哉往者
聖天子嚴久任之法重郡縣之選而亦無應
明詔者何也豪傑之士有尚友之志者誠僞公

translation_en:
…the sources of benefit and harm? Even so, are there no men of aspiration who stand distinctly above their fellows? Why, then, do their achievements ultimately fall short of those of antiquity? I have heard that the ministers of the Zhou each maintained their households for generations, and that officials in Han commanderies and counties all raised their descendants there, even taking their surnames from those places. Officials had settled populations to govern, and the people had settled expectations; thus those above could readily issue commands, and those below could readily carry them out. Today, those appointed to office are generally transferred once every three years, and some change posts several times within a single year.
Under the Han, regional inspectors entered the central government as the Three Dukes. Under Tang regulations, anyone who had not served as a prefect could not become a vice minister, and anyone who had not served as a district magistrate could not become a bureau director, supervising secretary, or Secretariat drafter. Thus the means of encouragement were effective, and officials readily responded. Today, district magistrates who complete three years of service may be appointed to censorial or remonstrance posts, but those governing prefectures are not treated in the same way. How much worse when officials themselves follow nothing but expedients for carrying on as before!
Previously, the sagely Son of Heaven made stringent the rules for lengthy tenure and placed great weight on the selection of officials for prefectures and districts. Yet still none responded to his enlightened edict. Why? Outstanding men who aspire to take the worthy men of antiquity as their friends should know what to choose between sincerity and falsehood, public duty and private interest.

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
赫斯怒武備抑豈可盡廢哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝天錫神武奮起淮服驅逐胡元徙
之塞外建五重鎮以制夷狄所謂大同宣
府甘肅遼東大寧是已迨我
成祖文皇帝道光繼述增飭寧夏薊州等邊徙
大寧於畿内而以朶顏福餘泰寧分戍其
地成化弘治間又衛榆林固原繞爲九邊
發卒四十萬以禦之節制之臣介胄之士
星布塞上備邊之制密以詳矣仰惟我
===
上
聖德中興懋隆治極任賢不貳去邪不疑頻年
以來甘露河清之瑞白雀白兎之祥莫不
畢至中國之氣可謂極盛而又
聖武遠布夷狄畏威封疆之臣屢以捷告何其
盛也邇者
明詔廷臣講求邊備豈非安不忘危者哉愚竊
觀今日之勢遼左諸夷屋居耕食無異編
氓土魯番雖竊據哈密再犯甘肅志在□□
punctuated:
赫斯怒，武備抑豈可盡廢哉？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，天錫神武，奮起淮服，驅逐胡元，徙之塞外，建五重鎮以制夷狄，所謂大同、宣府、甘肅、遼東、大寧是已。迨我成祖文皇帝，道光繼述，增飭寧夏、薊州等邊，徙大寧於畿内，而以朶顏、福餘、泰寧分戍其地。成化、弘治間，又衛榆林、固原，繞爲九邊，發卒四十萬以禦之。節制之臣、介胄之士，星布塞上，備邊之制密以詳矣。
仰惟我上，聖德中興，懋隆治極，任賢不貳，去邪不疑。頻年以來，甘露、河清之瑞，白雀、白兎之祥，莫不畢至。中國之氣可謂極盛，而又聖武遠布，夷狄畏威，封疆之臣屢以捷告，何其盛也！邇者，明詔廷臣講求邊備，豈非安不忘危者哉？愚竊觀今日之勢，遼左諸夷屋居耕食，無異編氓。土魯番雖竊據哈密，再犯甘肅，志在□□

He established five major garrison commands to control the barbarians: Datong, Xuanfu, Gansu, Liaodong, and Daning. When our Emperor Chengzu Wen succeeded him, he gloriously carried forward his predecessor’s way, further strengthened the frontiers at Ningxia, Jizhou, and elsewhere, and moved Daning within the metropolitan region, assigning Duoyan, Fuyu, and Taining to garrison its former territory in separate sectors. During the Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns, garrisons were also established at Yulin and Guyuan, forming a surrounding line of nine frontier commands [?], and four hundred thousand soldiers were mobilized to defend them. Officials entrusted with military command and armored warriors were scattered like stars along the frontier. The system of frontier defense was comprehensive and meticulously organized.
We reverently consider how our present sovereign, through his sagely virtue, has brought about a restoration and assiduously raised government to its highest excellence. He employs the worthy without wavering and dismisses the wicked without hesitation. In recent years, auspicious signs—sweet dew, the Yellow River running clear, white sparrows, and white hares—have all appeared. The vital force of the Central Realm may indeed be called supremely flourishing. text:
未添貢而已亦姑弗論延寧宣大固原五
鎮逼近北虜自據河套以來屢爲五鎮之
患而延綏偏關尤當其衝議者謂河套不
復則五鎮之患未已五鎮之患未已則延
寧偏關必有當其害者爲今日之計必先
屯田積穀選將練師逐虜出套復受降之
舊嚴東勝之守則邊境可以無事愚則以
爲不然何則帝王之道不徼其必可勝以
爲功而唯恃吾有自勝之術西漢之世幕
===
南雖無虜廷然中國耗弊亦已勞矣是故
河套之復可以不講也抑愚又有說焉獨
石雖有守矣葦花鎮可不加之意乎三衛
雖藩蔽矣潮河川可不爲之備乎必也重
武冑之選而將領之貪懦者必誅嚴清勾
之令而戍卒之逋逃者必罰復茶馬之舊
而牧圉之簡稽也必時通鹽商之利而芻
糧之儲積也必廣而又重巡撫之寉慎閫
帥之寄紀綱必正功罪必明則邊鎮其□
punctuated: 未添貢而已，亦姑弗論。延、寧、宣、大、固原五鎮逼近北虜，自據河套以來，屢爲五鎮之患，而延綏、偏關尤當其衝。議者謂河套不復，則五鎮之患未已；五鎮之患未已，則延、寧、偏關必有當其害者。爲今日之計，必先屯田積穀，選將練師，逐虜出套，復受降之舊，嚴東勝之守，則邊境可以無事。愚則以爲不然。何則？帝王之道，不徼其必可勝以爲功，而唯恃吾有自勝之術。西漢之世，幕南雖無虜廷，然中國耗弊，亦已勞矣。是故河套之復，可以不講也。抑愚又有說焉。獨石雖有守矣，葦花鎮可不加之意乎？三衛雖藩蔽矣，潮河川可不爲之備乎？必也重武冑之選，而將領之貪懦者必誅；嚴清勾之令，而戍卒之逋逃者必罰；復茶馬之舊，而牧圉之簡稽也必時；通鹽商之利，而芻糧之儲積也必廣。而又重巡撫之寉，慎閫帥之寄，紀綱必正，功罪必明，則邊鎮其□

…merely not increasing tribute [?]; let us also leave this aside for now. The five garrisons of Yansui, Ningxia, Xuanfu, Datong, and Guyuan lie close to the northern enemy. Since occupying the Hetao region, the enemy has repeatedly troubled these five garrisons, with Yansui and Pianguan bearing the brunt. Those discussing the matter say that unless Hetao is recovered, the troubles of the five garrisons will never cease; and while those troubles persist, Yansui, Ningxia, or Pianguan must inevitably suffer. They propose that our present policy must first be to establish military agricultural colonies and accumulate grain, select commanders and train troops, drive the enemy out of Hetao, restore the former arrangements at Shouxiang, and strengthen the defenses of Dongsheng. Then the frontier could be free from trouble.

I humbly think otherwise. Why? The way of emperors and kings does not seek achievement by gambling on assured victory over others; it relies solely on our own means of mastering ourselves. Yet I have another point to make. Although Dushi is defended, can we neglect Weihua Garrison? Although the Three Guards serve as a protective screen, can we fail to make defensive preparations in the Chaohe valley? 第五問
陶欽皐
同考試官教諭官　批〔治水之法莫善於禹貢莫詳於周官而尤莫備於我〕
〔之制第郡縣長吏視爲末務莫之舉行爾此篇條陳盡矣宜錄〕
〔以飾庶官之吏於玆土者〕
考試官訓導許　批〔博雅之學明達之才康濟之志讀此業可槩見矣佳士佳士〕
考試官教諭周　批〔因自然之利脩已然之法〕
格言格言
===
善治水者貴乎因自然之利而脩已然之
法自然之利而能導之則有以永其利於
無窮法之已然者而能脩之則有以維持
之於不壞舍此而曰紛紛焉則亦弊焉耳
punctuated:
無虞乎？雖然，「王猷允塞，徐方旣來。侯誰在矣？張仲孝友。」此周宣能復文武之業而燦然中興者也。愚不敏，顒以是爲今日獻。

第五問
陶欽皐
同考試官教諭官　批〔治水之法莫善於禹貢，莫詳於周官，而尤莫備於我之制。第郡縣長吏視爲末務，莫之舉行爾。此篇條陳盡矣，宜錄以飾庶官之吏於玆土者。〕
考試官訓導許　批〔博雅之學，明達之才，康濟之志，讀此業可槩見矣。佳士！佳士！〕
考試官教諭周　批〔因自然之利，脩已然之法。〕格言！格言！

善治水者，貴乎因自然之利而脩已然之法。自然之利而能導之，則有以永其利於無窮；法之已然者而能脩之，則有以維持之於不壞。舍此而曰紛紛焉，則亦弊焉耳
translation_en:
…be free from danger? Nevertheless, “The king’s plans were truly fulfilled; the lands of Xu had submitted. Who was there at his side? Zhang Zhong, filial and devoted to his brothers.” This explains how King Xuan of Zhou could restore the achievements of Kings Wen and Wu and bring about a brilliant resurgence. Though I am slow of understanding, I respectfully offer this counsel for the present day.

Fifth Policy Question
Tao Qingao

Comment by Associate Examiner Guan, Instructor: “For methods of water management, none surpass the Tribute of Yu; none are more detailed than the Offices of Zhou; and none are more comprehensive than the institutions of our own dynasty. Yet the chief officials of prefectures and counties regard these as minor matters and do not put them into practice. This essay sets them out exhaustively, point by point. It should be recorded to admonish [?] the officials serving in this region.”

Comment by Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: “Broad and refined learning, clear-sighted ability, and the ambition to bring peace and succor to the people—all can be discerned in outline from reading this composition. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!”

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “Build upon natural advantages and maintain established methods.” Wise words! Wise words!

Those skilled in managing water place the highest value on building upon natural advantages and maintaining established methods. If natural advantages can be properly channeled, their benefits can be perpetuated without end; if established methods can be maintained, they can be preserved from deterioration. To abandon these and speak instead of a flurry of undertakings would merely cause harm…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
矣愚嘗讀書至唐虞之際未嘗不掩卷歎
也嗟乎洪水滔天浩浩懐山襄陵此豈細
故哉舜擇於四岳舉伯禹而畀之以平水
土之寄則禹之智真有以逈出當時諸臣
之上而禹之治水不過曰決九川距四海
决畎澮距川而已而天下之言智者莫踰
焉何哉洪範五行水曰潤下知水之性潤
下則知禹之治水矣是故先決九川以導
於海使水之大者有所歸次濬畎澮以距
===
於川使水之小者有所洩此所以九州同
四隩宅而萬世永利也商之衰也五行之
官世失其業周人始命遂人十夫爲溝百
夫爲洫千夫爲澮萬夫爲川而𤲞洫之制
始立稻人以豬畜水以防止水以溝蕩水
以遂均水以列舍水以澮瀉水而溝洫之
制益詳至於匠人氏又辨其深廣之度而
通其蓄洩之宜其法可謂盡善矣然周人
豈夷陵谷而爲之哉亦不過因其自然之
punctuated:
矣。愚嘗讀書至唐虞之際，未嘗不掩卷歎也。嗟乎！洪水滔天，浩浩懐山襄陵，此豈細故哉？舜擇於四岳，舉伯禹而畀之以平水土之寄，則禹之智真有以逈出當時諸臣之上。而禹之治水，不過曰「決九川距四海，决畎澮距川」而已，而天下之言智者莫踰焉，何哉？《洪範》五行，水曰潤下。知水之性潤下，則知禹之治水矣。是故先決九川以導於海，使水之大者有所歸；次濬畎澮以距於川，使水之小者有所洩。此所以九州同、四隩宅，而萬世永利也。

商之衰也，五行之官世失其業。周人始命遂人，十夫爲溝，百夫爲洫，千夫爲澮，萬夫爲川，而𤲞洫之制始立。稻人以豬畜水，以防止水，以溝蕩水，以遂均水，以列舍水，以澮瀉水，而溝洫之制益詳。至於匠人氏，又辨其深廣之度，而通其蓄洩之宜，其法可謂盡善矣。然周人豈夷陵谷而爲之哉？亦不過因其自然之
translation_en:
… I have often, when reading of the age of Tang and Yu, closed the book with a sigh. Alas! Floodwaters rose to the heavens, vast waters encircled the mountains and overtopped the hills: could this have been a trifling matter? Shun made his selection through the Four Mountains officials, raised up Bo Yu, and entrusted him with the task of bringing order to the waters and the land. Yu’s wisdom truly far surpassed that of the other ministers of his time. Yet his management of the waters amounted simply to “opening the nine rivers to lead into the four seas, and opening the field channels and drains to lead into the rivers.” Nevertheless, none whom the world calls wise surpassed him. Why was this? In the account of the Five Phases in the Great Plan, water is said to “moisten and descend.” Once one understands that water’s nature is to moisten and descend, one understands Yu’s management of the waters. Thus he first opened the nine rivers to conduct their waters to the sea, giving the greater waters somewhere to go. Next he dredged the field channels and drains to connect them with the rivers, giving the lesser waters an outlet. This was how the Nine Regions were brought into order and the lands within the four bounds made habitable, providing lasting benefits for ten thousand generations.

When the Shang declined, the officials responsible for the Five Phases lost their expertise over successive generations. The Zhou then appointed Directors of Outlying Districts: for every ten husbandmen’s allotments there was a ditch, for a hundred a larger channel, for a thousand a main drain, and for ten thousand a river. Thus the system of irrigation channels [?] was first established. The Rice-field Officers used reservoirs to store water, embankments to hold it back, ditches to convey it, small channels to distribute it evenly, successive field channels to retain it, and main drains to discharge it. The system of ditches and channels thereby became more detailed. The Master Craftsmen further determined their proper depths and widths and worked out suitable arrangements for storing and releasing water. Their methods may be called consummately good. Yet did the Zhou level the hills and valleys to accomplish this? They merely followed the natural …

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
和而脩伯禹之故而已周之衰也遂人稱
人匠人之官又世失其業列國之君皆自
利以病隣國暴秦之興又廢溝洫開阡陌
而水利廢矣是故孫叔敖起芍陂則楚受
其惠文公穿腴口則蜀以富饒史起鑿漳
水於魏則鄴傍有稻粱之詠鄭國道涇水
於秦則谷口有禾黍之謠許景山復蕭何
之故堰則興元之荒瘠復爲膏腴趙尚寬
脩召信臣之故渠則南陽之瀉鹵變爲沃
壤之數君子者孰非因其自然之利而脩
其已然之法者謂之得周官之遺意亦可
===
也伏惟我
國家司空有總職水利有專官省以督之府
府以督之縣而縣之陂塘圩堰又莫不有
長重以憲臣之稽察皆以懋惠元元而興
水利也然遇水旱民輒告病者是必有其
故矣愚請以江右言之湖東西故揚州之
域厥土惟塗泥厥田下下而九江以西又
punctuated:
和，而脩伯禹之故而已。周之衰也，遂人、稱人、匠人之官又世失其業。列國之君皆自利以病隣國。暴秦之興，又廢溝洫、開阡陌，而水利廢矣。是故孫叔敖起芍陂，則楚受其惠；文公穿腴口，則蜀以富饒；史起鑿漳水於魏，則鄴傍有稻粱之詠；鄭國道涇水於秦，則谷口有禾黍之謠；許景山復蕭何之故堰，則興元之荒瘠復爲膏腴；趙尚寬脩召信臣之故渠，則南陽之瀉鹵變爲沃壤。之數君子者，孰非因其自然之利而脩其已然之法者？謂之得周官之遺意，亦可也。
伏惟我國家，司空有總職，水利有專官，省以督之府，府以督之縣，而縣之陂塘圩堰又莫不有長，重以憲臣之稽察，皆以懋惠元元而興水利也。然遇水旱，民輒告病者，是必有其故矣。愚請以江右言之：湖東西，故揚州之域，厥土惟塗泥，厥田下下，而九江以西又
translation_en:
…harmony, and merely restored the works of the great Yu. As the Zhou declined, the offices of the Sui Ren, Cheng Ren [?], and Jiang Ren—the rural administrators and construction officials—again lost their inherited expertise over successive generations. The rulers of the various states sought their own advantage at the expense of neighboring states. When tyrannical Qin arose, it further abolished the irrigation ditches and opened up the field boundaries, and hydraulic works fell into disuse. Thus, when Sun Shu’ao built the Shaopi reservoir, Chu benefited; when Duke Wen cut through Yukou [?], Shu grew prosperous; when Shi Qi dug a channel from the Zhang River in Wei, songs celebrating rice and millet arose around Ye; and when Zheng Guo diverted the Jing River in Qin, songs celebrating grain and millet arose at Gukou. When Xu Jingshan restored Xiao He’s old weir, the barren land of Xingyuan became fertile again; when Zhao Shangkuan repaired Shao Xinchen’s old canal, the saline land of Nanyang became rich soil. Which of these gentlemen did not take advantage of natural conditions and restore methods already established? It is fair to say that they grasped the intent bequeathed by the Offices of Zhou.
I humbly reflect that in our dynasty the Minister of Works exercises overall responsibility, while dedicated officials oversee hydraulic works. The provinces supervise the prefectures, and the prefectures supervise the counties. Every county’s reservoirs, ponds, polders, and weirs also have their own heads. Added to this are inspections by censorial officials, all intended to enrich the benefits afforded the common people by developing hydraulic works. Yet whenever floods or droughts occur, the people immediately report distress. There must surely be a reason for this. Permit me, in my ignorance, to speak of Jiangyou. The lands east and west of the lake were formerly within the territory of Yangzhou: “Its soil was mud; its fields were of the lowest grade.” The lands west of Jiujiang, moreover, …

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
古荊州之地禹貢所謂彭蠡既豬九江孔
殷者也夫其襟江帶湖水之大者有所歸
小者有所洩矣然小水輙溢小旱輙暵比
他省爲甚邇者春夏之交江水暴漲壞民
田居比連數郡此無他陂塘圩堰之長皆
失其業而郡縣長吏又莫之省憂故也執
事欲脩周官之職加疏濬之功通灌漑之
利絕漂没之患甚盛心也愚則以爲周官
之職不可卒復而溝洫之遺意尚亦可尋
===
周官曰溝必因水勢防必因地勢蓋溝以
導水不因水勢則其流易壅防以止水不
因地勢則其土易壞爲今之計莫若申飭
郡縣長吏督率陂塘圩堰之長察水勢之
曲直原地勢之高卑可堤則堤可決則決
因陂塘圩堰之舊加疏濬築塞之功而又
嚴侵占之禁明考課之法則灌漑之利興
漂没之患免矣雖然賈讓有言曰立國居
民疆理土地必遺川澤之分度水勢所不
punctuated:
古荊州之地，《禹貢》所謂「彭蠡既豬，九江孔殷」者也。夫其襟江帶湖，水之大者有所歸，小者有所洩矣。然小水輙溢，小旱輙暵，比他省爲甚。邇者春夏之交，江水暴漲，壞民田居，比連數郡。此無他，陂塘圩堰之長皆失其業，而郡縣長吏又莫之省憂故也。執事欲脩周官之職，加疏濬之功，通灌漑之利，絕漂没之患，甚盛心也。愚則以爲周官之職不可卒復，而溝洫之遺意尚亦可尋。

《周官》曰：「溝必因水勢，防必因地勢。」蓋溝以導水，不因水勢則其流易壅；防以止水，不因地勢則其土易壞。爲今之計，莫若申飭郡縣長吏，督率陂塘圩堰之長，察水勢之曲直，原地勢之高卑，可堤則堤，可決則決，因陂塘圩堰之舊，加疏濬築塞之功，而又嚴侵占之禁，明考課之法，則灌漑之利興，漂没之患免矣。雖然，賈讓有言曰：「立國居民，疆理土地，必遺川澤之分，度水勢所不
translation_en:
…the territory of ancient Jingzhou, of which the Tribute of Yu says: “Pengli was made into a reservoir, and the Nine Rivers were thoroughly regulated.” With the river at its breast and lakes about its waist, this region has places into which its larger waters can flow and outlets through which its smaller waters can drain. Yet even a slight rise in water brings flooding, and even a slight drought brings parching, more severely than in other provinces. Recently, at the turn of spring and summer, the river rose violently, destroying people’s fields and homes across several adjoining prefectures. There is no other reason for this than that those in charge of reservoirs, ponds, polder embankments, and weirs have all neglected their duties, while the chief officials of the prefectures and counties have given the matter neither scrutiny nor concern. Your wish to restore the duties prescribed in the Offices of Zhou, increase dredging work, secure the benefits of irrigation, and eliminate the scourge of inundation reflects a most admirable intention. In my humble view, however, the offices of Zhou cannot be restored at once, although the principles underlying their system of channels and ditches can still be sought out.

The Offices of Zhou says: “Channels must follow the disposition of the waters; embankments must follow the configuration of the land.” Channels guide water: unless they follow its disposition, their flow is easily obstructed. Embankments hold water back: unless they follow the configuration of the land, their earthworks are easily damaged. The best course now would be to issue renewed, strict instructions to the chief officials of prefectures and counties to supervise those in charge of reservoirs, ponds, polder embankments, and weirs. They should examine the bends and straight stretches of watercourses and investigate the elevations and depressions of the terrain, building embankments wherever appropriate and opening outlets wherever appropriate. Working from the existing reservoirs, ponds, polder embankments, and weirs, they should undertake further dredging, construction, and sealing of breaches. If, in addition, prohibitions against encroachment are strictly enforced and procedures for evaluating officials’ performance are made clear, the benefits of irrigation will be secured and the scourge of inundation avoided. Nevertheless, Jia Rang said: “In establishing a state and settling its people, demarcating and ordering its lands, one must reserve a share for rivers and marshes and determine where the waters do not…”

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
及大川無防小水得入陂障卑下以爲汙
澤使秋水多得有所休息左右游波寬衍
而不迫此誠萬世水利之上策也然豈可
以易言哉是故必有韋丹在豫章而後可
以興南塘之利必有吳明卓在吉水而後
可以興秭陂之利必有何易于在建昌而
後可以興捍水塘之利必有李復在鄱陽
而後可以興邵父塘之利否則亦行文書
具故實而已唯執事者圖之
punctuated: 及，大川無防，小水得入，陂障卑下，以爲汙澤，使秋水多，得有所休息，左右游波，寬衍而不迫。」此誠萬世水利之上策也，然豈可以易言哉？是故必有韋丹在豫章，而後可以興南塘之利；必有吳明卓在吉水，而後可以興秭陂之利；必有何易于在建昌，而後可以興捍水塘之利；必有李復在鄱陽，而後可以興邵父塘之利。否則亦行文書、具故實而已。唯執事者圖之。
translation_en: …reach. Great rivers should have no embankments, allowing lesser streams to enter them. Low-lying ground should be enclosed with banks to form marshes, so that abundant autumn waters have somewhere to settle, their waves spreading freely to either side, with ample room and without constriction.” This is indeed the best strategy for managing water for all ages. Yet how could it be spoken of as easy? Thus, only with a Wei Dan in Yuzhang could the benefits of Nantang Pond be realized; only with a Wu Mingzhuo in Jishui could the benefits of Zibei Reservoir be realized; only with a He Yiyu in Jianchang could the benefits of Hanshuitang Pond be realized; and only with a Li Fu in Poyang could the benefits of Shaofutang Pond be realized. Otherwise, there would merely be the circulation of official documents and the observance of established formalities. May those responsible give this due consideration.

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
夫聖人宰制萬物役使羣動
必錫之藝極以昭標訓是故
選舉之所由始也仰惟
聖朝取士爰立式程能者從之無
弗錄焉者何哉規矩誠陳難
眩以方圓準繩誠具難欺以
===
平直度量誠設難惑以長短
重輕也夫式也者規矩準繩
度量之謂也左不偏于左右
不偏于右高不過亢卑不過
抑中之謂也學者莫可跂焉
傳曰王天下有三重焉其寡
過矣乎三王不襲禮五帝不
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

夫聖人宰制萬物，役使羣動，必錫之藝極，以昭標訓，是故選舉之所由始也。仰惟聖朝取士，爰立式程，能者從之，無弗錄焉者，何哉？規矩誠陳，難眩以方圓；準繩誠具，難欺以平直；度量誠設，難惑以長短重輕也。夫式也者，規矩準繩度量之謂也。左不偏于左，右不偏于右，高不過亢，卑不過抑，中之謂也。學者莫可跂焉。傳曰：「王天下有三重焉，其寡過矣乎！」三王不襲禮，五帝不
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

The sage governs the myriad things and directs all that moves. He must bestow upon them rules and limits, making exemplary instruction manifest. This is the origin of selection for office. We reverently consider how our sagely dynasty, in recruiting men of talent, has established prescribed standards. Those with ability follow them, and none goes unrecorded. Why is this? When compass and square are properly set out, it is difficult to mislead anyone about squareness and roundness; when level and marking cord are properly provided, it is difficult to deceive anyone about evenness and straightness; when measures and weights are properly established, it is difficult to confuse anyone about length and shortness, heaviness and lightness. Prescribed standards are precisely what compass and square, level and marking cord, measures and weights represent. On the left, one does not incline excessively to the left; on the right, one does not incline excessively to the right. In a high position, one is not excessively exalted; in a low position, one is not excessively abased. This is what is meant by the mean. Students cannot reach it even on tiptoe [?]. The transmitted text says: “One who rules the world has three weighty responsibilities; surely he will then make few errors!” The Three Kings did not simply inherit their predecessors’ rites; the Five Emperors did not…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
沿樂法變而道不變其建極
一也高者躐躋般輸工垂之
上自加椎鑿而立門戶畢者
拘泥猥瑣勞筋苦力又矻矻
無成皆不可與于中其如式
何子諸士今以文見思薦
廟覲
===
□□
堂也亦既規矩準繩度量無爽
則焉豈唯爲下不倍又將式
是四方以光化理可謂無負
天子金聲玉振之教禮節樂和
之化矣夫式以立天下之極
者也器以適天下之用者也
方圓平直輕重長短無弗式
punctuated: 沿樂。法變而道不變，其建極一也。高者躐躋般輸、工垂之上，自加椎鑿而立門戶；畢者拘泥猥瑣，勞筋苦力，又矻矻無成，皆不可與于中，其如式何？子諸士今以文見，思薦廟覲□□堂也。亦既規矩準繩度量無爽則焉，豈唯爲下不倍，又將式是四方，以光化理，可謂無負天子金聲玉振之教、禮節樂和之化矣。夫式以立天下之極者也，器以適天下之用者也。方圓平直、輕重長短，無弗式
translation_en:
…continue the same music. Methods change, but the Way does not change: in establishing the supreme standard, they are one. Those who aim high leap above Ban Shu and the master craftsman Chui, applying their own mallets and chisels to establish schools of their own. Those at the lower level [?] cling rigidly to petty details, straining their sinews and exhausting their strength, yet toil without achievement. Neither can attain the mean; how, then, can they conform to the standard?

You gentlemen now present yourselves through your writings, hoping to be recommended for an audience at the ancestral temple and in the □□ hall [?]. Once your compasses, squares, marking lines, levels, measures, and capacities accord without deviation with the rules, you will not merely remain faithful in your subordinate positions: you will also become models for the four quarters, bringing lustre to moral transformation and governance. You may then be said not to have failed the Son of Heaven’s teaching, complete as the sounding of bronze bells and the concluding resonance of jade chimes, or his transforming influence through the discipline of ritual and the harmony of music.

Standards establish the supreme norm for all under Heaven; implements meet the practical needs of all under Heaven. Squareness and roundness, evenness and straightness, lightness and heaviness, length and shortness—none fails to conform to the standard…

鑿不合則偭背玫錯枉尺而
直尋是故吾懼其終離也飾
焉離焉其究也人已並失惟
塵之累士德何以釋於天下
戉相與有成合内外始終斯
可哉
===

導許士德謹序

焉。間施之用也，乃晉爲而無當，是故吾懼其外飾也。一枘鑿不合，則偭背玫錯，枉尺而直尋，是故吾懼其終離也。飾焉，離焉，其究也，人已並失，惟塵之累，士德何以釋於天下？戉相與有成，合内外始終，斯可哉！

…in this. When put to use, they advance into action yet prove unsuitable [?]; thus I fear that theirs is merely outward embellishment. Once a tenon and mortise fail to fit, there is divergence and disorder [?]: they bend a foot to straighten a fathom. Thus I fear that they will ultimately depart from the standard. title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄

政將安施乎聖人愛物之仁亦幾乎息矣是故
聖人知事之難周者莫重乎田而民之難給者
莫重乎食事難周則天下之勢莫可一食難給
則天下之情莫可通故制以經界定為井田其
立意也遠其慮患也周其制法也詳是以貴賤
有等豐殺有章車服田宅莫敢踰制而天下之
分定矣人無廢業田無曠土樂生利用莫肯轉
徙而天下之業安矣藏不偏多故物無偏罄用
不偏厚故人不偏窮無求於力分之外無貸於
===
力分之內務穡無增稅輟稼無減租而天下之
賦平矣伍兩有法車徒有制寓兵於農伏險於
順靡課而人自奮弛禁而衆不攜田不屯而食
足戍不更而守固而天下之變弭矣變弭則無
急難賦平則無怨讟業安則無離散分定則無
僭侈由是而制禮五禮可舉也由是而作樂六
樂可興也由是而明刑修政五刑入政無淫慝
也何也有恒產而有恒心故也不然分之不定
則曰民之悖戾業之不安則曰民之□□賦□
punctuated: 政將安施乎？聖人愛物之仁亦幾乎息矣。是故聖人知事之難周者莫重乎田，而民之難給者莫重乎食。事難周，則天下之勢莫可一；食難給，則天下之情莫可通。故制以經界，定為井田。其立意也遠，其慮患也周，其制法也詳。是以貴賤有等，豐殺有章，車服田宅莫敢踰制，而天下之分定矣。人無廢業，田無曠土，樂生利用，莫肯轉徙，而天下之業安矣。藏不偏多，故物無偏罄；用不偏厚，故人不偏窮。無求於力分之外，無貸於力分之內，務穡無增稅，輟稼無減租，而天下之賦平矣。伍兩有法，車徒有制，寓兵於農，伏險於順，靡課而人自奮，弛禁而衆不攜，田不屯而食足，戍不更而守固，而天下之變弭矣。變弭則無急難，賦平則無怨讟，業安則無離散，分定則無僭侈。由是而制禮，五禮可舉也；由是而作樂，六樂可興也；由是而明刑修政，五刑入政無淫慝也。何也？有恒產而有恒心故也。不然，分之不定，則曰民之悖戾；業之不安，則曰民之□□；賦□
translation_en:
…How, then, could government be put into effect? Even the sage’s benevolence, which cherishes all things, would come close to extinction. Thus the sage understood that, among affairs difficult to provide for comprehensively, none was more important than land, and among the people’s needs difficult to supply, none was more important than food. If affairs could not be comprehensively provided for, the conditions of the realm could not be brought into unity; if food could not be adequately supplied, the sentiments of the realm could not be brought into accord. He therefore regulated territorial boundaries and established the well-field system. His purpose was far-reaching, his precautions against trouble comprehensive, and his regulations detailed.

Accordingly, the noble and the lowly had their proper ranks, and greater and lesser allowances followed established rules. None dared exceed the prescribed limits for carriages, clothing, fields, and dwellings, and the distinctions throughout the realm were settled. No one neglected an occupation, and no land lay idle. People delighted in life and made beneficial use of resources; none wished to migrate elsewhere, and livelihoods throughout the realm were secure. Stores were not disproportionately abundant in one place, so goods were not disproportionately exhausted elsewhere; expenditure was not disproportionately lavish for some, so others were not disproportionately impoverished. Nothing was demanded beyond people’s capacity and allotted obligations, and nothing within those obligations was remitted. Diligent cultivation brought no increase in tax, and cessation of cultivation brought no reduction in rent. Thus taxation throughout the realm was equitable.

Military units of five and twenty-five had their rules, and chariots and infantry their regulations. Soldiers were incorporated among the farmers, and preparedness against danger lay within peaceful order. Without being pressed, people exerted themselves; even when prohibitions were relaxed, the multitude did not fall away. Without military agricultural colonies, food was sufficient; without rotating garrison duty, defenses were secure. Thus disturbances throughout the realm were quelled. With disturbances quelled, there were no emergencies; with taxation equitable, there were no resentful complaints; with livelihoods secure, there was no dispersal; with distinctions settled, there was no presumptuous extravagance.

On this foundation, rites could be instituted and the five categories of ritual practiced; music could be established and the six musical traditions revived. On this foundation, punishments could be clarified and government put in order: the five punishments entered into government [?], and there was no excess or wickedness. Why was this so? Because those with a constant livelihood have constant hearts. Otherwise, when distinctions are unsettled, one says that the people are rebellious; when livelihoods are insecure, one says that the people are [two illegible characters]; when taxation [illegible]…

不平，則曰民之游惰；變之不弭，則曰民之兇獷。其如政焉何哉？昔夏后氏五十而貢，殷人七十而助，周人百畝而徹，其興也勃焉。秦開阡陌，壞溝洫，先王之政戕之殆盡，秦亦與之俱焉。無他，心之仁不仁，田之均不均耳。此可以究立政之本矣。雖然，三代遠矣，井田不可復矣，則斯民終不被其澤，而聖人之仁將湮鬱乎？得井田之意，通其變，不失其宜，師其意，不泥其法，亦惟人君有是心耳。故孟子曰：「堯舜之道，不以仁政，不能平治天下。」蓋仁政者，爲治之本也，而仁心者，又爲政之本也。人君求所以端其本，則天下治矣。

translation_en:
…is inequitable, they say that the people are idle and indolent; when disturbances are not quelled, they say that the people are violent and unruly. What can such an approach accomplish in governing? In antiquity, the Xia rulers allotted fifty mu and employed the tribute system; the Yin allotted seventy and employed the labor-assistance system; the Zhou allotted a hundred mu and employed the shared-levy system. Their rise was vigorous. Qin opened up the field boundaries and destroyed the irrigation channels, almost entirely demolishing the government of the former kings; Qin itself shared its fate [?]. There was no other cause: it was simply a matter of whether their hearts were benevolent and whether their fields were equitably distributed. From this we can discern the foundation of government.

Nevertheless, the Three Dynasties are distant, and the well-field system cannot be restored. Must these people therefore forever go without its benefits, and must the sages’ benevolence remain obscured and stifled? To grasp the intent of the well-field system, adapt it to changing circumstances without losing what is appropriate, and follow its intent without clinging rigidly to its rules—all this depends solely on the ruler possessing such a heart. Thus Mengzi said: “Even with the Way of Yao and Shun, without benevolent government one cannot bring peace and order to the world.” Benevolent government is the foundation of good order, while a benevolent heart is in turn the foundation of government. If the ruler seeks the means to set this foundation right, the world will be well governed.

The he bell was on the carriage’s front rail, and the luan bell and kite [?] were on its crossbar; in going out and coming in, one invariably followed the good path. As for the establishment of preceptors, guardians, advisers, and assistants, which of these arrangements did not provide a pattern of gentleness, refinement, reverence, and respect? Their purpose was to dwell in rectitude and embody the primal principle; nothing was greater than establishing instruction rooted in the heart. These practices survived in the four schools, and their Way resided in the Six Classics. Then Qin, Han, Tang, and Song rose in succession, mixing the teachings of Huang-Lao with those of Shen Buhai and Han Fei and employing them together. Merely piecing together poems and becoming skilled at recitation—could this be called attaining worthiness? Studying ritual in autumn and writings in winter was not heard to foster goodness. Lecturing on the arts of learning in the Sucheng Hall—how did this help with the ocean’s depth [?]? Opening the Bowang establishment to welcome worthy men did nothing to help with shaking the mountain’s lofty heights [?]. These undertakings seemed to await their proper moment; the Way does not operate of itself.
Now we humbly encounter Your Majesty the Emperor, whose sagely reverence rises daily and whose perceptiveness brings timely good order. Succeeding Heaven and establishing the supreme standard, you spread your luminous transforming influence, rising to the level of the Three Sovereigns. Discerning things and examining human relationships, you display your grand designs, surpassing the Five Emperors. You elucidate the mysteries of ordering affairs and governing the heart, and bequeath plans for diligence and frugality. You hold that Heaven brings forth the common people and sets a ruler over them: even a few words become enduring instruction. And when one governs all under Heaven and transmits it to one’s son, one must instruct and admonish him, and □□□ [illegible]. As for established precedents, may there be no …
