translation_en: …virtue [?]. For presiding over the ancestral vessels, none is more important than the eldest son, represented by the hexagram Zhen; studying ancient teachings brings attainment, and nurturing rectitude takes its meaning from the hexagram Meng. The collected teachings are vast and profound, difficult to fathom; yet the learning of the sages, subtle and refined, has its essentials. Recently, in leisure from the myriad affairs of government and during Your Majesty’s reading in the second watch of the night, You drew upon Yao and Shun’s words concerning refinement and singleness of purpose, and upon the import of the sages’ and worthies’ classics and commentaries. The work combines original composition with transmission, and its meanings bear directly upon admonition and guidance. Some passages address particular matters to illuminate human relationships; others speak comprehensively to gather together the essentials. All that makes fathers fathers and sons sons is assembled in this book; rulers acting as rulers and ministers as ministers alike return to the Way. In speaking of diligent study, it calls for honoring teachers and valuing transmitted teachings; in discussing emulation of the ancestors, it calls for revering Heaven and laboring for the people. Its method of instruction takes filial piety, benevolence, ritual propriety, and righteousness as its foundation. Its detailed provisions extend even to the subtleties of bearing, expression, speech, and tone. As applied to affairs, they are penetrating, pertinent, lucid, and clear; their underlying purpose is, moreover, lofty, enlightened, broad, and great. Far-reaching in conception, it matches the ancient chapter ‘King Wen as Heir Apparent’; manifest in its models and warnings, it makes the later bestowal of the Tang emperor’s Model for Emperors seem paltry. Engraving it upon fine jade fittingly enhances the plan to secure peace for future generations; extending its bestowal to the officials spreads still further the abundant outpouring of imperial benevolence. Even such uncultivated and unlearned servants as we have shared in this gracious bestowal and humbly glimpse…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
金鐀之閟嚴仰見
瑤編之易簡如游河洛重披龍馬之祥若在
唐虞親聞授受之語
帝澤沃江河之潤
天文爛奎璧之輝喜溢縉紳光生蔀屋此
熙朝之盛事爲儒者之極榮臣廣等深惟保
傳以無功重拜
絲綸於有奕
慶雲豐惠雖不遺葑菲之微爝火餘明亦何
===
日星之耀自兹以往益勵厥初尊所聞行所知
補
期不負於
教育道於前承於後庶仰答於涓埃伏願
慎迺永圖
克昌厥後
惇德允元而蠻夷服
本支延百世之長
家齊國治而天下平
punctuated:
金鐀之閟嚴，仰見瑤編之易簡，如游河洛，重披龍馬之祥；若在唐虞，親聞授受之語。帝澤沃江河之潤，天文爛奎璧之輝，喜溢縉紳，光生蔀屋。此熙朝之盛事，爲儒者之極榮。
臣廣等深惟保傳以無功，重拜絲綸於有奕。慶雲豐惠，雖不遺葑菲之微；爝火餘明，亦何日星之耀？自兹以往，益勵厥初，尊所聞，行所知，補。期不負於教育，道於前，承於後，庶仰答於涓埃。
伏願慎迺永圖，克昌厥後，惇德允元而蠻夷服，本支延百世之長，家齊國治而天下平。
translation_en:
…the solemn secrecy of the golden coffer, and reverently perceive the ease and simplicity of the precious volume. It is as though we were traveling along the He and Luo rivers, beholding anew the auspicious dragon-horse; as though we were present in the days of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, personally hearing their words as they handed on and received the succession. Imperial favor moistens us with the bounty of rivers; the imperial writing shines with the brilliance of the Kui and Bi constellations. Joy overflows among the gentry, and light reaches even humble, darkened dwellings. This is a glorious event of our flourishing dynasty and the highest honor for scholars.
Your servant Guang and the others reflect deeply that, though we have rendered no service as guardians and tutors [?], we have again reverently received your resplendent imperial words. The abundant bounty of auspicious clouds does not overlook even such insignificant plants as turnips and radishes; yet what can the lingering glimmer of a torch add to the brilliance of sun and stars [?]? Henceforth we shall strive still harder to fulfill our original resolve, honor what we have heard, and practice what we know. [The character 補, “supplement,” appears displaced here.] We hope not to fail the instruction we have received: with guidance given before us and taken up by us afterward [?], we may thus repay the smallest measure of your favor.
We humbly wish that you will attend carefully to your enduring plans and bring prosperity to your descendants; that, by fostering virtue and trusting the good, you will win the submission of the Man and Yi peoples; that the main and collateral branches of your house will endure for a hundred generations; and that, with the family ordered and the state well governed, all under Heaven will be at peace…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
宗社衍萬年之盛臣廣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叅場
策五道
第一問
雷達
===
同考試官教諭文　批我
皇上一心學與吾子能發揚卓有真見是有得於理學者其録之
同考試官教諭楊　批措詞敬慎
考試官訓導許　批明哲渾融
考試官教諭周　批典重
帝王之學一本於道帝王之道一本於心
心也者道之會也道也者文之會也心而
非道則非所以爲心矣文而非心又豈所
punctuated:
宗社衍萬年之盛。臣廣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叅場，策五道。
第一問。
雷達。
同考試官教諭文，批：「我皇上一心學與，吾子能發揚，卓有真見，是有得於理學者，其録之。」
同考試官教諭楊，批：「措詞敬慎。」
考試官訓導許，批：「明哲渾融。」
考試官教諭周，批：「典重。」
帝王之學，一本於道；帝王之道，一本於心。心也者，道之會也；道也者，文之會也。心而非道，則非所以爲心矣；文而非心，又豈所
translation_en:
…may the ancestral temples and the altars of state enjoy flourishing prosperity for ten thousand years. Your servant Guang and the others, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, are overcome with fervent emotion and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third session: five policy questions.
First question.
Lei Da.
Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor, comments: “Our Emperor’s learning of the mind [?]—you have been able to expound it, displaying outstanding and genuine insight. Here is someone who has attained an understanding of the Learning of Principle. Let him be selected.”
Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “Respectful and circumspect in wording.”
Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Lucid and discerning, thoroughly integrated.”
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “Classical and dignified.”
The learning of emperors and kings is rooted wholly in the Way; the Way of emperors and kings is rooted wholly in the mind. The mind is where the Way comes together; the Way is where literary expression comes together. If the mind departs from the Way, it loses that by which it is the mind. If literary expression departs from the mind, how could it…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
以爲文也哉是則帝王之學必以養心爲
主而養心之要必以體道爲功養心體道
則帝王之道盡矣若以心術之微用之於
文辭之末則亦藝焉爾已亦豈帝王之學
哉夫嘗求之於伏羲之爻象堯舜之典謨
商周之雅頌矣即其書而論其世即其世
而論其人然其所言之理即其所行之道
唐虞三代之治可以想見其形容也三代
而下漢高帝有三侯之章武帝有秋風之
===
詞唐太宗教子有書宋眞宗尊孔子有贊
宋理宗崇儒有論宏詞雅什渢渢乎非不
可觀與心無補與治無益雜伯雜夷所以
不能復唐虞三代之舊矣洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
帝王之資出於
天授
聖哲之學本於性成有
大誥以諭天下
punctuated:
以爲文也哉？是則帝王之學必以養心爲主，而養心之要必以體道爲功。養心體道，則帝王之道盡矣。若以心術之微用之於文辭之末，則亦藝焉爾已，亦豈帝王之學哉？夫嘗求之於伏羲之爻象、堯舜之典謨、商周之雅頌矣。即其書而論其世，即其世而論其人，然其所言之理，即其所行之道。唐虞三代之治，可以想見其形容也。三代而下，漢高帝有《三侯》之章，武帝有《秋風》之詞，唐太宗教子有書，宋眞宗尊孔子有贊，宋理宗崇儒有論。宏詞雅什，渢渢乎非不可觀，與心無補，與治無益，雜伯雜夷，所以不能復唐虞三代之舊矣。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，帝王之資出於天授，聖哲之學本於性成，有《大誥》以諭天下。
translation_en:
…be regarded as writing? Thus the learning of emperors and kings must take nurturing the mind as its principal concern, and the essential work of nurturing the mind must consist in embodying the Way. Nurture the mind and embody the Way, and the Way of emperors and kings is fully realized. If the subtle workings of the mind are applied merely to the minor pursuit of literary expression, this amounts only to an art. How could it constitute the learning of emperors and kings? I have sought it in Fuxi’s hexagram lines and images, in the Canons and Counsels of Yao and Shun, and in the Odes and Hymns of Shang and Zhou. From their writings one considers their age; from their age one considers the men themselves. The principles they expressed were precisely the Way they practiced. One can thus envision the character of government under Yao and Shun and the Three Dynasties. After the Three Dynasties, Emperor Gao of Han composed the Three Marquises [?], and Emperor Wu composed the Autumn Wind. Emperor Taizong of Tang wrote to instruct his son; Emperor Zhenzong of Song composed a eulogy honoring Confucius; and Emperor Lizong of Song composed a discourse exalting Confucian learning. Their grand compositions and elegant verses, so richly resonant, were certainly worthy of attention. Yet they did nothing to improve the mind or benefit government. Their rule mingled hegemonic practices with those of the barbarians; hence they could not restore the ways of Yao and Shun and the Three Dynasties.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao received his imperial endowments from Heaven, and that his sagely learning was rooted in his innate nature. He produced the Grand Pronouncements to instruct all under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
大祀文幷歌九章以祀
天地神祇有諭高麗西番等國
詔誥見於儒臣劉基宋濂輩所贊述者有曰與
典謨訓誥實相表裏有曰
聖子
神孫俾爲矜式眞與唐虞三代之文一矣其曰
帝王之治莫盛於堯舜觀其授受其要在執
厥中斯義也其得堯舜之心傳矣乎迨我
□上欽承
===
綂丕著
鴻猷
祖德有詩繼
宣宗章皇帝
御製而作也
繼述之志可以感孚
天地矣
大狩龍飛有錄展謁
顯陵而作也
punctuated: 大祀文幷歌九章，以祀天地神祇；有諭高麗、西番等國詔誥。見於儒臣劉基、宋濂輩所贊述者，有曰：「與典謨訓誥實相表裏。」有曰：「聖子神孫，俾爲矜式。」眞與唐虞三代之文一矣。其曰：「帝王之治莫盛於堯舜，觀其授受，其要在執厥中。」斯義也，其得堯舜之心傳矣乎！迨我□上欽承綂，丕著鴻猷，《祖德》有詩，繼宣宗章皇帝御製而作也，繼述之志可以感孚天地矣。《大狩龍飛》有錄，展謁顯陵而作也。
translation_en:
…texts for the great sacrifices, together with nine songs, to offer sacrifice to Heaven, Earth, and the spirits; and edicts and proclamations addressing Gaoli, Xifan, and other countries. Among the laudatory accounts by such Confucian officials as Liu Ji and Song Lian, one says: “They truly complement the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements.” Another says: “Let his sagely sons and divine grandsons take them as their model.” They are indeed at one with the writings of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. He says: “Among the reigns of emperors and kings, none surpassed those of Yao and Shun. Looking at their transmission and receipt of sovereignty, its essence lay in holding fast to the Mean.” Does this principle not show that he had grasped the teaching transmitted from the minds of Yao and Shun?
When our present sovereign [?] reverently inherited the imperial succession and splendidly manifested his grand designs, he composed a poem, Ancestral Virtue, continuing an imperial composition by Emperor Xuanzong Zhang. His resolve to carry on his predecessors’ work could move Heaven and Earth and win their trust. There is also a record entitled The Great Hunt and the Dragon’s Ascent [?], composed on the occasion of his reverential visit to Xianling.

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
仁孝之誠可以對越
神明矣
穀祇蠶壇有甝則
敬天勤民之本也非無逸七月之心乎
敬一有箴則脩巳治人之實也非洪範典謨
之旨乎眞與
聖祖之文一矣其曰
皇極建其中王道弘正直又曰惟敬惟一畏天
敬民斯義也其得
===
===
祖之心傳矣乎其視漢唐宋諸作殆亦騷人
韻士焉耳其可以並觀乎哉是則天道弗
巳吾心之道亦弗巳易有大極書有執中
詩有敬止皆此義也有巳則與天有間而
去道也遠矣詩曰小心翼翼昭事上帝又
曰勉勉我王綱紀四方此文王之所以爲
文也愚也零育化澤乂矣敢以此義而爲
當寧獻焉
第二問
punctuated:
仁孝之誠，可以對越神明矣。穀祇蠶壇有甝，則敬天勤民之本也，非《無逸》《七月》之心乎？敬一有箴，則脩巳治人之實也，非《洪範》《典》《謨》之旨乎？眞與聖祖之文一矣。其曰：「皇極建其中，王道弘正直。」又曰：「惟敬惟一，畏天敬民。」斯義也，其得祖之心傳矣乎？其視漢唐宋諸作，殆亦騷人韻士焉耳，其可以並觀乎哉？是則天道弗巳，吾心之道亦弗巳。《易》有大極，《書》有執中，《詩》有敬止，皆此義也。有巳，則與天有間，而去道也遠矣。《詩》曰：「小心翼翼，昭事上帝。」又曰：「勉勉我王，綱紀四方。」此文王之所以爲文也。愚也零育化澤乂矣，敢以此義而爲當寧獻焉。

第二問
translation_en:
…The sincerity of his benevolence and filial devotion enables him to stand before the divine powers. The writings concerning grain, the earth spirits, and the silkworm altar [?; the character 甝 is unclear here] concern the foundation of revering Heaven and diligently caring for the people. Is this not the spirit of “Against Idleness” and “The Seventh Month”? The admonition on reverence and single-mindedness concerns the actual practice of cultivating oneself and governing others. Is this not the purport of “The Great Plan,” the “Canons,” and the “Counsels”? His writings truly accord with those of the sagely ancestor. They say: “The imperial standard establishes the mean; the kingly Way extends rectitude.” They also say: “Be reverent, be single-minded; stand in awe of Heaven and respect the people.” In this teaching, has he not received the transmission of his ancestor’s mind? Viewed against these writings, the works of the Han, Tang, and Song seem merely the compositions of poets and versifiers. How could they be considered on equal terms?

Thus, the Way of Heaven never ceases, and the Way within our minds likewise never ceases. The Book of Changes speaks of the Supreme Ultimate; the Book of Documents, of holding fast to the mean; and the Book of Odes, of abiding in reverence. All express this meaning. If there is any cessation, a separation arises between oneself and Heaven, and one becomes far removed from the Way. The Book of Odes says: “With vigilant care and reverence, he illustriously served the Lord on High.” It also says: “Unremitting was our king, ordering and regulating the four quarters.” This is why King Wen was called Wen, “the Cultured.” In my ignorance, I have long been nurtured by the beneficent influence of imperial transformation [?; the transcription is garbled]. I venture to present this meaning to Your Majesty.

Second Question

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
雷賀
同考試官教諭陳　批〔修明禮樂已有〕
〔成典而子欲爲樂經以與禮經並行推究本原深得〕
聖人制作至意可見知本之學矣
同考試官教諭毛　批〔修補樂經〕
〔今日首務此作能言其意殆有得於治道者〕
考試官訓導許　批〔禮樂之旨此作發明殆盡〕
〔足見所學〕
考試官教諭周　批〔純雅〕
===
治天下有道本乎人心而已矣治人心有
道本乎禮樂而已矣何也人生而靜天之
性也感物而動性之欲也而其主之者心
也不有禮樂以爲之制則蕩然靡然將有
無所止極者矣天下何從而治邪故聖人
緣人情以制禮樂蓋所以立其本也記曰
樂者天地之和也禮者天地之序也禮樂
之道蓋通乎天地而繫乎人心者也禮樂
明備則天地斯可以官矣否則此心不存
punctuated:
雷賀

同考試官教諭陳，批〔修明禮樂，已有〕〔成典，而子欲爲樂經，以與禮經並行，推究本原，深得〕聖人制作至意，可見知本之學矣。

同考試官教諭毛，批〔修補樂經，〕〔今日首務。此作能言其意，殆有得於治道者。〕

考試官訓導許，批〔禮樂之旨，此作發明殆盡，〕〔足見所學。〕

考試官教諭周，批〔純雅。〕

治天下有道，本乎人心而已矣；治人心有道，本乎禮樂而已矣。何也？人生而靜，天之性也；感物而動，性之欲也。而其主之者，心也。不有禮樂以爲之制，則蕩然靡然，將有無所止極者矣，天下何從而治邪？故聖人緣人情以制禮樂，蓋所以立其本也。《記》曰：「樂者，天地之和也；禮者，天地之序也。」禮樂之道，蓋通乎天地而繫乎人心者也。禮樂明備，則天地斯可以官矣；否則，此心不存，
translation_en:
Lei He

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Established canons already exist for clarifying and perfecting rites and music, yet you propose to compile a Classic of Music to circulate alongside the Classic of Rites. By investigating their fundamental origins, you have deeply grasped the sages’ ultimate intention in instituting them. This reveals learning that understands the foundations.”

Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: “Restoring the Classic of Music is the foremost task today. This composition expresses the intention behind it; its author seems to have gained an understanding of the Way of government.”

Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This composition elucidates the meaning of rites and music almost exhaustively, amply demonstrating the author’s learning.”

Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “Pure and elegant.”

There is a Way to govern all under Heaven: it is rooted simply in the human heart. There is a Way to govern the human heart: it is rooted simply in rites and music. Why is this? The stillness with which people are born is their Heaven-given nature; their stirring in response to things is the desire of that nature. What presides over these is the heart. Without rites and music to regulate it, it will become unrestrained and wayward, potentially knowing no bounds. How, then, could all under Heaven be governed? Thus the sages instituted rites and music in accordance with human feelings, thereby establishing the foundation. The Record of Rites says: “Music is the harmony of Heaven and Earth; rites are the order of Heaven and Earth.” The Way of rites and music pervades Heaven and Earth and is bound to the human heart. When rites and music are clearly established and fully provided, Heaven and Earth can thereby be brought under ordered administration. Otherwise, this heart is not preserved …

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
此理亦從泯沒沒聖人之道亦幾乎熄
矣樂焉何足以配天而禮焉何足以配地
邪五禮六樂之作肇自唐虞皆與人心以
爲之主也三綱五常禮之大體三代因之
而不能變以至於樂則亦兼綜而用之周
禮大司徒非不有私於大武而必與六樂
同之蓋不容有所去取於其間矣漢高帝
有叔孫禮唐太宗有貞觀禮宋太祖有建
隆禮而天下未底於中正豈叔孫魏徵之
===
徒未得其人亦當時之治有未辨而禮有
未具焉者邪漢惠帝有安世樂唐高祖有
雅樂宋仁宗有大安樂而天下未協於和
平豈祖孝孫和峴之輩未得其人亦當時
之功有未大而樂有未備焉者邪洪惟我
太祖高皇帝以
聖人之德在
天子之位
命牛諒制禮陶凱典樂復唐虞三代之舊以爲
punctuated:
此理亦從泯沒沒，聖人之道亦幾乎熄矣。樂焉何足以配天，而禮焉何足以配地邪？五禮六樂之作，肇自唐虞，皆與人心以爲之主也。三綱五常，禮之大體，三代因之而不能變；以至於樂，則亦兼綜而用之。《周禮》大司徒，非不有私於大武，而必與六樂同之，蓋不容有所去取於其間矣。漢高帝有叔孫禮，唐太宗有貞觀禮，宋太祖有建隆禮，而天下未底於中正，豈叔孫、魏徵之徒未得其人，亦當時之治有未辨而禮有未具焉者邪？漢惠帝有安世樂，唐高祖有雅樂，宋仁宗有大安樂，而天下未協於和平，豈祖孝孫、和峴之輩未得其人，亦當時之功有未大而樂有未備焉者邪？
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，以聖人之德，在天子之位，命牛諒制禮，陶凱典樂，復唐虞三代之舊，以爲
translation_en:
…this principle, too, consequently disappears [?], and the Way of the sages comes close to extinction. How, then, could music be worthy of matching Heaven, or ritual be worthy of matching Earth? The creation of the five categories of ritual and the six musical traditions began in the ages of Tang and Yu; all took the human heart as their governing basis. The Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues constitute the essential framework of ritual. The Three Dynasties followed these and could not alter them; as for music, they likewise incorporated the inherited traditions and employed them together. The Minister of Education in the Rites of Zhou was not without a particular preference for the Great Martial Dance (Dawu), yet necessarily accorded it the same standing as the six musical traditions: there could be no picking and choosing among them.
Emperor Gao of Han had the rites of Shusun, Emperor Taizong of Tang the Zhenguan rites, and Emperor Taizu of Song the Jianlong rites, yet the realm did not attain balance and rectitude. Was this because men such as Shusun and Wei Zheng were not the right men for the task? Or was it also because the government of those times had matters still unresolved, and their rites remained incomplete? Emperor Hui of Han had the Music for Pacifying the Age (Anshi), Emperor Gaozu of Tang had Elegant Music (Yayue), and Emperor Renzong of Song had the Music of Great Peace (Da’an), yet the realm did not achieve harmony and peace. Was this because men such as Zu Xiaosun and He Xian were not the right men for the task? Or was it also because the achievements of those times were not yet great, and their music remained incomplete?
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao, possessing the virtue of a sage and occupying the position of the Son of Heaven, ordered Niu Liang to establish the rites and Tao Kai to direct music. He restored the ancient practices of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, to make them …

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
一代之典眞
大聖人之所作爲矣迨我
皇上建中和之極懋中興之業修著
大明集禮
郊
廟之祀朝會之儀縣邑里社飲酒讀律之法朝
貢
親征遣將之制以至於弔賻喪儀罔不俱載鍾
律則有律原律數中聲子聲之類雅樂則
===
有樂制樂舞樂歌樂章之說以至俗樂罔
不畢舉是眞可以官天地協陰陽定上下
和神人者矣然天下之人散處於閭閻里
巷之下
聖人制作未得以覩其全書日用之間莫不用
禮而禮或失之於有慝莫不用樂而樂或
失之於有淫則亦何所適從哉是故禮樂
二經不可偏廢禮已備矣而樂經猶有所
未修爲治之道是誠有所未盡者矣然欲
punctuated: 一代之典，眞大聖人之所作爲矣！迨我皇上建中和之極，懋中興之業，修著《大明集禮》，郊廟之祀、朝會之儀、縣邑里社飲酒讀律之法、朝貢親征遣將之制，以至於弔賻喪儀，罔不俱載。鍾律則有律原、律數、中聲、子聲之類；雅樂則有樂制、樂舞、樂歌、樂章之說，以至俗樂，罔不畢舉。是眞可以官天地、協陰陽、定上下、和神人者矣！然天下之人散處於閭閻里巷之下，聖人制作，未得以覩其全書。日用之間，莫不用禮，而禮或失之於有慝；莫不用樂，而樂或失之於有淫，則亦何所適從哉？是故禮樂二經不可偏廢。禮已備矣，而樂經猶有所未修，爲治之道，是誠有所未盡者矣。然欲
translation_en:
…the institutions of a dynasty: truly the work of a great sage! In our own time, His Majesty has established the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony, advanced the enterprise of dynastic renewal, and compiled the Collected Rites of the Great Ming (Da Ming jili). It records everything: sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temples; ceremonies of court assemblies; rules for communal drinking ceremonies and readings of the laws in counties, towns, and village communities; regulations for tribute audiences, imperial military expeditions, and the dispatch of commanders; and even condolences, contributions toward funeral expenses, and mourning ceremonies. On bells and pitch standards, it includes such matters as the origins and numerical principles of pitch standards, principal tones, and upper-octave tones. On elegant music, it discusses musical institutions, dances, songs, and compositions; it even comprehensively covers popular music. These truly are means to order Heaven and Earth, harmonize yin and yang, establish the distinctions between superior and inferior, and bring spirits and human beings into concord!

Yet the people throughout the realm, scattered among humble neighborhoods and village lanes, have been unable to see the complete book of the sage’s institutional creations. In daily life, everyone practices ritual, yet ritual sometimes goes astray through depravity; everyone uses music, yet music sometimes goes astray through excess. What, then, are they to follow? Thus neither of the two classics, the Classic of Rites and the Classic of Music, may be neglected. Ritual is already fully provided for, but the Classic of Music remains incompletely compiled. In the way of governing, there is indeed something still unfulfilled. Yet if one wishes to…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
考黄鍾員徑之法裁五聲六律之變參變
宮變徵之宜審變律半聲之例各極其妙
以定律吕則當本之於
大明集禮合之於禮記以肇其端參之以古人
成法以窮其變采之以先儒格言以致其
詳作爲樂經一書以補六經之缺與禮經
並行於天下使天下之人士傳其義人守
其法父子兄弟夫婦莫不和親長幼朋友
莫不和順如此則政化大行風俗淳美而
===
禮樂達於天下矣嗟夫斯民也與三代之
民一也其心未嘗不同而禮樂之制何其
不同有如是哉盖三代而上治出於一而
禮樂達於天下三代而下治出於二而禮
樂爲虛文故也人心豈有未一者乎寥寥
千古良有慨嘆幸有
聖天子在上敢不悉心以究乎禮樂之說焉
第三問
陳炌
punctuated:
考黄鍾員徑之法，裁五聲六律之變，參變宮變徵之宜，審變律半聲之例，各極其妙，以定律吕，則當本之於《大明集禮》，合之於《禮記》以肇其端，參之以古人成法以窮其變，采之以先儒格言以致其詳，作爲《樂經》一書，以補六經之缺，與禮經並行於天下，使天下之人士傳其義，人守其法，父子兄弟夫婦莫不和親，長幼朋友莫不和順。如此則政化大行，風俗淳美，而禮樂達於天下矣。嗟夫！斯民也，與三代之民一也，其心未嘗不同，而禮樂之制何其不同有如是哉？盖三代而上，治出於一，而禮樂達於天下；三代而下，治出於二，而禮樂爲虛文故也。人心豈有未一者乎？寥寥千古，良有慨嘆！幸有聖天子在上，敢不悉心以究乎禮樂之說焉！

第三問
陳炌
translation_en:
…to investigate the methods for determining the circumference and diameter of the Huangzhong pitch pipe, regulate the variations of the five notes and six pitch standards, consider the appropriate use of the altered gong and altered zhi notes, and examine the rules for altered pitch standards and half-tones [?], mastering the subtleties of each so as to establish the pitch standards, one should take the Collected Rites of the Great Ming as the foundation and reconcile it with the Record of Rites to lay the groundwork. One should consult established methods of the ancients to explore the full range of variations and draw upon authoritative sayings of earlier Confucian scholars to work out the details. A Classic of Music should thus be compiled to fill the gap among the Six Classics and circulate throughout the realm alongside the Classic of Rites. This would enable the scholars of the realm to transmit its meaning and everyone to observe its rules. Fathers and sons, elder and younger brothers, and husbands and wives would all live in affection and harmony; elders and juniors, and friends, would all live in concord. In this way, governance and moral transformation would spread widely, customs would become pure and fine, and rites and music would prevail throughout the realm.

Alas! These people are the same as the people of the Three Dynasties, and their hearts have never been different. Why, then, should their institutions of rites and music differ so greatly? It is because, in the Three Dynasties and earlier, governance issued from a single source, and rites and music prevailed throughout the realm; after the Three Dynasties, governance issued from two sources, and rites and music became empty forms. How could human hearts ever have lacked this unity? Across the long, silent ages, there is indeed much to lament! Fortunately, the sage Son of Heaven reigns above. How could we dare not devote our whole minds to investigating the teachings concerning rites and music!

Third Question
Chen Kai

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導彭 批〔誠偽公私之辨最切為吏〕
者〔心術聞斯言者可以興矣〕
同考試官學正王 批〔爾雅渾厚宛然漢作子其〕
〔工古文辭者邪〕
同考試官學正羅 批〔博聞彊記篤志力行之學〕
〔讀此作可以見矣敬羨敬羨〕
考試官訓導許 批〔敷陳條答曲盡其妙可錄〕
考試官教諭周 批〔是知尚友古人者〕
古之吏民者純心以為民故功烈施於當
===
時聲名垂於後世而亦有以享其祀於無
窮今之吏民者虛文以自為故名立而隳
亦隨之亦有名未立而輒以敗者此其故
何哉誠偽之所繇分而公私之辨也執事
發策以古人之治江西績效顯著隆載祀
典者為問其所以開尚友之志而致意於
郡縣之治其憂勤可知已愚謹按祭法曰
法施於民則祀之以死勤事則祀之以勞
定國則祀之能禦大災則祀之能捍大患
punctuated:
同考試官訓導彭批：〔誠偽公私之辨，最切為吏〕者〔心術。聞斯言者，可以興矣。〕
同考試官學正王批：〔爾雅渾厚，宛然漢作。子其〕〔工古文辭者邪？〕
同考試官學正羅批：〔博聞彊記，篤志力行之學，〕〔讀此作可以見矣。敬羨！敬羨！〕
考試官訓導許批：〔敷陳條答，曲盡其妙，可錄。〕
考試官教諭周批：〔是知尚友古人者。〕
古之吏民者，純心以為民，故功烈施於當時，聲名垂於後世，而亦有以享其祀於無窮。今之吏民者，虛文以自為，故名立而隳亦隨之，亦有名未立而輒以敗者。此其故何哉？誠偽之所繇分，而公私之辨也。執事發策，以古人之治江西、績效顯著、隆載祀典者為問，其所以開尚友之志，而致意於郡縣之治，其憂勤可知已。愚謹按《祭法》曰：「法施於民則祀之，以死勤事則祀之，以勞定國則祀之，能禦大災則祀之，能捍大患
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Peng, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The distinction between sincerity and falsity, public service and private interest, bears most directly upon the moral disposition of officials. Those who hear these words may be stirred to action.”
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “Refined, substantial, and vigorous: this reads just like a work of the Han. Are you perhaps an accomplished writer of ancient-style prose?”
Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “The learning that comes from extensive knowledge, a strong memory, firm purpose, and earnest practice is evident in this composition. Respect and admiration! Respect and admiration!”
Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The exposition and point-by-point responses bring out every subtlety. Worthy of selection.”
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “Here is someone who understands how to take the ancients as his friends.”
Those who governed the people in antiquity served them with a sincere heart. Thus their achievements benefited their own times, their reputations endured in later ages, and they also earned sacrificial honors without end. Those who govern the people today employ empty formalities to serve themselves. Thus, once their reputation is established, its ruin follows; some meet with failure before their reputation has even been established. Why is this? It lies in the divide between sincerity and falsity, and the distinction between public service and private interest. title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
則祀之聖王之制祭祀而必謹此五者何
哉蓋所以端爲吏之趨而示斯民以義之
道也姑自漢以下祀於江右者論之宋敂
庠退奸貪進忠善而虎東渡江其化遠矣
陶士行勤於吏職筆翰如流而匡輔王室
竟以成功其勞著矣夫是有九江之祀房
琯撫宜春而列郡是式建學興禮之功崇
矣韓昌黎刺袁州而其政推之天下計傭
贖隸之法詳矣李德裕爲州長史而奬掖
===
士類不以遷謫介意其大節卓犖矣夫是
有袁之祀狄梁公精忠大節與日月爭光
而奏免民租縱囚歸獄尤繫彭澤之思夫
是有彭澤之祀張曲江危言正論與風霜
俱厲而循孺子祠禱雨輙應尤繫洪州之
思夫是有南昌之祀顏魯公脩塍築陂溉
田萬頃撫民于今賴之况忠義之素著乎
夫是有撫之祀濂溪周子司理南安洗冤
澤物而殺人媚人吾不爲也一言有以奪
punctuated:
則祀之。聖王之制祭祀而必謹此五者，何哉？蓋所以端爲吏之趨，而示斯民以義之道也。

姑自漢以下祀於江右者論之。宋敂庠退奸貪，進忠善，而虎東渡江，其化遠矣。陶士行勤於吏職，筆翰如流，而匡輔王室，竟以成功，其勞著矣。夫是有九江之祀。房琯撫宜春，而列郡是式，建學興禮之功崇矣。韓昌黎刺袁州，而其政推之天下，計傭贖隸之法詳矣。李德裕爲州長史，而奬掖士類，不以遷謫介意，其大節卓犖矣。夫是有袁之祀。狄梁公精忠大節，與日月爭光，而奏免民租、縱囚歸獄，尤繫彭澤之思。夫是有彭澤之祀。張曲江危言正論，與風霜俱厲，而循孺子祠，禱雨輙應，尤繫洪州之思。夫是有南昌之祀。顏魯公脩塍築陂，溉田萬頃，撫民于今賴之，况忠義之素著乎？夫是有撫之祀。濂溪周子司理南安，洗冤澤物，而「殺人媚人，吾不爲也」，一言有以奪
translation_en:
…then he is to receive sacrifices. Why did the sage kings, in establishing sacrifices, insist on scrupulously observing these five criteria? They did so to set officials’ aspirations aright and show the people the way of righteousness.

Let us consider those who have received sacrifices in Jiangyou since the Han. Song Kouxiang [?] dismissed the wicked and corrupt and promoted the loyal and good; tigers crossed the river eastward. Far-reaching indeed was his transforming influence. Tao Shixing worked diligently at his official duties, his writing flowing freely; he supported the royal house and ultimately achieved success. Conspicuous indeed were his services. Hence the sacrifices to them in Jiujiang. Fang Guan governed Yichun, and the surrounding commanderies took him as their model. Great were his achievements in establishing schools and promoting ritual propriety. Han Changli served as Prefect of Yuanzhou, and his policies were extended throughout the realm. Detailed were his provisions for reckoning the value of labor to redeem bondspeople. Li Deyu served as Chief Administrator of the prefecture and encouraged and supported men of learning, taking no offense at his demotion and banishment. Outstanding indeed was his integrity. Hence the sacrifices to them in Yuanzhou. Di, Duke of Liang, displayed pure loyalty and high integrity that rivaled the sun and moon in brilliance. His memorial requesting exemption from the people’s grain tax, and his release of prisoners who subsequently returned to prison, especially bound the people of Pengze to his memory. Hence the sacrifices to him in Pengze. Zhang Qujiang’s forthright words and upright arguments were as stern as wind and frost. His visits to the shrine of Ruzi [?], where his prayers for rain were invariably answered, especially bound the people of Hongzhou to his memory. Hence the sacrifices to him in Nanchang. Yan, Duke of Lu, repaired field embankments and built reservoirs, irrigating ten thousand qing of farmland. The people of Fuzhou depend on these works to this day—how much more, then, on his long-renowned loyalty and righteousness! Hence the sacrifices to him in Fuzhou. Master Zhou of Lianxi served as Judicial Officer in Nan’an, redressing wrongful accusations and extending benefits to others. His single declaration, “To kill someone in order to flatter another—I will not do it,” was enough to subdue…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
王遠之氣況得千載不傳之學乎夫是有
南安之祀考亭朱子知南康軍勸學敎民
而下三章約立五賢堂條聖賢爲學大端
有以垂白鹿萬世之規況能集諸儒之大
成乎夫是有南康之祀趙抃守虔則戒諸
縣令使自爲治而改鹽法濂溪石虔以爲
利楊龜山司法于虔則忠信果决而疑獄
立斷虔以爲明夫是有虔之祀沈希顔衛
廢舉墜有功于雩然一錢不取妖禽不敢
===
啼樹矣劉藻興學勸耕亦有功于雩然增
王萬孝義二十四圖民至有割股以救親
者矣夫是有雩之祀范文正公守饒政先
豈弟而歲饑活民以萬計夫是有饒之祀
鍾離瑾令德化守義愛民而緩期輟耷以
嫁前令之女尤爲世所稱夫是有德化之
祀張師亮爲轉運副使奏定歲鑄之巻奏
捐錮送之令而又止旁地出稅放顆配歸
農其利愽矣張士遜爲轉運使不增羨餘
punctuated: 王遠之氣，況得千載不傳之學乎？夫是有南安之祀。考亭朱子知南康軍，勸學敎民，而下三章約，立五賢堂，條聖賢爲學大端，有以垂白鹿萬世之規，況能集諸儒之大成乎？夫是有南康之祀。趙抃守虔，則戒諸縣令，使自爲治，而改鹽法，濂溪石，虔以爲利。楊龜山司法于虔，則忠信果决，而疑獄立斷，虔以爲明。夫是有虔之祀。沈希顔衛廢舉墜，有功于雩，然一錢不取，妖禽不敢啼樹矣。劉藻興學勸耕，亦有功于雩，然增王萬孝義二十四圖，民至有割股以救親者矣。夫是有雩之祀。范文正公守饒，政先豈弟，而歲饑活民以萬計。夫是有饒之祀。鍾離瑾令德化，守義愛民，而緩期輟耷以嫁前令之女，尤爲世所稱。夫是有德化之祀。張師亮爲轉運副使，奏定歲鑄之巻，奏捐錮送之令，而又止旁地出稅，放顆配歸農，其利愽矣。張士遜爲轉運使，不增羨餘
translation_en: …Wang Yuan’s overbearing spirit—and how much more so, since he recovered a learning that had gone untransmitted for a thousand years! Hence the sacrifices to him at Nan’an. Master Zhu of Kaoting, as prefect of Nankang Military Prefecture, encouraged learning and instructed the people. He issued a compact in three articles, established the Hall of the Five Worthies, and set out the principal essentials of the sages’ and worthies’ pursuit of learning, thereby bequeathing lasting rules to White Deer Grotto Academy. How much more so, since he brought the learning of the various Confucian masters to its culmination! Hence the sacrifices to him at Nankang. When Zhao Bian governed Qian, he admonished the county magistrates and allowed them to conduct their own administrations. He also reformed the salt regulations; the following words, “Lianxi stone,” are unclear [?]. The people of Qian regarded this as beneficial. When Yang Guishan served as judicial officer in Qian, he was loyal, trustworthy, and decisive, settling doubtful cases immediately. The people of Qian considered him discerning. Hence the sacrifices to them at Qian. Shen Xiyan restored neglected undertakings [?] and rendered meritorious service to Yudu. Yet he would not take a single coin, and even ominous birds dared not cry in the trees. Liu Zao promoted learning and encouraged farming, likewise rendering meritorious service to Yudu. He also added twenty-four illustrations of filial piety and righteousness associated with Wang Wan [?]; among the people there were even those who cut flesh from their own thighs to save their parents. Hence the sacrifices to them at Yudu. Lord Fan Wenzheng, when governing Rao, made kindness the foremost principle of his administration; in a famine year, he saved tens of thousands of people. Hence the sacrifices to him at Rao. Zhongli Jin, as magistrate of Dehua, upheld righteousness and cherished the people. He was especially praised for postponing a deadline and suspending something unspecified [?] so that the daughter of the previous magistrate could marry. Hence the sacrifices to him at Dehua. Zhang Shiliang, as vice transport commissioner, petitioned to fix the annual minting quota [?] and to abolish an order concerning guarded conveyance [?]. He also stopped the exaction of taxes from adjoining lands and released people subjected to an obscure form of assignment [?] to return to farming. His benefits were extensive. Zhang Shixun, as transport commissioner, did not increase surplus revenues…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
之利而議者謂其識大體其濟衆矣夫是
有列郡之祀揆之祭法夫何間然哉然數
君子在當時豈有意於民之祀而民祀之
者亦非有以私之也數君子之治純心爲
民而已之利害夷危不計焉則其功德之
在民者遠而流風餘澤猶有以丐被後世
故也仰惟我
聖天子作人弘化屢
渙號申飭郡縣長吏固宜仰承
===
德奮起事功而大江以西未聞有以效令哲
而稱
上意者竊意今之守令能免於拘攣牽俗循常
習故而廓然爲民深慮者寡也世之吏者
責成於簿書期會之間以爲是大故至於
俗流敗壞而恬不以爲怪一也養祿待遷
僥倖以無罪襲高位寵厚祿自以爲成功
二也竭民之膏血以自媒利取寵一時三
也此三者膠固於中何繇深究民萌以達
punctuated:
之利，而議者謂其識大體，其濟衆矣。夫是有列郡之祀，揆之祭法，夫何間然哉？然數君子在當時，豈有意於民之祀？而民祀之者，亦非有以私之也。數君子之治，純心爲民，而已之利害夷危不計焉，則其功德之在民者遠，而流風餘澤猶有以丐被後世故也。
仰惟我聖天子作人弘化，屢渙號申飭郡縣長吏，固宜仰承德，奮起事功。而大江以西，未聞有以效令哲而稱上意者。竊意今之守令，能免於拘攣牽俗、循常習故，而廓然爲民深慮者寡也。世之吏者，責成於簿書期會之間，以爲是大故，至於俗流敗壞，而恬不以爲怪，一也；養祿待遷，僥倖以無罪襲高位、寵厚祿，自以爲成功，二也；竭民之膏血，以自媒利，取寵一時，三也。此三者膠固於中，何繇深究民萌以達
translation_en:
…profits; commentators said that he understood the larger principles of government and brought relief to the multitude. Thus these men received sacrifices in the various prefectures. Judged by the rules governing sacrifices, what fault could be found with this? Yet in their own day, did these gentlemen ever intend that the people should offer sacrifices to them? Nor did the people sacrifice to them out of personal favoritism. These gentlemen governed with hearts devoted entirely to the people, disregarding their own advantage or disadvantage, safety or danger. Their achievements and beneficence therefore had a lasting effect upon the people, and the influence and blessings they left behind continued to extend to later generations.
We reverently consider how our sagely Son of Heaven nurtures worthy men and extends his transforming influence, repeatedly issuing proclamations to admonish the chief officials of prefectures and counties. They surely ought reverently to receive his virtue and rouse themselves to accomplishment. Yet west of the great river, we have heard of none who emulate those worthy and wise men and satisfy His Majesty’s intentions. I venture to think that few prefects and magistrates today can escape constraint by conventional practices and adherence to familiar routines, and instead take a broad view and think deeply on the people’s behalf. Officials nowadays seek results in registers, documents, and scheduled reporting, regarding these as matters of great importance; meanwhile, when popular customs deteriorate, they remain complacent and see nothing strange in it. This is the first failing. They live on their salaries while awaiting promotion, hoping that merely avoiding punishment will allow them to succeed to high office and enjoy generous salaries, and they count this as achievement. This is the second. They drain the people’s lifeblood to secure advantages for themselves and win passing favor. This is the third. With these three failings firmly lodged within them, how can they thoroughly investigate the condition of the people [?] so as to comprehend…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
利害之原哉雖然亦豈無有志之士卓然
不群者然功業卒不逮古何也竊嘗聞之
矣周之卿士各世其家漢郡縣吏皆長子
孫甚以爲姓氏官有定民民有定志故上
易令而下易行也今任吏者率三歲一遷
而或一歲數遷其官矣漢刺史入爲三公
唐制不任州刺史者不得官侍郎不任縣
令不得爲臺郎給舍故激勸之道得而吏
易從也今縣令長滿三歲得任臺諫而守
===
郡者則不然矣况爲之吏者又從一切因
循之謀哉往者
聖天子嚴久任之法重郡縣之選而亦無應
明詔者何也豪傑之士有尚友之志者誠僞公
私之間當知所擇焉耳矣
第四問
劉朝佐
同考試官教諭汪　批〔九邊利害敷陳詳盡末篇〕
以重巡撫之權慎閫帥之寄正紀綱明功罪爲說尤
punctuated:
利害之原哉？雖然，亦豈無有志之士卓然不群者？然功業卒不逮古，何也？竊嘗聞之矣：周之卿士各世其家，漢郡縣吏皆長子孫，甚以爲姓氏。官有定民，民有定志，故上易令而下易行也。今任吏者率三歲一遷，而或一歲數遷其官矣。漢刺史入爲三公，唐制不任州刺史者不得官侍郎，不任縣令不得爲臺郎、給舍，故激勸之道得而吏易從也。今縣令長滿三歲得任臺諫，而守郡者則不然矣。况爲之吏者又從一切因循之謀哉？往者，聖天子嚴久任之法，重郡縣之選，而亦無應明詔者，何也？豪傑之士有尚友之志者，誠僞公私之間，當知所擇焉耳矣。

第四問
劉朝佐
同考試官教諭汪　批〔九邊利害敷陳詳盡，末篇〕以重巡撫之權、慎閫帥之寄、正紀綱、明功罪爲說，尤
translation_en:
…the sources of benefit and harm? Even so, are there no men of resolve who stand conspicuously above the crowd? Why, then, do their achievements ultimately fall short of those of antiquity? I have heard that the ministers of the Zhou each maintained their houses through successive generations, while the commandery and county officials of the Han all raised their children and grandchildren in their places of service, even taking these places as their surnames. Officials had a settled population to govern, and the people had settled expectations; thus those above could readily issue commands, and those below could readily carry them out. Nowadays, officials generally transfer once every three years, and some change office several times within a single year.

Under the Han, regional inspectors entered the central government as one of the Three Dukes. Under Tang regulations, anyone who had not served as a prefect could not become a vice minister, and anyone who had not served as a county magistrate could not become a bureau director, supervising secretary, or Secretariat drafter. Thus the means of encouragement were properly established, and officials readily followed them. Nowadays, county magistrates who have completed three years may take up censorial or remonstrance offices, but those governing prefectures cannot do likewise. How much worse when the officials themselves pursue nothing but expedients that perpetuate established habits! Previously, the sagely Son of Heaven strictly enforced provisions for long tenure and attached great importance to selecting prefectural and county officials. Yet none responded to his enlightened edict. Why was this? Men of outstanding ability who aspire to take the worthies of antiquity as their friends should surely know what to choose between sincerity and falsehood, public duty and private interest.

Liu Chaozuo

The concluding section〕 argues for strengthening the authority of grand coordinators, exercising care in entrusting military command, rectifying discipline, and clearly distinguishing merit from culpability. title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
見卓識可以爲
九重
獻矣
同考試官學正王　批〔惇德允元而難任人此唐虞率服蠻夷第一義子能備言之而發明陰陽消長之義讀之令人凜然可敬可敬〕
考試官訓導許　批〔内順治而外威嚴之道備矣子其吉甫邪方叔邪〕
考試官教諭周　批〔書生諳世務如此後傑也它日遠大之業可占矣健羨健羨〕
===
帝王之御夷狄不求其必可勝恃吾中國
之氣有以勝之而已是故其道約而不煩
逸而不勞治其所當治而夷狄卒爲所治
此非明於天道察於民故神武而不殺者
其孰能與於此哉執事發策下詢而有感
於帝王制御夷狄之道其於詩書所稱必
聞之熟矣愚不暇遠引敢陳歷代之得失
而以理折衷之中國内也四夷外也中國
punctuated:
見卓識，可以爲九重獻矣。

同考試官學正王　批〔惇德允元而難任人，此唐虞率服蠻夷第一義。子能備言之，而發明陰陽消長之義，讀之令人凜然。可敬，可敬！〕

考試官訓導許　批〔内順治而外威嚴之道備矣。子其吉甫邪？方叔邪？〕

考試官教諭周　批〔書生諳世務如此，後傑也。它日遠大之業可占矣。健羨，健羨！〕

帝王之御夷狄，不求其必可勝，恃吾中國之氣有以勝之而已。是故其道約而不煩，逸而不勞，治其所當治，而夷狄卒爲所治。此非明於天道、察於民故、神武而不殺者，其孰能與於此哉？執事發策下詢，而有感於帝王制御夷狄之道，其於詩書所稱，必聞之熟矣。愚不暇遠引，敢陳歷代之得失，而以理折衷之。中國内也，四夷外也。中國
translation_en:
…shows outstanding insight and may be presented to His Majesty.

Associate Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: 〔To honor the virtuous, trust the good, and keep flatterers at a distance: this was the foremost principle by which Tang and Yu brought the barbarian peoples into submission. You have explained it fully and elucidated the waxing and waning of yin and yang. Reading this inspires awe. Admirable, admirable!〕

Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The way to achieve orderly government within and awe-inspiring authority abroad is fully set forth here. Are you a Jifu or a Fang Shu?〕

Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: 〔A scholar who understands worldly affairs so well is an outstanding talent of the coming generation. One can foresee your great and far-reaching achievements in days to come. How enviable, how enviable!〕

In controlling the barbarian peoples, emperors and kings do not seek certainty of defeating them; they rely only on the vital force of our Central Kingdom being sufficient to overcome them. Thus their way is simple rather than cumbersome, effortless rather than laborious. They put in order what ought to be put in order, and the barbarian peoples ultimately come under their governance. Who could attain this without understanding the Way of Heaven, discerning the circumstances of the people, and possessing numinous martial power that achieves its ends without killing?

You, honored examiners, have issued a policy question to solicit our views, expressing concern about the way emperors and kings control the barbarian peoples. You must be thoroughly familiar with what the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents say on this subject. I, in my ignorance, have no leisure to draw extensively on distant precedents. I venture instead to set forth the successes and failures of successive dynasties and assess them according to principle. title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
於類爲陽爲君子夷狄於類爲陰爲小人
而其勝也各以其類堯舜禹湯文武之爲
君君子則舉小人則退君子道長小人道
消中國之氣常勝故當其時天清地寧雖
鳥獸魚鼈莫不咸若况夷狄乎此則陽氣
盛而陰不能姦也故二帝三王之世夷狄
之患無聞焉秦漢以下德衰而力雄善有
聞而不舉惡有聞而不去小人之道日長
君子之道日消中國之氣常不勝故當其
===
時日食地震雖蝛草槁木亦出妖孽况夷
狄乎是陰氣盛而陽不得其位也故夷狄
之患滋焉魏絳班固之徒不究本始而徒
以戰守和親爲言抑末矣朱子之論曰其
本不在於威强而在於德業其備不在於
邊境而在於朝廷其具不在於兵食而在
於紀綱名言哉愚所謂帝王之御夷狄不
恃其可勝恃吾中國之氣有以勝之者此
也雖然有苗弗率伯禹徂征崇密之伐文
punctuated:
於類爲陽，爲君子；夷狄於類爲陰，爲小人。而其勝也，各以其類。堯舜禹湯文武之爲君，君子則舉，小人則退；君子道長，小人道消，中國之氣常勝。故當其時，天清地寧，雖鳥獸魚鼈，莫不咸若，况夷狄乎？此則陽氣盛而陰不能姦也。故二帝三王之世，夷狄之患無聞焉。秦漢以下，德衰而力雄，善有聞而不舉，惡有聞而不去；小人之道日長，君子之道日消，中國之氣常不勝。故當其時，日食地震，雖蝛草槁木，亦出妖孽，况夷狄乎？是陰氣盛而陽不得其位也。故夷狄之患滋焉。魏絳班固之徒，不究本始，而徒以戰守和親爲言，抑末矣。朱子之論曰：「其本不在於威强，而在於德業；其備不在於邊境，而在於朝廷；其具不在於兵食，而在於紀綱。」名言哉！愚所謂帝王之御夷狄，不恃其可勝，恃吾中國之氣有以勝之者，此也。

雖然，有苗弗率，伯禹徂征；崇密之伐，文
translation_en:
…belongs, by category, to yang and to the noble man; the Yi and Di belong, by category, to yin and to the petty man. Each prevails through those of its own category. When Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu ruled, they promoted noble men and dismissed petty men. The way of noble men advanced, while the way of petty men receded, and the vital force of the Central Realm always prevailed. Thus, in their time, Heaven was clear and Earth tranquil; even birds, beasts, fish, and turtles all lived in harmony—how much more so the Yi and Di! This was because yang flourished and yin could do no mischief. Hence, in the age of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, troubles from the Yi and Di were unheard of. From the Qin and Han onward, virtue declined while coercive power grew strong. Those known for goodness were not promoted, and those known for evil were not removed. The way of petty men advanced daily, while the way of noble men receded daily, and the vital force of the Central Realm continually failed to prevail. Thus, in those times, there were solar eclipses and earthquakes; even insects and grasses [?] and withered trees produced baleful portents—how much more so the Yi and Di! This was because yin flourished and yang could not occupy its proper place. Hence troubles from the Yi and Di multiplied. Men such as Wei Jiang and Ban Gu failed to investigate the root of the matter and spoke merely of warfare, defense, and peace through marriage alliances. Surely these were only secondary concerns. Master Zhu stated: “Its foundation lies not in intimidating force but in virtuous achievement; its defenses lie not at the frontier but at court; its instruments lie not in troops and provisions but in the governing order.” Admirable words! This is what I mean when I say that, in controlling the Yi and Di, emperors and kings rely not on their ability to defeat them, but on the vital force of our Central Realm being sufficient to prevail over them.

Nevertheless, when the Youmiao refused obedience, Bo Yu went forth on a punitive expedition; in the campaigns against Chong and Mi, Wen…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
赫斯怒武備抑豈可盡廢哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝天錫神武奮起淮服驅逐胡元徙
之塞外建五重鎮以制夷狄所謂大同宣
府甘肅遼東大寧是已迨我
成祖文皇帝道光繼述增飭寧夏薊州等邊徙
大寧於畿內而以朶顏福餘泰寧分戍其
地成化弘治間又衛榆林固原繞爲九邊
發卒四十萬以禦之節制之臣介胄之士
星布塞上備邊之制密以詳矣仰惟我
===
上
聖德中興懋隆治極任賢不貳去邪不疑頻年
以來甘露河清之瑞白雀白兎之祥莫不
畢至中國之氣可謂極盛而又
聖武遠布夷狄畏威封疆之臣屢以捷告何其
盛也邇者
明詔廷臣講求邊備豈非安不忘危者哉愚竊
觀今日之勢遼左諸夷屋居耕食無異編
氓土魯番雖竊據哈密再佗甘肅志在□□
punctuated:
赫斯怒，武備抑豈可盡廢哉？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，天錫神武，奮起淮服，驅逐胡元，徙之塞外，建五重鎮以制夷狄，所謂大同、宣府、甘肅、遼東、大寧是已。迨我成祖文皇帝，道光繼述，增飭寧夏、薊州等邊，徙大寧於畿內，而以朶顏、福餘、泰寧分戍其地。成化、弘治間，又衛榆林、固原，繞爲九邊，發卒四十萬以禦之。節制之臣、介胄之士，星布塞上，備邊之制密以詳矣。
仰惟我上，聖德中興，懋隆治極，任賢不貳，去邪不疑。頻年以來，甘露、河清之瑞，白雀、白兎之祥，莫不畢至。中國之氣可謂極盛，而又聖武遠布，夷狄畏威，封疆之臣屢以捷告，何其盛也！邇者，明詔廷臣講求邊備，豈非安不忘危者哉？愚竊觀今日之勢，遼左諸夷屋居耕食，無異編氓。土魯番雖竊據哈密，再佗甘肅，志在□□
translation_en:
…flared up in wrath. How, then, could military preparedness be wholly abandoned? Our august Emperor Taizu Gao, endowed by Heaven with divine martial prowess, rose in the Huai region, drove out the alien Yuan, and displaced them beyond the frontier. He established five major garrisons to control the barbarians: Datong, Xuanfu, Gansu, Liaodong, and Daning. When our Emperor Chengzu Wen succeeded him, he gloriously carried forward his predecessor’s work, further strengthening the frontier defenses at Ningxia, Jizhou, and elsewhere. He relocated Daning within the metropolitan region and assigned Duoyan, Fuyu, and Taining to garrison its former territory in separate divisions. During the Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns, garrisons were also established at Yulin and Guyuan, forming a circuit of nine frontier commands. Four hundred thousand troops were mobilized to defend them. Commanding officials and armored soldiers were scattered like stars along the frontier: the system of frontier defense was comprehensive and meticulously organized.
We reverently consider how our present sovereign has brought about a restoration through his sagely virtue and diligently raised government to its highest excellence. He employs the worthy without wavering and removes the wicked without hesitation. In recent years, auspicious signs—sweet dew, the Yellow River running clear, white sparrows, and white hares—have all appeared. The vital force of the Central Realm may be said to have reached its fullest strength. Moreover, His Majesty’s sagely martial power extends afar; the barbarians fear his might, and officials guarding the frontiers repeatedly report victories. How flourishing an age this is! Recently, an enlightened edict instructed the court officials to investigate frontier preparedness. Is this not a case of remembering danger even in security? In my humble view of present conditions, the various barbarian peoples of Liaozuo live in houses and sustain themselves by farming, no differently from registered commoners. Although Turfan has unlawfully occupied Hami and twice encroached upon Gansu [?], its intention lies in [two illegible characters]…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
末添貢而已亦姑弗論延寧宣大固原五
鎮逼近北虜自據河套以來屢爲五鎮之
患而延綏偏關尤當其衝議者謂河套不
復則五鎮之患未已五鎮之患未已則延
寧偏關必有當其害者爲今日之計必先
屯田積穀選將練師逐虜出套復受降之
舊嚴東勝之守則邊境可以無事愚則以
爲不然何則帝王之道不徼其必可勝以
爲功而唯恃吾有自勝之術西漢之世幕
===
南雖無虜廷然中國耗弊亦已勞矣是故
河套之復可以不講也抑愚又有說焉獨
石雖有守矣薊花鎮可不加之意乎三衛
雖藩蔽矣潮河川可不爲之備乎必也重
武冑之選而將領之貪懦者必誅嚴清勾
之令而戍卒之逋逃者必罰復茶馬之舊
而牧圉之簡稽也必時通鹽商之利而芻
糧之儲積也必廣而又重巡撫之寉愼閫
帥之寄紀綱必正功罪必明則邊鎮其□
punctuated:
末添貢而已，亦姑弗論。延、寧、宣、大、固原五鎮逼近北虜，自據河套以來，屢爲五鎮之患，而延綏、偏關尤當其衝。議者謂河套不復，則五鎮之患未已；五鎮之患未已，則延、寧、偏關必有當其害者。爲今日之計，必先屯田積穀，選將練師，逐虜出套，復受降之舊，嚴東勝之守，則邊境可以無事。愚則以爲不然。何則？帝王之道，不徼其必可勝以爲功，而唯恃吾有自勝之術。西漢之世，幕南雖無虜廷，然中國耗弊，亦已勞矣。是故河套之復，可以不講也。

抑愚又有說焉：獨石雖有守矣，薊花鎮可不加之意乎？三衛雖藩蔽矣，潮河川可不爲之備乎？必也重武冑之選，而將領之貪懦者必誅；嚴清勾之令，而戍卒之逋逃者必罰；復茶馬之舊，而牧圉之簡稽也必時；通鹽商之利，而芻糧之儲積也必廣。而又重巡撫之寉，愼閫帥之寄，紀綱必正，功罪必明，則邊鎮其□
translation_en:
… merely to increase tribute [?]; let us also leave that aside for now. The five frontier garrisons of Yan, Ning, Xuan, Da, and Guyuan lie close to the northern foes. Since occupying the Hetao region, these foes have repeatedly troubled the five garrisons, with Yansui and Pianguan especially bearing the brunt. Those discussing the matter maintain that unless Hetao is recovered, the troubles of the five garrisons will not cease; and while those troubles persist, Yan, Ning, and Pianguan will inevitably suffer harm. As a strategy for the present, they insist that we must first establish military agricultural colonies and accumulate grain, select generals and train troops, drive the foes out of Hetao, restore the former establishments at Shouxiang, and strengthen the defenses of Dongsheng. Then the frontier can be free of trouble. In my humble view, this is not so. Why? The way of emperors and kings is not to seek achievement by counting on certain victory over others, but solely to rely on possessing the means of mastering oneself. In Western Han times, although no enemy court remained south of the desert, the realm was depleted and exhausted, and had already suffered greatly. Thus, recovering Hetao need not be pursued.

Yet I have a further argument. Although Dushi has defenders, can we neglect the garrison of Jihua [?]? Although the Three Guards serve as a protective screen, can we fail to prepare defenses in the Chaohe valley? We must give weight to selecting descendants of military families, and invariably punish avaricious or cowardly commanders; strictly enforce the orders for checking military rolls and securing replacements, and invariably punish garrison soldiers who abscond; restore the former tea-for-horses arrangements, and inspect horse herds and their keepers at the proper times; facilitate the profitable operations of salt merchants, and greatly expand stores of fodder and grain. Furthermore, we must give weight to the appointment [?] of grand coordinators and exercise care in entrusting command to frontier generals. Discipline must be set right, and merit and guilt clearly distinguished. Then the frontier garrisons would □ …

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
無虞乎雖然王猷允塞徐方旣來侯誰在
矣張仲孝友此周宣能復文武之業而燦
然中興者也愚不敏顒以是爲
今日獻
第五問
陶欽臯
同考試官教諭官　批〔治水之法莫善於禹貢莫詳於周官而尤莫備於我〕
〔之制第郡縣長吏視爲末務莫之舉行爾此篇條陳盡矣宜錄〕
===
〔以飾庶官之吏於茲土者〕
考試官訓導許　批〔博雅之學明達之才康濟之志讀此業可槩見矣佳士佳士〕
考試官教諭周　批〔因自然之利脩已然之法〕
〔格言格言〕
善治水者貴乎因自然之利而脩已然之
法自然之利而能導之則有以永其利於
無窮法之已然者而能脩之則有以維持
之於不壞舍此而日紛紛焉則亦弊焉耳
punctuated:
無虞乎？雖然，「王猷允塞，徐方旣來。」「侯誰在矣？張仲孝友。」此周宣能復文武之業而燦然中興者也。愚不敏，顒以是爲今日獻。

第五問
陶欽臯
同考試官教諭官，批〔治水之法，莫善於禹貢，莫詳於周官，而尤莫備於我〕〔之制。第郡縣長吏視爲末務，莫之舉行爾。此篇條陳盡矣，宜錄〕〔以飾庶官之吏於茲土者。〕
考試官訓導許，批〔博雅之學，明達之才，康濟之志，讀此業可槩見矣。佳士！佳士！〕
考試官教諭周，批〔因自然之利，脩已然之法。〕〔格言！格言！〕

善治水者，貴乎因自然之利而脩已然之法。自然之利而能導之，則有以永其利於無窮；法之已然者而能脩之，則有以維持之於不壞。舍此而日紛紛焉，則亦弊焉耳
translation_en:
…be free from danger? Nevertheless, “The king’s plans were truly fulfilled; the lands of Xu had submitted.” “Who was there? Zhang Zhong, filial and brotherly.” These were the circumstances in which King Xuan of Zhou restored the achievements of Kings Wen and Wu and brought about a glorious resurgence. Though I lack ability, I respectfully offer these observations today.

Fifth Policy Question
By Tao Qingao

Comment by Associate Examiner Guan, Instructor: 〔No methods of water management surpass those in the Tribute of Yu (Yu gong); none are more detailed than those in the Offices of Zhou (Zhou guan); and none, above all, are more comprehensive than our〕〔institutions. It is simply that prefectural and county chief officials regard them as minor concerns and do not put them into practice. This essay sets out the proposals exhaustively and should be recorded〕〔to admonish [?] the officials serving in this region.〕

Comment by Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: 〔His broad and cultivated learning, his perceptive ability, and his aspiration to bring peace and relief to the people can all be discerned in outline from reading this composition. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!〕

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: 〔“Make use of natural advantages and maintain established methods.”〕〔Wise words! Wise words!〕

Those skilled in managing water place the highest value on making use of natural advantages and maintaining established methods. If one can guide the natural advantages, one has the means to perpetuate their benefits without end. If one can maintain established methods, one has the means to preserve them from deterioration. To abandon these principles and bustle about day after day will merely produce harm…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
矣愚嘗讀書至唐虞之際未嘗不掩卷歎
也嗟乎洪水滔天浩浩懷山襄陵此豈細
故哉舜擇於四岳舉伯禹而畀之以平水
土之寄則禹之智真有以逈出當時諸臣
之上而禹之治水不過曰決九川距四海
浚畎澮距川而已而天下之言智者莫踰
焉何哉洪範五行水曰潤下知水之性潤
下則知禹之治水矣是故先決九川以導
於海使水之大者有所歸次濬畎澮以距
===
於川使水之小者有所洩此所以九州同
四隩宅而萬世永利也商之衰也五行之
官世失其業周人始命遂人十夫為溝百
夫為洫千夫為澮萬夫為川而溝洫之制
始立稻人以豬畜水以防止水以溝蕩水
以遂均水以列舍水以澮瀉水而溝洫之
制益詳至於匠人氏又辨其深廣之度而
通其蓄洩之宜其法可謂盡善矣然周人
豈夷陵谷而為之哉亦不過因其自然之
punctuated:
矣。愚嘗讀書至唐虞之際，未嘗不掩卷歎也。嗟乎！洪水滔天，浩浩懷山襄陵，此豈細故哉？舜擇於四岳，舉伯禹而畀之以平水土之寄，則禹之智真有以逈出當時諸臣之上。而禹之治水，不過曰「決九川距四海，浚畎澮距川」而已，而天下之言智者莫踰焉，何哉？《洪範》五行，水曰「潤下」。知水之性潤下，則知禹之治水矣。是故先決九川以導於海，使水之大者有所歸；次濬畎澮以距於川，使水之小者有所洩。此所以九州同，四隩宅，而萬世永利也。
商之衰也，五行之官世失其業。周人始命遂人，十夫為溝，百夫為洫，千夫為澮，萬夫為川，而溝洫之制始立。稻人以豬畜水，以防止水，以溝蕩水，以遂均水，以列舍水，以澮瀉水，而溝洫之制益詳。至於匠人氏，又辨其深廣之度，而通其蓄洩之宜，其法可謂盡善矣。然周人豈夷陵谷而為之哉？亦不過因其自然之
translation_en:
…that is all. Whenever I have read about the age of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, I have closed the book and sighed. Alas! Floodwaters rose to the heavens, their vast expanse encircling mountains and overtopping hills: was this any trifling calamity? Shun consulted the Four Mountains in making his selection, raised up Bo Yu, and entrusted him with the task of bringing the waters and land into order. Yu’s wisdom truly surpassed that of all the ministers of his time. Yet his control of the waters amounted to no more than “opening the nine rivers to reach the four seas, and dredging the field channels and drains to reach the rivers.” Nevertheless, among all those in the world renowned for wisdom, none surpassed him. Why was this? In the account of the Five Phases in the Great Plan, water is said to “moisten and descend.” Understand that water’s nature is to moisten and descend, and you understand Yu’s management of the waters. Thus he first opened the nine rivers to lead the waters into the sea, giving the larger bodies of water somewhere to converge; next he dredged the field channels and drains to connect them with the rivers, giving the smaller bodies of water an outlet. This was how the Nine Provinces were brought into harmony and the lands within the four quarters made habitable, securing enduring benefits for ten thousand generations.
As the Shang declined, the officials responsible for the Five Phases lost their professional knowledge over successive generations. The Zhou first appointed Directors of Rural Districts, providing a ditch for every ten cultivators’ holdings, a larger channel for every hundred, a main drain for every thousand, and a river for every ten thousand. Thus the system of ditches and channels was established. The Superintendents of Rice Fields used reservoirs to store water, embankments to hold it back, ditches to conduct it, small channels to distribute it evenly, branching channels to release it into the fields, and main drains to discharge it. The system of ditches and channels thereby became more detailed. The Master Craftsmen further determined their appropriate depths and widths and worked out suitable arrangements for storing and releasing water. Their methods may be called perfect in every respect. Yet did the Zhou level hills and valleys to accomplish this? They merely followed the natural …

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
和而脩伯禹之故而已周之衰也遂人稻
人匠人之官又世失其業列国之君皆自
利以病隣國暴秦之興又廢溝洫開阡陌
而水利廢矣是故孫叔敖起芍陂則楚受
其惠文公穿腴口則蜀以富饒史起鑿漳
水於魏則鄴傍有稻梁之詠鄭國道涇水
於秦則谷口有禾黍之謠許景山復蕭何
之故堰則興元之荒瘠復爲膏腴趙尚寛
脩召信臣之故渠則南陽之潟鹵變爲沃
壤之數君子者孰非因其自然之利而脩
其已然之法其謂之得周官之遺意亦可
也伏惟我
===
國家司空有總職水利有專官省以督之府
府以督之縣而縣之陂塘圩堰又莫不有
長重以憲臣之稽察皆以懋惠元元而興
水利也然遇水旱民輒告病者是必有其
故矣愚請以江右言之湖東西故揚州之
域厥土惟塗泥厥田下下而九江以西又
punctuated:
和，而脩伯禹之故而已。周之衰也，遂人、稻人、匠人之官又世失其業，列国之君皆自利以病隣國。暴秦之興，又廢溝洫，開阡陌，而水利廢矣。是故孫叔敖起芍陂，則楚受其惠；文公穿腴口，則蜀以富饒；史起鑿漳水於魏，則鄴傍有稻梁之詠；鄭國道涇水於秦，則谷口有禾黍之謠；許景山復蕭何之故堰，則興元之荒瘠復爲膏腴；趙尚寛脩召信臣之故渠，則南陽之潟鹵變爲沃壤。之數君子者，孰非因其自然之利而脩其已然之法？其謂之得周官之遺意，亦可也。
伏惟我國家，司空有總職，水利有專官，省以督之府，府以督之縣，而縣之陂塘圩堰又莫不有長，重以憲臣之稽察，皆以懋惠元元而興水利也。然遇水旱，民輒告病者，是必有其故矣。愚請以江右言之：湖東西，故揚州之域，厥土惟塗泥，厥田下下；而九江以西，又
translation_en:
…harmony, and merely restored the works of Bo Yu. As the Zhou declined, the offices of the Directors of Rural Administration, Rice Cultivation officials, and master builders again lost their inherited expertise. The rulers of the various states all sought their own advantage at their neighbors’ expense. With the rise of tyrannical Qin, the irrigation channels were abolished and the field boundaries opened up, and water management fell into neglect. Thus, when Sun Shuao constructed the Shaopi reservoir, Chu benefited; when Duke Wen excavated Yukou [?], Shu became prosperous; when Shi Qi cut a channel from the Zhang River in Wei, songs about rice and millet arose around Ye; when Zheng Guo channeled the Jing River in Qin, songs about grain and millet arose at Gukou; when Xu Jingshan restored Xiao He’s old weir, the barren land of Xingyuan became fertile again; and when Zhao Shangkuan repaired Shao Xinchen’s old canal, the saline soil of Nanyang became rich farmland. Which of these gentlemen did not follow the advantages of the natural terrain and restore established methods? It would be fair to say that they grasped the surviving intent of the Offices of Zhou.
I humbly reflect that in our dynasty the Minister of Works has overall responsibility, while dedicated officials oversee water management. The provinces supervise the prefectures, and the prefectures supervise the counties; every county’s reservoirs, ponds, embankments, and weirs also have their overseers. Added to these are inspections by censorial officials—all intended to confer abundant benefits upon the common people by improving water management. Yet whenever floods or droughts occur, the people immediately report distress. There must surely be a reason for this. Let me speak of Jiangyou. The lands east and west of the lake formerly lay within the territory of Yangzhou: “Their soil was muddy; their fields were of the lowest grade.” And the lands west of Jiujiang were also…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
古荊州之地禹貢所謂彭蠡既豬九江孔
殷者也夫其襟江帶湖水之大者有所歸
小者有所洩矣然小水輙溢小旱輙暵比
他省爲甚邇者春夏之交江水暴漲壞民
田居比連數郡此無他陂塘圩堰之長皆
失其業而郡縣長吏又莫之省憂故也執
事欲脩周官之職加疏濬之功通灌溉之
利絶漂没之患甚盛心也愚則以爲周官
之職不可卒復而溝洫之遺意尚亦可尋
===
周官曰溝必因水勢防必因地勢蓋溝以
導水不因水勢則其流易壅防以止水不
因地勢則其土易壞爲今之計莫若申飭
郡縣長吏督率陂塘圩堰之長察水勢之
曲直原地勢之高卑可堤則堤可決則決
因陂塘圩堰之舊加疏濬築塞之功而又
嚴侵占之禁明考課之法則灌溉之利興
漂没之患免矣雖然賈讓有言曰立國居
民疆理土地必遺川澤之分度水勢所不
punctuated:
古荊州之地，《禹貢》所謂「彭蠡既豬，九江孔殷」者也。夫其襟江帶湖，水之大者有所歸，小者有所洩矣。然小水輙溢，小旱輙暵，比他省爲甚。邇者春夏之交，江水暴漲，壞民田居，比連數郡。此無他，陂塘圩堰之長皆失其業，而郡縣長吏又莫之省憂故也。執事欲脩周官之職，加疏濬之功，通灌溉之利，絶漂没之患，甚盛心也。愚則以爲周官之職不可卒復，而溝洫之遺意尚亦可尋。

《周官》曰：「溝必因水勢，防必因地勢。」蓋溝以導水，不因水勢則其流易壅；防以止水，不因地勢則其土易壞。爲今之計，莫若申飭郡縣長吏，督率陂塘圩堰之長，察水勢之曲直，原地勢之高卑，可堤則堤，可決則決，因陂塘圩堰之舊，加疏濬築塞之功，而又嚴侵占之禁，明考課之法，則灌溉之利興，漂没之患免矣。雖然，賈讓有言曰：「立國居民，疆理土地，必遺川澤之分，度水勢所不
translation_en:
…the territory of ancient Jingzhou, of which the Tribute of Yu says: “Pengli was made a collecting basin, and the nine rivers were thoroughly brought into order.” With the river at its breast and lakes encircling it, its larger waters have somewhere to gather, and its smaller waters have outlets. Yet even a slight rise in water causes flooding, and even a brief drought causes parching, more severely than in other provinces. Recently, at the turn of spring and summer, the river rose suddenly, destroying people’s fields and dwellings across several adjoining prefectures. There is no other cause than this: those responsible for ponds, reservoirs, polder embankments, and weirs have all neglected their duties, while the chief officials of prefectures and counties have failed to inspect these matters or take them to heart. Your wish to restore the functions described in the Offices of Zhou, increase dredging work, secure the benefits of irrigation, and eliminate the calamity of inundation is most generous in intention. In my humble view, however, the offices of Zhou cannot be restored all at once, though the principles underlying their drainage channels can still be recovered.

The Offices of Zhou says: “Channels must follow the configuration of the waters; embankments must follow the configuration of the land.” Channels guide water; unless they follow its configuration, their flow is easily obstructed. Embankments hold water back; unless they follow the configuration of the land, their earthworks are easily breached. The best course now would be to issue renewed, strict instructions to the chief officials of prefectures and counties to supervise those responsible for ponds, reservoirs, polder embankments, and weirs. They should examine where watercourses bend or run straight and investigate the elevations and depressions of the land, building embankments wherever appropriate and opening outlets wherever appropriate. They should work from the existing ponds, reservoirs, polder embankments, and weirs, increasing their efforts at dredging, construction, and sealing breaches. If, in addition, prohibitions against encroachment are strictly enforced and procedures for evaluating officials’ performance are made clear, the benefits of irrigation will be secured and the calamity of inundation avoided. Nevertheless, Jia Rang once said: “When establishing a state and settling its people, demarcating and ordering the land, one must leave a portion for rivers and marshes, and determine where the waters do not…”

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
及大川無防小水得入陂障卑下以爲汙
澤使秋水多得有所休息左右游波寬衍
而不迫此誠萬世水利之上策也然豈可
以易言哉是故必有韋丹在豫章而後可
以興南塘之利必有吳明卓在吉水而後
可以興柿陂之利必有何易于在建昌而
後可以興捍水塘之利必有李復在鄱陽
而後可以興邵父塘之利否則亦行文書
具故實而已唯執事者圖之
punctuated: 及，大川無防，小水得入，陂障卑下以爲汙澤，使秋水多，得有所休息，左右游波，寬衍而不迫。」此誠萬世水利之上策也，然豈可以易言哉？是故必有韋丹在豫章，而後可以興南塘之利；必有吳明卓在吉水，而後可以興柿陂之利；必有何易于在建昌，而後可以興捍水塘之利；必有李復在鄱陽，而後可以興邵父塘之利。否則亦行文書、具故實而已。唯執事者圖之。
translation_en: …reach; leave the great rivers without embankments, so that smaller streams can flow into them; embank low-lying ground to form pools and marshes, so that when autumn waters are abundant, they have somewhere to settle, with room for waves to spread on either side, broad and unconfined.” This is indeed the best policy for water management for all ages. Yet how could it be spoken of lightly? Thus, only with a Wei Dan in Yuzhang could the benefits of Nantang be realized; only with a Wu Mingzhuo in Jishui could the benefits of Shibei be realized; only with a He Yiyu in Jianchang could the benefits of Hanshui Tang be realized; and only with a Li Fu in Poyang could the benefits of Shaofu Tang be realized. Otherwise, there will be nothing more than circulating official documents and observing established formalities. May those responsible give this due consideration.

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
夫聖人宰制萬物役使羣動
必錫之藝極以昭標訓是故
選舉之所由始也仰惟
聖朝取士爰立式程能者從之無
弗錄焉者何哉規矩誠陳難
眩以方圓準繩誠具難欺以
===
平直度量誠設難惑以長短
重輕也夫式也者規矩準繩
度量之謂也左不偏于左右
不偏于右高不過亢卑不過
抑中之謂也學者莫可践焉
傳曰王天下有三重焉其寡
過矣乎三王不襲禮五帝不
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

夫聖人宰制萬物，役使羣動，必錫之藝極，以昭標訓，是故選舉之所由始也。仰惟聖朝取士，爰立式程，能者從之，無弗錄焉者，何哉？規矩誠陳，難眩以方圓；準繩誠具，難欺以平直；度量誠設，難惑以長短重輕也。夫式也者，規矩準繩度量之謂也。左不偏于左，右不偏于右，高不過亢，卑不過抑，中之謂也。學者莫可践焉。傳曰：「王天下有三重焉，其寡過矣乎！」三王不襲禮，五帝不
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

When the sage governs the myriad things and directs all living beings, he must bestow standards of accomplishment upon them, thereby making exemplary instruction manifest. This is the origin of selection for office. We reverently reflect that our august dynasty, in recruiting men of talent, has established prescribed standards. Those with ability follow them, and none goes unselected. Why is this? When compass and square are properly set out, it is difficult to mislead anyone about squareness and roundness; when level and inked cord are properly provided, it is difficult to deceive anyone about evenness and straightness; when measures and balances are properly established, it is difficult to confuse anyone about length and shortness, heaviness and lightness. These prescribed standards are what we mean by compass and square, level and inked cord, measures and balances. To stand to the left without veering too far left, to stand to the right without veering too far right, to be high without excessive elevation, and low without excessive abasement: this is what is meant by the mean. No learner can put this into practice [?]. The transmitted text says: “One who rules all under Heaven has three weighty responsibilities. Surely his errors will be few!” The Three Kings did not simply inherit the rites of their predecessors; the Five Emperors did not…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
沿樂法變而道不變其建極
一也高者躐躋般輸工垂之
上自加椎鑿而立門戶畢者
拘泥猥瑣勞筋苦力又矻矻
無成皆不可與于中其如式
何子諸士今以文見思薦
□廟覲
===
□堂也亦既規矩準繩度量無爽
則焉豈唯爲下不倍又將式
是四方以光化理可謂無負
天子金聲玉振之教禮節樂和
之化矣夫式以立天下之極
者也器以適天下之用者也
方圓平直輕重長短無弗式
punctuated: 沿樂，法變而道不變，其建極一也。高者躐躋般輸、工垂之上，自加椎鑿而立門戶；畢者拘泥猥瑣，勞筋苦力，又矻矻無成，皆不可與于中，其如式何？子諸士今以文見，思薦□廟、覲□堂也。亦既規矩準繩度量無爽，則焉豈唯爲下不倍？又將式是四方，以光化理，可謂無負天子金聲玉振之教、禮節樂和之化矣。夫式，以立天下之極者也；器，以適天下之用者也。方圓平直、輕重長短，無弗式
translation_en:
…follow the same music. Methods change, but the Way does not; in establishing the highest standard, they are one. Those who aim high leap above Ban Shu [?] and the master craftsman Chui, applying their own mallets and chisels to establish separate schools. Others, described here as “bi” [?], cling to petty details, straining their sinews and exhausting their strength, yet toil away without accomplishment. Neither can attain the mean: how, then, can they conform to the standard? You gentlemen now present yourselves through your writing, hoping to be recommended at the □ temple and received in audience in the □ hall [?]. Once you have conformed without error to compass and square, level and plumb line, measures of capacity and weight, surely you will do more than serve without disobedience in a subordinate position. You will also become models for the four quarters, bringing lustre to moral transformation and good governance. You may then be said not to have failed the Son of Heaven’s teaching, complete as the sounding of bronze bells and the concluding resonance of jade chimes, or his transforming influence through the restraints of ritual and the harmonies of music.

Standards establish the highest norm for the world; implements meet the world’s practical needs. Whether square or round, level or straight, light or heavy, long or short, nothing fails to conform to a standard…

title: 嘉靖十九年江西鄉試錄
text:
焉間施之用也乃菩廬而無
當是故吾懼其外飾也一枘
鑿不合則偭背攷錯枉尺而
直尋是故吾懼其終離也飾
焉離焉其究也人已並失惟
塵之累士德何以釋於天下
戉相與有成合內外始終斯
可哉
===
直隸蘇州府吳江縣儒學訓
導許士德謹序
punctuated:
焉。間施之用也，乃菩廬而無當，是故吾懼其外飾也。一枘鑿不合，則偭背攷錯，枉尺而直尋，是故吾懼其終離也。飾焉，離焉，其究也，人已並失，惟塵之累，士德何以釋於天下？戉相與有成，合內外始終，斯可哉！
直隸蘇州府吳江縣儒學訓導許士德謹序。
translation_en:
…to it. Yet when put to use [?], it becomes a gourd with no practical purpose [?]; hence I fear mere outward ornament. Once tenon and mortise fail to fit, there follow deviation and misalignment [?]—bending a foot to straighten a fathom. Hence I fear eventual departure from the standard. With outward ornament and departure, the ultimate result is the loss of both others and oneself [?], leaving only the burden of worldly dust. How could I, Shide, explain myself to all under Heaven? May we [?] together achieve something, bringing the inner and outer, beginning and end, into accord. Only thus might it be acceptable!
Respectfully prefaced by Xu Shide, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian School of Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region.
